teile.einleitung: **Fasting** means **deliberately going without something** for a certain time, usually food and drink. Many religions have times of fasting. They are meant to help people think about themselves, come closer to God and think of others.
wichtigste: The fasting month of Muslims is called Ramadan.
In Ramadan, people who fast do not eat or drink from morning until sunset.
At the end of Ramadan, people celebrate the Festival of Breaking the Fast.
The Christian season of fasting lasts 40 days and begins on Ash Wednesday.
Before the season of fasting, Fasnacht is celebrated in many places in Switzerland.
On Yom Kippur, Jews fast for a whole day.

abschnitte.text: **Ramadan** is the ninth month in the Islamic lunar calendar. That is why it shifts every year. In this month adult Muslims neither eat nor drink **from morning until sunset**. Children, the sick, the old and travellers do not have to fast. In the evening the fast is often broken with **dates and water**, followed by a shared meal. At the end people celebrate the **Festival of Breaking the Fast**.

For Christians the season of fasting begins on **Ash Wednesday** and lasts **40 days** until Easter. Sundays are not counted. The number 40 recalls that, according to the Bible, Jesus fasted for 40 days in the desert. Today many people give up, for example, sweets, meat or their mobile phone. In Switzerland, church charities collect money in this season for people in poorer countries.

Before the season of fasting begins, there is celebrating. In many places in Switzerland it is then **Fasnacht**, the carnival, with masks, parades and brass-band music. The word is connected with fasting: it is the night or time before the fast. Well known, for example, are the carnivals in Lucerne and Basel. The Basel carnival even begins only on the Monday after Ash Wednesday.

In Judaism, **Yom Kippur** is the most important day of fasting. In English it is called the **Day of Atonement**. Jews then fast for a whole day, from one evening to the next, and pray a great deal. In Hinduism and Buddhism too there are days of fasting. Everywhere the same holds: you **deliberately give something up** in order to reflect on what matters.

gewusst: Because the Islamic calendar is shorter than our year, Ramadan moves through all the seasons.
In some countries the Festival of Breaking the Fast is also called the Sugar Festival.

teile.einleitung: Ashkenazi Jews are Jewish people whose ancestors came from Central and Eastern Europe. The name comes from the Hebrew word “Ashkenaz”, which in the Middle Ages stood for the German-speaking area. The Ashkenazim developed a culture of their own, with a language of their own, Yiddish.
wichtigste: In medieval Hebrew, “Ashkenaz” referred to the German-speaking area.
Early centres were the SchUM cities of Speyer, Worms and Mainz.
The SchUM sites have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2021.
After persecutions, many Ashkenazim moved to Poland-Lithuania.
In the 18th century, Hasidism arose in Eastern Europe.
Many Ashkenazim spoke Yiddish.

abschnitte.text: In medieval Hebrew, **Ashkenaz** stood for Germany, especially for the Rhineland. From this came the name **Ashkenazim** for the Jews of this region. Later it came to mean all Jews with Central and Eastern European roots. The Jews from Spain and Portugal, by contrast, are called **Sephardim**. Both groups partly have customs and ways of praying of their own.

Early centres of Ashkenazi Judaism lay on the Rhine. The cities of **Speyer, Worms and Mainz** formed the **SchUM communities**. The name is put together from the Hebrew initial letters of Shpira, Warmaisa and Magenza. Famous scholars worked there, and there were synagogues, ritual baths and cemeteries. Since 2021 the SchUM sites have belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

In the late Middle Ages, Jews were persecuted and driven out of many German cities. Many emigrated to **Poland-Lithuania**. Polish rulers granted them privileges of protection. In this way Poland-Lithuania became the centre of Ashkenazi Judaism until the 20th century. Here **Yiddish** developed further, a language with many German, Hebrew and Slavic words.

In the 18th century, **Israel ben Eliezer**, known as the Baal Shem Tov, founded **Hasidism** in Eastern Europe. This devout movement stresses joy, prayer and closeness to God in everyday life. In the Holocaust, a large part of Europe’s Jewish communities was destroyed. Today Ashkenazim live mainly in Israel, the USA and Europe. In Switzerland too, for example in the old Jewish villages of **Endingen and Lengnau** in Aargau, there are traces of Ashkenazi culture.

gewusst: The word SchUM is put together from the Hebrew initial letters of three cities.
For a long time, Endingen and Lengnau in the canton of Aargau were the only places in the Old Swiss Confederacy where Jews were permitted to live permanently.

teile.einleitung: The Gemara is a large part of the Talmud, one of the most important works of Judaism. It contains the discussions of Jewish scholars about the Mishnah. Together, the Mishnah and the Gemara make up the Talmud.
wichtigste: The Gemara explains and discusses the Mishnah.
The Mishnah and the Gemara together make up the Talmud.
The scholars of the Gemara are called Amoraim.
The word Gemara means roughly “completion” and “learning”.
The Babylonian Talmud was essentially completed around 500 to 600 AD.

abschnitte.text: The **Mishnah** is a collection of Jewish laws and teachings that was written down around the year 200 AD. In the following centuries, scholars discussed every sentence of the Mishnah. Their questions, answers and debates were recorded in the **Gemara**. The Gemara is mostly written in **Aramaic**. The Mishnah and the Gemara together make up the **Talmud**.

The scholars of the Gemara are called **Amoraim**. They worked roughly from **200 to 500 AD** in Palestine and in **Babylonia**, the area of present-day Iraq. There were large Jewish **academies** there, that is, houses of learning. The word **Gemara** comes from the root “gamar”, which means “to complete” and “to learn”. So the Gemara completes the Mishnah through explanations.

There are two versions: the **Jerusalem Talmud** from Palestine and the **Babylonian Talmud**. The Babylonian Talmud is much larger and was essentially completed around the 6th century, that is, **around 500 to 600 AD**. It is still the more important one today. When people simply speak of “the Talmud”, they usually mean it.

The Gemara contains two kinds of text. The **halakha** are the discussions of law: they settle how to live according to Jewish law. Alongside these are legends, parables and words of wisdom. These narrative parts are called **aggadah**. To this day, Jews often study the Gemara in pairs and discuss it aloud with one another as they do so.

gewusst: On a page of the Talmud, the text of the Mishnah and Gemara stands in the middle, with later explanations all around.
In the study programme “Daf Yomi”, you read one leaf of the Talmud every day and are through it after about seven and a half years.

teile.einleitung: A prayer is a conversation with God or with something divine. People in almost all religions pray. They give thanks, ask for something or simply become quiet.
wichtigste: In prayer, people speak with God, aloud or in their thoughts.
Many Christians fold their hands to pray.
The best-known Christian prayer is the Our Father.
Muslims pray five times a day at fixed times.
In Switzerland there is the Federal Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer.

abschnitte.text: A **prayer** is a conversation with God. You can pray aloud or quietly in your thoughts. You can pray alone or together with others, for example in a church. People pray to **give thanks**, to **ask for something** or to hope for others. Some pray in their own words, others with prayers that are already very old.

Many Christians **fold** their hands to pray. In this way they show that they are becoming calm and thinking of God. Some kneel or close their eyes. The best-known prayer is the **Our Father**, which, according to the Bible, Jesus himself taught. Many families say a short **grace** before the meal or pray in the evening before sleep.

**Muslims** pray five times a day at fixed times. They turn towards Mecca, bow and kneel on a carpet. In **Judaism**, the “Shema Yisrael” is an important prayer. **Hindus** often pray in front of pictures or figures of their gods and bring flowers or lights. In **Buddhism**, meditation and good wishes for all beings are important.

In Switzerland there has long been the **Federal Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer**. It falls on the third Sunday in September. On this day people of different denominations are meant to give thanks and reflect together. On some mountain pastures in central Switzerland, the herdsman sings the **Alpsegen** or **Betruf** (the “alpine blessing”) in the evening. He calls through a wooden funnel and asks for protection for people and cattle.

gewusst: The word “Amen” at the end of many prayers comes from Hebrew and means roughly “so be it”.
The Our Father is prayed in very many languages all over the world.

teile.einleitung: The Epic of Gilgamesh is one of the oldest stories in the world. It comes from Mesopotamia, the land between the Euphrates and the Tigris, and was written in cuneiform on clay tablets. It tells of King Gilgamesh, his friend Enkidu and the search for eternal life.
wichtigste: Gilgamesh was king of the city of Uruk in southern Mesopotamia.
His wild friend was called Enkidu.
The epic was written in cuneiform on clay tablets.
After Enkidu’s death, Gilgamesh searched for immortality.
Utnapishtim tells him of a great flood.
The best-known version comes from the library of Ashurbanipal in Nineveh.

abschnitte.text: **Gilgamesh** was king of **Uruk** in southern Mesopotamia. He is said to have built the great city wall. At the beginning he is strong, but arrogant. That is why the gods create **Enkidu**, a wild man from the steppe, as his opponent. After a fight the two become **close friends**. Together they go through great adventures.

abschnitte.titel: Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven
abschnitte.text: Gilgamesh and Enkidu travel to the **cedar forest**. There they defeat the guardian **Humbaba**, a monster. Afterwards Gilgamesh rejects the goddess **Ishtar**. Ishtar is furious and sends the **Bull of Heaven** against him. The two friends kill the bull. As a punishment, the gods decide that Enkidu must die.

Enkidu’s death makes Gilgamesh afraid of his own death. He wanders far to find **immortality**. He meets **Utnapishtim**, who survived a great **flood** in a ship and received eternal life from the gods. The story is similar to the tale of **Noah** in the Bible. Gilgamesh finds a plant of rejuvenation. But while he is bathing, a **snake** eats the plant. Gilgamesh returns to Uruk without it.

The epic was pressed into soft clay with styluses. These wedge-shaped signs are called **cuneiform**. The best-known version comes from the **library** of the Assyrian king **Ashurbanipal** in **Nineveh**. The tablets were dug up in the 19th century and today lie mostly in the British Museum in London. Older parts of the story arose much earlier.

gewusst: After the snake has eaten the plant, it sheds its skin. In this way the story explained why snakes change their skin.
When researchers in the 19th century deciphered the tablet with the flood story, it caused a great stir, because it is so similar to the story of Noah.

teile.einleitung: In the Bible the **patriarchs** are **Abraham**, his son **Isaac** and his grandson **Jacob**. Their stories are in the first book of Moses, **Genesis**. They are important for Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
wichtigste: According to the Bible, Abraham came from the city of Ur in Mesopotamia.
At God’s call he moved to the land of Canaan.
Abraham’s wife was called Sarah, Isaac’s wife Rebekah.
Esau sold Jacob his birthright for a dish of lentils.
After the struggle at the river Jabbok, Jacob received the name Israel.
At Bethel, Jacob dreamed of a ladder to heaven.
The tomb of the patriarchs, the Cave of Machpelah, lies in Hebron.

abschnitte.text: According to the Bible, **Abraham** first lived in the city of **Ur** in Mesopotamia, in present-day Iraq. God called him to leave his homeland and promised him a new land and many descendants. So Abraham moved with his wife **Sarah** and his flocks to the land of **Canaan**. He trusted God, although he did not know what awaited him. That is why he is regarded as a model of faith.

**Isaac** was the son of Abraham and Sarah. When he was grown up, Abraham sent a servant to his old homeland to look for a wife for him. At a well the servant met **Rebekah**, who gave water to him and his camels. She became Isaac’s wife. Isaac and Rebekah had the twins **Esau** and **Jacob**.

Esau was the older twin and therefore had the **birthright**. One day he came home hungry. Jacob was just cooking a **dish of lentils**, and Esau sold him his right for it. Later Jacob also obtained his father’s blessing by a trick. He then had to flee from his angry brother. On the way he dreamed at **Bethel** of a **ladder** that reached up to heaven, with angels going up and down on it.

Many years later Jacob returned. One night at the river **Jabbok** he wrestled with a mysterious man until morning. After that he received the new name **Israel**. His twelve sons are regarded as the forefathers of the **twelve tribes of Israel**. According to tradition, the patriarchs were buried in the **Cave of Machpelah** in **Hebron**. The place is still holy to Jews and Muslims today.

gewusst: In Islam Abraham is called Ibrahim and is regarded as an important prophet.
Because of Abraham, Judaism, Christianity and Islam are also called the Abrahamic religions.

teile.einleitung: Anubis was a god of the ancient Egyptians. He had the head of a jackal and was responsible for the dead, for tombs and for embalming. He accompanied the dead on their way to the afterlife.
wichtigste: Anubis is shown as a man with a jackal’s head.
He was the god of the dead and of cemeteries.
Anubis was regarded as the god of mummification.
In pictures he is mostly black.
At the judgement of the dead, he weighed the heart of the deceased.
He led the dead into the afterlife and watched over the tombs.

abschnitte.titel: A god with a jackal’s head
abschnitte.text: Anubis is shown as a man with the head of a **jackal**. A jackal is a wild dog and looks similar to a dog. Sometimes the Egyptians also showed Anubis entirely as a lying jackal. In Egypt, jackals often roamed around the tombs at the edge of the desert. That is probably why the jackal became the animal of the god of the dead.

The ancient Egyptians believed that the body had to be preserved for life after death. That is why the dead were **embalmed** and made into mummies. Anubis was regarded as the god of this **mummification**. The priests who did this work sometimes wore an Anubis mask. In this way they showed that they were acting on behalf of the god.

According to Egyptian belief, every dead person came before a **judgement of the dead**. There the person’s **heart** was placed on a set of scales. On the other side lay a feather, which stood for truth and justice. Anubis supervised the weighing. If the heart was not heavier than the feather, the dead person was allowed to go on into the afterlife.

abschnitte.titel: Guardian of the cities of the dead
abschnitte.text: Anubis was regarded as lord of the **cities of the dead**, that is, the great cemeteries. He was supposed to protect the tombs from disturbance. He accompanied the dead and looked after them on their way to the afterlife. In pictures Anubis is usually painted **black**. Black recalled the fertile soil along the Nile and so new life.

gewusst: For the ancient Egyptians black was not a sad colour, but a sign of fertile soil and new life.
In the tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun, a large figure of Anubis as a lying jackal was found.

teile.einleitung: Many Catholics do not eat meat on Friday, but fish. This custom is very old and has to do with belief in Jesus. In Switzerland too, many canteens offer a fish dish on Fridays.
wichtigste: Many Catholics go without meat on Friday.
On Friday they think of the death of Jesus on the cross.
Going without is a small sacrifice and a form of fasting.
In tradition, fish did not count as meat and was therefore allowed.
The abstinence is especially strict on Good Friday and Ash Wednesday.

abschnitte.text: According to the Bible, Jesus died on the cross on a Friday. That is why Friday is a special day of reflection for Christians. The Catholic Church invites people to give something up on this day. For a long time this was above all **going without meat**. This is called **abstinence**. The abstinence is meant to show that you are thinking of the suffering of Jesus.

In the past meat was regarded as a special, festive food. According to the old tradition, fish did not count as meat. That is why it could be eaten on days of fasting too. So fish became the typical **Friday meal**. In monasteries people therefore often laid out fish ponds of their own. Fish was already an important sign for the first Christians: the Greek word for fish is **ichthys**.

abschnitte.titel: Days of fasting in the year
abschnitte.text: Abstinence is especially important on **Ash Wednesday** and **Good Friday**. Ash Wednesday is the beginning of the season of fasting before Easter, and Good Friday recalls the death of Jesus directly. On these two days adult Catholics are to fast and not eat meat. On the other Fridays the Church today also allows other good deeds instead of giving up meat, for example a prayer or help for others.

Today not all Catholics keep to the Friday without meat. Even so, the custom lives on, including among people who are not religious. In many Swiss restaurants, schools and canteens, a **fish dish** is on the menu on Fridays. Those who give up meat today usually decide for themselves how strictly they keep the custom.

gewusst: The letters of the Greek word ichthys were read as an abbreviation for “Jesus Christ, God’s Son, Saviour”.
Many Orthodox Christians too have days of fasting on which they give up meat.

teile.einleitung: A summit cross stands right at the top of a mountain. It marks the highest point and is a goal for walkers and mountaineers. At the same time it is a sign of the Christian faith.
wichtigste: A summit cross stands on the highest point of a mountain.
It is usually made of wood or metal.
Often a summit book lies nearby in a box.
The cross is a sign of the Christian faith.
Heavy summit crosses are today often brought up by helicopter.
In a thunderstorm it is dangerous at the summit cross, because lightning can strike.

abschnitte.text: A **summit cross** stands on the **highest point** of a mountain. Anyone who reaches it knows: I have arrived at the top. For many walkers the cross is therefore a fine **goal**. Summit crosses stand in the Alps, for example in Switzerland, Austria, Germany and Italy. You can often see them from far below in the valley.

The cross is the sign of **Christianity**. With the summit cross, people give thanks for **protection** in the mountains. Some crosses also recall people who had accidents in the mountains. Many summit crosses are blessed by a priest when they are put up. For many people the cross is a **holy sign**. That is why out of respect you do not climb about on it.

Summit crosses have to withstand **wind and weather**, including snow, ice and storms. That is why they are built of strong **wood** or **metal**. Often a weatherproof box with a **summit book** hangs on the cross. There mountaineers write their name, the date and sometimes a greeting. In the past people carried the crosses up over many hours. Today a **helicopter** often flies the heavy parts to the summit.

A summit cross is the highest point for miles around, especially if it is made of metal. That is why **lightning** often strikes there. In a **thunderstorm** you should leave the summit and the cross at once. It is best to check the **weather forecast** before a mountain tour. In Switzerland, a thunderstorm often builds up in the afternoon in summer.

gewusst: Not every summit has a cross: sometimes there is a cairn, a flag or a survey marker.
New summit crosses are sometimes argued about: some see in them an important sign, while others would rather leave the mountain tops without structures.

teile.einleitung: Gnosis is the name for religious movements in the first centuries after Christ. Their followers, the Gnostics, believed that secret knowledge redeems human beings. The Greek word “gnosis” means “knowledge”.
wichtigste: “Gnosis” is Greek and means “knowledge”.
The Gnostics believed that knowledge about God and the origin of the soul redeems.
The material world was seen as a prison for the divine spark in human beings.
They called the subordinate creator of the world the Demiurge.
In 1945 a large collection of Gnostic writings was found at Nag Hammadi in Egypt.
The Church Father Irenaeus of Lyon wrote against the Gnostics.

abschnitte.text: The **Gnostics** lived mainly in the 2nd and 3rd centuries after Christ. They believed that a **secret knowledge** about God and the origin of the soul redeems human beings. That is where the name comes from: **gnosis** means **knowledge** in Greek. There was not one single Gnosis, but many different groups and teachings. Some combined their ideas with Christianity.

Most Gnostic teachings saw the **material world** as something bad, even as a **prison**. According to their teaching, a **divine spark of light** is lodged in human beings. Through knowledge it is to be freed and return to the heavenly world. This world is called the **Pleroma**, Greek for “fullness”. There live the **aeons**, spiritual beings that emerge from the highest God.

The Gnostics distinguished the highest, hidden God from a subordinate **creator** of the material world. They called him the **Demiurge**. In Gnosis he is regarded as ignorant or even evil. Sometimes he is also called **Yaldabaoth**. This teaching differs greatly from the belief of the Christian Church, according to which the one good God created the world.

For a long time Gnosis was known almost only from the writings of its **opponents**. The most important was the work **“Against Heresies”**, which **Irenaeus of Lyon** wrote around 180 AD. A heresy is a teaching that the Church rejects. In **1945**, farmers near **Nag Hammadi** in Egypt found 13 papyrus volumes in a clay jar, written in the **Coptic** language. Among them is the **Gospel of Thomas** with 114 sayings of Jesus, which does not belong to the New Testament.

gewusst: The Gospel of Thomas contains no narrative about the life of Jesus, but only a collection of sayings.
Coptic is a late form of the ancient Egyptian language, written with Greek letters.

teile.einleitung: The Daodejing is the most important book of Daoism. It is attributed to the Chinese sage Laozi and, despite its brevity, is one of the most influential and most translated books in the world.
wichtigste: The title means roughly “Book of the Way and Its Power”.
The usual version has 81 short chapters in two parts.
The book has only about 5,000 written characters.
It is written in brief, poem-like verses.
Water is seen as a model, because it is soft and yet overcomes what is hard.
“Wu wei” means acting without forcing anything.

abschnitte.text: The title **Daodejing** is made up of three words. **Dao** means way, **de** means power or virtue, and **jing** stands for a classic book. That is why the title is often translated as “**Book of the Way and Its Power**”. According to tradition, the sage **Laozi** is the author. Who exactly wrote the book, and when, is disputed among scholars.

The Daodejing is a very short book. It has only about **5,000** Chinese characters. The usual version is divided into **81 short chapters** and two parts. Many chapters are written like little **poems**, brief and often mysterious. That is why there are very many different interpretations.

An important image in the Daodejing is **water**. It is soft and yielding. Even so, over time it can even hollow out **rock**. From this we learn that gentleness can be strong. Another basic concept is **wu wei**. This is often translated as “non-action”. But it does not mean doing nothing; it means natural action that **forces nothing**.

A well-known saying comes from the Daodejing: “**A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.**” The sentence is in **chapter 64**. It means that even great undertakings begin with a small start. Many people know the saying without knowing where it comes from.

The Daodejing is one of the **most translated books in the world**. It has been translated into very many languages, including several times into German. Every translation sounds a little different, because the old characters can have many meanings. In this way the book is still exciting for readers in Europe today.

gewusst: According to a legend, Laozi wrote the book at a border pass, because a guard asked him to write down his wisdom before he left the country.
In a tomb at Mawangdui in China, old copies of the Daodejing on silk were found.

teile.einleitung: Hindutva is a political idea from India. It sees Hindu culture as the foundation of the Indian nation. Supporters see in it pride in their own culture, critics a disadvantage for religious minorities.
wichtigste: The term Hindutva was coined by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar in 1923.
Hindutva is a form of Hindu nationalism.
In 1925 the RSS was founded in Nagpur, which is regarded as the core of the movement.
The party BJP, founded in 1980, is close to the idea.
On 6 December 1992, Hindu activists destroyed the Babri Mosque in Ayodhya.
In January 2024 a new Ram temple was consecrated in Ayodhya.

abschnitte.text: The term **Hindutva** comes from **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar**. In 1923, during his imprisonment, he wrote the pamphlet “Essentials of Hindutva”. In it he determined who is a Hindu: anyone who regards India as the **land of their ancestors** and as a **holy land**. In Sanskrit he called this pitribhumi and punyabhumi. In this way Jains, Buddhists and Sikhs also counted for him.

Hindutva sees India as a **Hindu nation**. Hindu culture is to be the foundation of the country. Supporters say it is about culture and national unity. **Critics** see in it a disadvantage for religious minorities, especially Muslims and Christians. According to its constitution, India is a secular state, that is, not tied to any religion. The relationship between religion and state is fiercely disputed in India.

In 1925, K. B. Hedgewar founded the **Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh**, **RSS** for short, in **Nagpur**. It is a large volunteer organisation and is regarded as the core of the Hindutva movement. Several parties and associations arose from its circle. The **Bharatiya Janata Party**, **BJP** for short, was founded in 1980 and is close to the idea. Since 2014 it has provided the prime minister, Narendra Modi (as of 2025).

In the city of **Ayodhya** stood the **Babri Mosque**. Many Hindus believe that the god **Rama** was born there. On **6 December 1992**, Hindu activists destroyed the mosque. Afterwards there were serious riots with many dead. In 2019 the Supreme Court of India decided that a temple may be built at this site. On **22 January 2024** the new **Ram temple** was consecrated.

gewusst: The word Hindutva means roughly “Hindu-ness” or “Hinduness”.
After Indonesia and Pakistan, India has one of the largest Muslim populations in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Bhagavad Gita is one of the most important texts of Hinduism. It tells of a conversation between the warrior Arjuna and the god Krishna before a great battle. Its name means “Song of the Lord”.
wichtigste: The Gita is part of the great epic Mahabharata.
It is a conversation between Krishna and Arjuna.
It is set on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.
The Gita has 18 chapters with about 700 verses.
It teaches that you should do your duty without craving the result.
It describes three paths: action, knowledge and devotion.
Sanjaya tells the blind king Dhritarashtra what is happening.

abschnitte.text: The **Bhagavad Gita** is in the sixth book of the **Mahabharata**, the Bhishma Parva. The Mahabharata is a huge epic about the war between the related families of the **Pandavas** and the **Kauravas**. The Gita has **18 chapters** with about 700 verses. The Mahabharata itself also has 18 books. In the framing story, **Sanjaya** tells the blind king **Dhritarashtra** what is happening on the battlefield.

The Gita is set on the battlefield of **Kurukshetra**, which it calls the “field of dharma”. There the armies face each other. The warrior **Arjuna** sees relatives and teachers on the other side. He doubts and does not want to fight. His charioteer **Krishna** instructs him and in doing so reveals himself as a god.

Krishna advises Arjuna to do his **duty** without clinging to the fruits of the action. This ideal is called **nishkama karma**, that is, acting without craving for the result. In this way, according to the teaching, no binding karma arises. What matters is not success, but doing the right thing with a pure heart. This idea also influenced people outside India.

The Gita describes three paths to liberation. **Karma yoga** is the path of selfless action. **Jnana yoga** is the path of knowledge. **Bhakti yoga** is the path of loving devotion to God. According to the Gita, all three paths lead to God, though devotion is especially stressed.

In chapter 11, Krishna shows his all-embracing form. From it comes a verse that the physicist **Robert Oppenheimer** quoted after the first atomic bomb test: “Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.” He later told this in an interview. **Mahatma Gandhi** also loved reading the Gita. It has been translated into many languages.

gewusst: Both the Bhagavad Gita and the Mahabharata are divided into 18 parts.
Mahatma Gandhi called the Bhagavad Gita his spiritual book of reference.

teile.einleitung: Auffahrt is a Christian holiday that is called by this name in Switzerland. In Germany it is called Christi Himmelfahrt. On this day, Christians remember that Jesus ascended into heaven.
wichtigste: Ascension Day is 40 days after Easter, counting Easter Sunday.
The holiday always falls on a Thursday.
Christians remember the ascension of Jesus.
The story is in the Acts of the Apostles in the Bible.
In Switzerland, Ascension Day is a public holiday.
Ten days later comes Pentecost.

abschnitte.text: On **Ascension Day**, Christians remember that Jesus ascended into heaven after his resurrection. The Bible tells of this in the **Acts of the Apostles**. After Easter, Jesus showed himself to his disciples for 40 days. Then he was taken up into heaven before their eyes, and a cloud hid him. In Germany the day is called **Christi Himmelfahrt**.

Ascension Day is on the **40th day after Easter**, counting Easter Sunday. That is why the holiday always falls on a **Thursday**. Because Easter is on a different date every year, Ascension Day moves too. It falls between 30 April and 3 June. Ten days after Ascension Day, Christians celebrate **Pentecost**.

In Switzerland, Ascension Day is a **public holiday** in all the cantons. Schools and many shops stay closed. Many people take the Friday after it off and so have a long weekend, the **Auffahrtsbrücke**, or “Ascension bridge”. That is why Ascension Day is a popular time for outings and short holidays. In many churches there are services, sometimes outdoors.

For Christians, Ascension Day means that Jesus is with God. At the same time, according to their faith, he is still close to people. In the Bible, Jesus promises his disciples the **Holy Spirit**. At Pentecost, Christians then celebrate that this promise was fulfilled. Ascension Day, Easter and Pentecost are therefore closely connected.

gewusst: Ascension Day can fall at the earliest on 30 April and at the latest on 3 June.
The name “Auffahrt” is typical of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Gall was a monk who came to Lake Constance about 1,400 years ago. At the place where he settled, a monastery later arose, and from it the town of St Gallen. Many legends are woven around him, the best known being about a bear.
wichtigste: Gall was a monk and spread the Christian faith.
According to the old tradition, he came from Ireland.
He travelled to Lake Constance with the monk Columbanus.
He built himself a cell in the forest on the Steinach.
The town of St Gallen is named after him.
His feast day, St Gall’s Day, is 16 October.

abschnitte.text: Old biographies name **Ireland** as Gall’s homeland. Today experts do not entirely agree about his origins. Gall was a **monk** and travelled through Europe with his teacher **Columbanus** and other monks. They wanted to spread the Christian faith. Around the year 610 they came to **Lake Constance**. When Columbanus moved on to Italy, Gall stayed behind.

Gall withdrew into the forest to pray there. According to the legend, he fell into a **thorn thicket**. He saw the fall as a sign from God and decided to stay in this place. There, on the river **Steinach**, he built himself a simple **cell**, that is, a small hut to live and pray in. Gall died around the year 640.

One evening a **bear** came to Gall’s campfire. Gall asked it to fetch **wood** for the fire. The bear obeyed and brought wood. In thanks Gall gave it a **piece of bread** and sent it away into the mountains. That is why the bear is still the heraldic animal of the town of St Gallen today.

About 80 years after Gall’s death, the monk **Othmar** founded a monastery at this place in the year 719. The **Abbey of St Gall** became an important centre of learning and books in the Middle Ages. The town of **St Gallen** grew up around the monastery. The abbey district with the famous **Abbey Library** has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983. On **16 October**, St Gall’s Day is celebrated.

gewusst: In the Abbey Library of St Gall there are very old manuscripts, some of them over 1,000 years old.
The coat of arms of Appenzell also shows a bear, because the Appenzell region once belonged to the Abbey of St Gall.

teile.einleitung: Jupiter was the highest god of the ancient Romans. He was regarded as king of the gods and lord of the sky, lightning and thunder. The largest planet of our solar system is also named after him.
wichtigste: Jupiter was the king of the gods for the Romans.
He corresponded to the Greek Zeus.
His most important temple stood on the Capitoline Hill in Rome.
With Juno and Minerva he formed the most important group of gods in Rome.
Minerva corresponded to the Greek Athena.
The largest planet of the solar system bears his name.

abschnitte.text: **Jupiter** was the highest god of the Romans. He ruled over the sky and the weather. His weapon was the **thunderbolt**, and his sacred animal was the **eagle**. Jupiter corresponded to the Greek god **Zeus**. Many stories about Zeus the Romans also told about Jupiter.

The most important temple for Jupiter stood on the **Capitoline Hill**, one of the seven hills of Rome. There he was worshipped as Jupiter Optimus Maximus, the “Best and Greatest”. In the same temple, **Juno**, goddess of women and marriage, and **Minerva**, goddess of wisdom, were also honoured. These three are called the **Capitoline Triad**. Minerva corresponded to the Greek **Athena**.

In the area of present-day Switzerland too, Jupiter was worshipped. On the summit of the **Great St Bernard Pass** there stood in Roman times a sanctuary of **Jupiter Poeninus**. Travellers asked him there for a safe crossing of the Alps. The god lives on in French too: Thursday is called **“jeudi”**, which comes from “day of Jupiter”.

The planet **Jupiter** is the largest planet of our solar system. That is why its name suits the king of the gods well. It is a gas planet and has very many moons. Galileo Galilei discovered the four largest in 1610. In the night sky Jupiter often shines brighter than any star.

gewusst: The French name for Thursday, “jeudi”, comes from the god Jupiter.
More than a thousand Earths would fit inside the planet Jupiter.

teile.einleitung: A **dreidel** is a small spinning top with four sides. Jewish children play with it at the festival of lights, **Hanukkah**. On each side is a Hebrew letter, and in the game each letter has a meaning of its own.
wichtigste: A dreidel is a spinning top with four sides.
It is played with at Hanukkah.
Children often play for chocolate coins.
The letters stand for: “A great miracle happened there.”
If the dreidel lands on gimel, you win everything.
If it lands on nun, nothing happens.

abschnitte.text: **Hanukkah** lasts eight days and usually falls in December. The festival recalls the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem over 2,000 years ago. According to tradition, a small jar of oil was enough for the lamp for eight days. That is why one more light is lit each evening on the **Hanukkah menorah**. Games such as the dreidel are also part of the festival.

On the dreidel are the Hebrew letters **nun**, **gimel**, **he** and **shin**. They are the first letters of the words “Nes gadol haya sham”. That means: **“A great miracle happened there.”** This refers to the miracle of the oil in Jerusalem. In Israel the letter pe stands in place of shin. Then it reads: “A great miracle happened here.”

First all the children put something in the middle, often **chocolate coins**, nuts or sweets. Then each child in turn spins the top. With **nun** nothing happens. With **gimel** you get everything from the middle. With **he** you get half. With **shin** you have to put something into the middle. Whoever has the most at the end has won.

gewusst: The word dreidel comes from Yiddish and has to do with “turning”. In Hebrew it is called a sevivon.
At Hanukkah people like to eat foods fried in oil, for example potato pancakes and doughnuts.

teile.einleitung: A gurdwara is the house of worship of the Sikhs. Their holy scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, lies there, and the community prays and sings together. Everyone is welcome, whatever their religion.
wichtigste: Gurdwara means “door to the Guru”.
The holy scripture of the Sikhs lies in the gurdwara.
The assembled community is called the sangat.
In the communal kitchen, the langar, everyone gets a free meal.
Visitors cover their heads and take off their shoes.
Outside every gurdwara flies the flag Nishan Sahib.
In Langenthal stands the first traditionally built gurdwara in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The word **gurdwara** is made up of “guru” and “dwara”. Dwara means door or gate. In the gurdwara lies the holy scripture of the Sikhs, the **Guru Granth Sahib**. The community that gathers to pray and sing is called the **sangat**. Everyone sits together on the floor, without distinction of rank or origin.

Every gurdwara includes a communal kitchen, the **langar**. There all visitors receive a meal free of charge. It does not matter where someone comes from or what they believe. Volunteers cook, serve and wash up. In this way the Sikh teaching shows that all people are of equal worth.

Anyone who visits a gurdwara **covers their head** and **takes off their shoes**. This is a sign of respect. Often you also wash your hands. Smoking and alcohol are forbidden in the gurdwara. Outside every gurdwara flies the **Nishan Sahib**, a mostly orange flag with the Khanda symbol. By it you can recognise the building from far away.

The best-known gurdwara is the **Golden Temple** in Amritsar in India. It stands in the middle of a holy pool, the **Amrit Sarovar**. The name means “pool of nectar”, and the city of Amritsar is named after it. Pilgrims bathe in it. In the langar of the Golden Temple, very many people eat every day.

Some thousands of Sikhs live in Switzerland. The first gurdwara in the traditional style of building was completed in 2006 in **Langenthal** in the canton of Bern. It has a white façade and domes, as you know them from India. As everywhere, guests are welcome there too.

gewusst: In the langar of the Golden Temple, over 50,000 meals are served on some days.
In the gurdwara the Guru Granth Sahib is honoured like a living teacher; at night it is taken to a room of its own.

teile.einleitung: Aventicum was the main town of the Helvetii in Roman times. Today the small town of Avenches in the canton of Vaud stands on this spot. In the 1st to 3rd centuries, Aventicum was the largest town on Swiss soil.
wichtigste: Aventicum lies at today’s Avenches in the canton of Vaud.
It was the main town of the Helvetii.
Emperor Vespasian raised the town to the status of a colony around AD 70.
The Cigognier sanctuary is named after a stork’s nest.
In 1939 a gold bust of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius was found.
The amphitheatre held about 14,000 to 16,000 spectators.

abschnitte.text: On the site of today’s **Avenches** in the canton of Vaud lay **Aventicum**. It was the main town of the **Helvetii**, a Celtic people. In the 1st to 3rd centuries, Aventicum was the largest town on Swiss soil. At times probably around 20,000 people lived there. A long town wall with towers surrounded the town.

Around AD 70, Emperor **Vespasian** raised Aventicum to the status of a **colony**. This was an honour for a town. According to the historian **Suetonius**, Vespasian’s father had lived among the Helvetii as a moneylender and died there. The town afterwards bore the additional name **Flavia**, after the emperor’s family.

The **Cigognier sanctuary** gets its name from a stork’s nest on its last standing column. “Cigogne” is the French word for stork. The column is about 12 metres high. At the **Grange des Dîmes** temple there was an older Celtic place of worship. In the early Middle Ages this temple was turned into a **church**.

In 1939, a **gold bust** of the Emperor **Marcus Aurelius** was discovered in a drain near the Cigognier. It is 33.5 cm high and weighs about 1.6 kg. It was probably hidden from plundering Alemanni. The **amphitheatre** held about 14,000 to 16,000 spectators. In the past there were animal hunts and gladiator fights there; today there are concerts and opera performances.

gewusst: The only standing column of the Cigognier sanctuary really did carry a stork’s nest in the past.
The gold bust of Marcus Aurelius is one of the best-known Roman finds in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Christ is not a surname, but a title. It means “the anointed one”. Christians call Jesus of Nazareth this because they see in him the saviour sent by God.
wichtigste: Christ means “the anointed one”.
The word comes from Greek.
The Hebrew word with the same meaning is Messiah.
In the past, kings were anointed with oil.
The word Christians comes from Christ.

abschnitte.text: **Christ** is a **Greek** word and means “**the anointed one**”. In ancient Israel, **kings** and sometimes priests were anointed with **oil**. Oil was poured on their heads. This showed that God had chosen them for a special task.

In Hebrew, “the anointed one” is **Messiah**. The Jews expected a Messiah who would be sent by God. **Christians** believe that **Jesus of Nazareth** is this Messiah. That is why they call him **Jesus Christ**. Christ is therefore a title, not a surname. Judaism does not regard Jesus as the Messiah.

From the word Christ comes the name **Christians** for his followers, and from that the word **Christianity**. An early symbol of the Christians is the **Chi-Rho monogram**: the Greek letters **chi** and **rho**, the first letters of Christ, placed one on top of the other. The **fish** was also an early sign by which Christians recognised each other.

gewusst: The Greek word for fish, “ichthys”, was read by early Christians as an abbreviation for “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour”.
Even the Christmas season carries the title in its name: in English, Weihnachten is called “Christmas”.

teile.einleitung: The cult of Isis is the worship of the Egyptian goddess Isis, which spread far beyond Egypt in antiquity. In the Roman Empire, Isis had temples, festivals and priests. Her cult lasted until the 6th century.
wichtigste: In Egyptian mythology Isis is the wife of Osiris and mother of Horus.
In the Roman Empire Isis was regarded as the protector of sailors.
The festival Navigium Isidis in March celebrated the opening of the sailing season.
A typical instrument of the cult is the sistrum, a metal rattle.
In Rome the great sanctuary Iseum Campense stood on the Campus Martius.
Isis was often worshipped together with the god Serapis.
The temple of Philae was the last temple of Isis in use.

abschnitte.text: In Egyptian mythology **Isis** is the wife of **Osiris**. According to the myth, she gathered the parts of Osiris, killed by Seth, and raised him to life again. Her son is **Horus**. This story of grief, loyalty and new life made Isis very attractive to many people. After the time of Alexander the Great, her cult spread throughout the Mediterranean region.

In the Roman Empire Isis was regarded as the **protector of sailors**. At the festival of **Navigium Isidis** in March, the opening of the sailing season was celebrated. A decorated ship was given to the sea. Typical of the cult was the **sistrum**, a metal rattle with movable plates on rods. It was shaken at processions and services.

In Rome the great sanctuary **Iseum Campense** stood on the Campus Martius. Under Emperor Domitian it was splendidly rebuilt. Several Egyptian **obelisks** that stand in Rome today come from there. In **Pompeii** the temple of Isis had been rebuilt after an earthquake. When Vesuvius erupted in the year 79 AD, the ash covered it and preserved it together with its wall paintings.

Isis was often worshipped together with **Serapis**. This god was introduced in Egypt under King Ptolemy I. He combined features of Osiris with features of Greek gods. In this way the cult suited Egyptians, Greeks and Romans at the same time.

The cult of Isis is also known from literature. In the ancient novel **“Metamorphoses”** by Apuleius, also called “The Golden Ass”, Lucius is turned into a donkey. The goddess Isis makes him human again. In the eleventh book he is initiated into her **mysteries**, that is, secret ceremonies only for initiates. On the Nile island of **Philae**, Isis was still worshipped until the 6th century, until Emperor Justinian had the temple closed.

gewusst: Some Egyptian obelisks in Rome come from the sanctuary of Isis.
The temple of Philae was moved to a neighbouring island because of the Aswan Dam.

teile.einleitung: “God is dead” is a famous sentence by the German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche. By it he did not mean that a being had died, but that belief in God had lost its strength in modern culture. Nietzsche asked what this means for people’s values.
wichtigste: The sentence is in aphorism 125 of “The Gay Science” from the year 1882.
There “the madman” searches for God with a lantern in the bright morning.
He holds people themselves responsible for the death of God.
Nietzsche saw nihilism as the danger.
In “Thus Spoke Zarathustra” he sets the Übermensch against the dead God.
From 1869 Nietzsche was a professor at the University of Basel.

abschnitte.text: In his book **“The Gay Science”** of **1882**, Nietzsche tells a short story in **aphorism 125**. An aphorism is a short text with one thought. A man, **“the madman”**, runs into the marketplace in the bright morning with a lit **lantern**. He cries: “I am looking for God!” The people laugh at him. The image recalls the ancient philosopher **Diogenes**, who searched for a human being with a lantern.

The madman cries: **“God is dead!”** and says: “We have killed him, you and I!” So he holds **people themselves** responsible. What is meant is that modern culture, for example through science and new ways of thinking, has itself dissolved belief in God. Nietzsche describes this as a great event whose consequences people have not yet understood at all. Believers naturally see the question of God differently.

If God, as the ground of all values, falls away, all values threaten to become **meaningless**. Nietzsche called this state **nihilism**, from the Latin word “nihil” for “nothing”. He demanded a **revaluation of all values**. In “On the Genealogy of Morality” of **1887**, he criticised the morality that he ascribed to Christianity and called it **slave morality**. In **“Thus Spoke Zarathustra”** he sets the dead God against the **Übermensch** (“overman”), who is to create new values himself.

**Friedrich Nietzsche** lived from 1844 to 1900. At only 24, in **1869**, he became professor of classical philology at the **University of Basel**. Philology is the study of languages and ancient texts. He taught in Basel until 1879. Later he spent many summers in **Sils Maria** in the Engadine, where he worked on his books. Today the Nietzsche House there recalls him.

gewusst: Nietzsche became a professor in Basel before he had finished his doctoral thesis.
In Sils Maria you can today visit the house where Nietzsche lived in summer as a small museum.

teile.einleitung: The sign of peace is a short moment in the service. In the Catholic Mass, people wish each other peace. As they do so, they usually shake hands.
wichtigste: The sign of peace is part of the Catholic Mass.
People wish each other peace and shake hands.
Often people say “Peace be with you” as they do so.
The sign of peace comes just before Communion.
The custom goes back to the first Christians.

abschnitte.text: At the **sign of peace** you turn to the people nearby, for example in the pew in front or beside you. You shake **hands** and say “Peace be with you” or simply “Peace”. It does not matter whether you know the others or not. The greeting lasts only a moment. Then the Mass continues.

The sign of peace has a fixed place in the **Mass**. It comes after the shared prayer of the **Our Father** and just before **Communion**. At Communion the faithful receive the host. First the priest says a prayer for peace. Then he invites the people to give each other a sign of peace.

The greeting is meant to show that everyone in the church belongs to one **community**. Anyone who has a quarrel should make peace before celebrating together with the others. This recalls a saying of Jesus in the Bible: you should first be reconciled with your brother. Even the **first Christians** greeted one another in worship as a sign of peace. In other Christian churches too there are similar greetings.

Not everywhere do people shake hands. In some countries people only bow or nod to one another in a friendly way. In times when illnesses spread easily, many parishes give up the handshake. Then people simply smile at one another. What matters is not the form, but the wish for **peace**.

gewusst: The sign of peace is one of the few moments in the Mass when the faithful speak directly to one another.
The words “Peace be with you” are an old greeting in many other languages too, for example “Shalom” in Hebrew.

teile.einleitung: The Fraumünster is a well-known church in the old town of Zurich. It stands on the Limmat and was formerly a convent for women. Today it is famous above all for its colourful stained-glass windows by Marc Chagall.
wichtigste: The Fraumünster stands in Zurich on the left bank of the Limmat.
It goes back to a convent for women founded in the year 853.
The founder was the East Frankish king Louis the German.
With the Reformation the convent was dissolved; today it is a Reformed church.
Marc Chagall created the five large choir windows around 1970.
The windows show stories from the Bible.

abschnitte.text: In the year **853**, King **Louis the German** founded a convent for noble women in Zurich. His daughter **Hildegard** became the first abbess, that is, the head of the convent. The abbesses of the Fraumünster were very powerful for a long time. They had, for example, the right to mint coins in Zurich. The name “Fraumünster” (“Women’s Minster”) recalls the women who lived here.

In the 16th century the **Reformation** changed the life of the Church strongly in Zurich. The last abbess, **Katharina von Zimmern**, handed the convent over to the city of Zurich of her own free will in 1524. In this way she prevented quarrels and violence. Since then the Fraumünster has been a **Reformed church**. The convent buildings afterwards served the city for other purposes.

Around 1970 the artist **Marc Chagall** created the five large **stained-glass windows** in the choir of the Fraumünster. Chagall was already over 80 years old at the time. The windows glow in strong blue, green, red and yellow. They show stories from the **Bible**, for example from the life of Jesus. Many people from all over the world visit the church to see these windows.

In the transept of the Fraumünster there is another large window by the Swiss artist **Augusto Giacometti**. In the old cloister next to the church, murals by **Paul Bodmer** tell the founding legend of the convent. The Fraumünster has a slender tower with a green spire. Together with the Grossmünster and St Peter, it shapes the old town of Zurich.

gewusst: According to the legend, a stag with a shining antler led the king’s daughters to the place where the convent was to be built.
The Fraumünster is one of the best-known sights of the city of Zurich.

teile.einleitung: The “House of Religions, Dialogue of Cultures” stands in Bern. Here several religions have their prayer rooms under a single roof. The house is meant to promote encounter and dialogue between the religions.
wichtigste: The House of Religions stands on Europaplatz in Bern.
It was opened on 14 December 2014.
The association behind it was founded in 2002.
Eight religions take part.
Under one roof there are, for example, a Hindu temple, a mosque and a church.
Jews and Baha’is take part, but have no room of their own.
Since 2015 the Hindu community has also ordained women as priestesses.

abschnitte.text: The **House of Religions** stands in the west of **Bern**, on **Europaplatz** in the Ausserholligen district. The building lies in a triangle between motorway and railway line. What is special: several religions have their **prayer rooms under one roof** here. There is a Hindu temple, a mosque, a church, and Buddhist and Alevi rooms. The house is known all over Switzerland for dialogue.

The association “House of Religions, Dialogue of Cultures” was founded on **25 April 2002**. In 2006 it received the integration prize of the city of Bern. Many more years passed before the house stood. It was opened on **14 December 2014**. The mosque in the house followed in April 2015.

**Eight religions** take part in the House of Religions. They include, among others, Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Buddhism and Sikhism, along with Alevis and Baha’is. The **Jewish Community of Bern** and the **Baha’i community** support the project, but do without prayer rooms of their own in the house. All communities work together in the shared association.

Since 2015 the Bern Hindu community has also ordained **women as priestesses**. In the countries of origin of most members, this is hardly possible. In this way the house has also received attention beyond Switzerland.

The house is not only for believers. School classes, families and tourists can visit it and take part in guided tours. There are events, courses and a restaurant with dishes from different cultures. In this way people of different origins get to know one another.

gewusst: In the same building there are also flats and shops, not only prayer rooms.
A Hindu temple with priestesses was new for the whole of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The dastar is the Sikh turban. Many Sikh men and some Sikh women wear it as a sign of their faith. It covers and protects the long, uncut hair.
wichtigste: Dastar is the Sikh word for their turban.
It covers the long, uncut hair, which is called kesh.
A turban is tied from a long strip of cloth several metres long.
Small boys often wear a simpler cloth, the patka.
Under the turban many Sikhs wear a small comb, the kangha.
On the wrist many wear a steel bangle, the kara.

abschnitte.text: **Sikhism** is a religion that arose in the 15th century in the **Punjab** in the north of India. Many Sikh men wear a **turban**. In Punjabi it is called a **dastar**. It is tied anew every day. For many Sikhs it is an important sign of their faith and their dignity.

Many devout Sikhs do not cut their **hair**. Uncut hair is called **kesh** and is regarded as a sign of faith. The turban **covers** and protects the long hair and keeps it clean and neatly together. Under the turban, many wear a small wooden comb in their hair. It is called a **kangha**.

A turban is a long strip of **cloth**. It is usually about **five to six metres** long. It is wound several times around the head until the turban sits firmly. This takes practice. Small boys often wear a **patka** first. This is a simple cloth that holds the hair together.

For many Sikhs, other signs of faith go with the turban. On the wrist they wear a bangle of steel or iron, the **kara**. It is round and recalls **God**, who has no beginning and no end. Sikhs live in **Switzerland** too, and there are Sikh temples called **gurdwaras**, for example in Langenthal.

gewusst: Turbans come in many colours; some Sikhs choose the colour to suit a festival or their clothes.
In a gurdwara, all visitors are given a free meal, whatever religion they belong to.

teile.einleitung: Basel Minster is one of the best-known churches in Switzerland. It is built of red sandstone and stands high above the Rhine. With its two towers, it is a landmark of the city of Basel.
wichtigste: Basel Minster is built of red sandstone.
It stands on Minster Hill high above the Rhine.
It has two towers, the St George’s Tower and the St Martin’s Tower.
In the past it was the church of the Bishop of Basel.
It was badly damaged in the earthquake of 1356.
Since the Reformation it has been a Protestant church.
The scholar Erasmus of Rotterdam is buried here.

abschnitte.text: **Basel Minster** stands on Minster Hill high above the **Rhine**. It is built of **red sandstone**, which is why it glows reddish. The colourful roof is covered with coloured tiles. Behind the church lies the **Pfalz**, a terrace with a view over the Rhine. From there you can see far across the city to the Black Forest.

The minster has two towers. They are called the **St George’s Tower** and the **St Martin’s Tower**, after Saint George and Saint Martin. On the St George’s Tower the saint is shown as a dragon slayer. You can climb the towers. At the top there is a fine view over Basel and the Dreiland, where Switzerland, Germany and France meet.

The minster was once the church of the **Bishop of Basel**. It was begun in the **Romanesque** style and later rebuilt in the **Gothic** style. In the great **Basel earthquake** of 1356 it was badly damaged. After that it was rebuilt. A fine example of Romanesque art is the **Gallus Portal**, a richly decorated entrance gate.

In 1529 Basel became **Protestant**. Since then the minster has been a Protestant church, and many pictures and figures were removed at that time. The famous scholar **Erasmus of Rotterdam**, who lived in Basel for a long time, is buried in the minster. In the 15th century a great council of the Church met in Basel. Today services and concerts are held in the minster.

gewusst: The Basel earthquake of 1356 is regarded as the strongest known earthquake in Central Europe.
From the Pfalz behind the minster, you can see as far as the Black Forest in good weather.

teile.einleitung: The Bodhi tree is the tree under which, according to tradition, Siddhartha Gautama found enlightenment and became the Buddha. It is one of the most important symbols of Buddhism.
wichtigste: Siddhartha found enlightenment under the Bodhi tree.
“Bodhi” means awakening or enlightenment.
The Bodhi tree is a sacred fig, that is, a type of fig tree.
Its leaves are heart-shaped and have a long tip.
It stands in Bodhgaya in the Indian state of Bihar.
In Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka, a very old tree grows from a cutting.

abschnitte.text: According to tradition, **Siddhartha Gautama** sat down under a large tree and **meditated** for a long time. He was then about **35 years** old. The demon **Mara** wanted to distract him with fear and temptations. But Siddhartha remained sitting calmly. In the end he recognised the truth and became the **Buddha**, the “Awakened One”.

The name comes from the word **bodhi**, which means awakening or enlightenment. The tree is a **sacred fig**, which belongs to the **fig trees**. Its leaves are **heart-shaped** and end in a long tip. They are often seen as a symbol in Buddhist pictures. Sacred figs can grow very large and very old.

The place where the Bodhi tree stands is called **Bodhgaya**. It lies in the state of **Bihar** in eastern India. Next to the tree stands the great **Mahabodhi Temple**. Bodhgaya is the most important place of pilgrimage in Buddhism. Every year very many pilgrims come there from all over the world.

According to tradition, a cutting of the Bodhi tree was brought to **Sri Lanka**. In the city of **Anuradhapura** stands the tree that grew from it. It was planted over 2,200 years ago and is regarded as one of the oldest trees planted by humans whose planting date is known. Many Bodhi trees in Buddhist monasteries around the world are descended from such cuttings.

gewusst: The tree in Anuradhapura has been cared for and guarded for over 2,000 years.
Buddhists celebrate the day of enlightenment as “Bodhi Day”.

teile.einleitung: In Hinduism a guru is a spiritual teacher. He accompanies his pupils on the spiritual path and passes on knowledge. The word comes from Sanskrit, the ancient language of India.
wichtigste: A guru is a spiritual teacher.
The Sanskrit word “guru” literally means “heavy” or “weighty”.
In Sanskrit the pupil is called a shishya.
The chain of teachers and pupils is called the guru-shishya-parampara.
At the festival of Guru Purnima, Hindus honour their teachers.

abschnitte.text: In **Hinduism** a **guru** is a teacher who shows others the way to knowledge and inner peace. He explains holy texts, teaches meditation and gives advice for life. Literally, “guru” in **Sanskrit** means “heavy” or “weighty”. What is meant is that the teacher is significant and venerable. The word is also important in Buddhism and among the Sikhs.

The pupil of a guru is called a **shishya** in Sanskrit. In the past, pupils often lived with the teacher and learned from him over many years. Later the pupil passes the knowledge on to pupils of his own. In this way a long chain of tradition arises, the **guru-shishya-parampara**. In this way teachings, music and dance were handed down over generations.

On **Guru Purnima**, Hindus thank their gurus and teachers. The festival is celebrated at the full moon in June or July. People bring their teachers flowers or gifts and remember what they have learned from them. Buddhists and Jains also celebrate at this full moon.

In English too, the word guru is used in everyday speech today. For example, someone who knows a great deal about computers is called a “computer guru”. Sometimes the word also sounds critical, when someone binds followers to himself. In religion itself, however, a guru is above all a respected teacher.

gewusst: Among the Sikhs, the holy scripture itself is regarded as the eternal guru.
Many classical Indian musicians still learn from a single guru over years today.

teile.einleitung: Ásatrú is a modern religion based on the old gods of the Viking Age. Its followers revere gods such as Odin, Thor and Freyja. The community in Iceland, where it is officially recognised, is especially well known.
wichtigste: Ásatrú means roughly “faith in the Aesir”.
The Icelandic community Ásatrúarfélagið was founded in 1972.
A year later it was officially recognised.
The most important ritual is called blót.
Important sources are the Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda.
The high priest is called the Allsherjargoði.

abschnitte.text: The name **Ásatrú** means roughly **faith in the Aesir**. The **Aesir** are a group of gods in Norse mythology, including **Odin** and **Thor**. Alongside them are the **Vanir** with Njörd, Freyr and Freyja. According to the myth, the Aesir and the Vanir went to war and then made peace. The Old Norse word “trú” means faith or loyalty.

In **1972** the community **Ásatrúarfélagið** was founded in Iceland. The poet **Sveinbjörn Beinteinsson** was at its centre. A year later it received **official recognition** as a religious community. Its high priest bears the title **Allsherjargoði**. In Old Norse, a goði was a priest and chieftain.

The central ritual is called **blót**. In it, the participants offer the gods food and drink, mostly **mead** or beer. Another ritual is the **sumbel**: a drinking horn is passed around in several rounds. The participants honour gods and ancestors or make vows. The terms **seiðr** and **galdr**, by contrast, refer to forms of magic.

What the people of the Viking Age believed exactly is only partly known. The most important sources are the **Poetic Edda** and the **Prose Edda**. They were written down in Iceland in the **13th century** and contain myths about the Norse gods. Ásatrú is therefore a **reconstruction**: its followers try to bring the old faith back to life from these texts.

gewusst: Thursday is named after the thunder god, whom the Norse peoples called Thor.
In Iceland, Ásatrú was officially recognised just a year after the community was founded.

teile.einleitung: The Cathedral of Notre-Dame in Lausanne is one of the most important Gothic churches in Switzerland. It sits high above the city on Lake Geneva. It is also famous for its night watchman, who calls out the hours every night.
wichtigste: The cathedral of Lausanne is called Notre-Dame.
It is regarded as one of the most important Gothic buildings in Switzerland.
It was solemnly consecrated in 1275.
Since the Reformation it has been a Reformed church.
A night watchman, “le guet”, calls out the hours from the tower at night.

abschnitte.text: The **Cathedral of Notre-Dame** stands on a hill in the middle of the old town of **Lausanne**. It was built in the **Gothic** style, with high pointed arches and large windows. Many regard it as the most important Gothic building in Switzerland. In **1275** it was solemnly consecrated, in the presence of Pope Gregory X and King Rudolf of Habsburg.

Especially famous is the **rose window**, a large round window from the 13th century. Its coloured glass pictures show the world as people imagined it in the Middle Ages: seasons, months, signs of the zodiac and the four elements. The richly decorated **portal** with painted figures is also worth seeing. Since the **Reformation** of 1536, the cathedral has been a Reformed church.

An old tradition lives on in Lausanne. Every night a **night watchman** climbs the tower of the cathedral. In French he is called “**le guet**”. Between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m., after every striking of the hour, he calls out in all directions: “C’est le guet, il a sonné l’heure”. That means: “Here is the watchman, the hour has struck”. In the past the watchman warned above all of **fires** in the city.

gewusst: Lausanne is one of the few cities in Europe where a night watchman still calls out the hours every night.
At the consecration of the cathedral in 1275, a pope and a king were present at the same time.

teile.einleitung: **Epicurus** was a Greek philosopher who lived from 341 to 270 BC. He asked how people can lead a happy life. His answer: through friendship, a simple life and a soul without fear.
wichtigste: Epicurus lived from 341 to 270 BC.
Around 306 BC he founded his school “The Garden” in Athens.
His goal was ataraxia, peace of mind.
For him the gods exist, but do not care about human beings.
He took over the teaching about atoms from Democritus.
In the “Letter to Menoeceus” he writes: death is nothing to us.

abschnitte.text: Epicurus was born on the island of **Samos**. Around 306 BC he bought a house with a garden in **Athens** and founded his school there. That is why it was simply called **“The Garden”**. Unusually, women and slaves also belonged to it. People lived together modestly, and **friendship** was especially important.

For Epicurus the goal of life is **pleasure**, in the sense of well-being. But by this he did not mean feasts and luxury. For him happiness is above all freedom from pain in the body and from unease in the soul. He called this **peace of mind** **ataraxia**. Whoever needs little is easily satisfied. Bread and water were often enough for him as a meal.

Epicurus took over from **Democritus** the teaching that everything consists of tiny, indivisible **atoms**. The world comes about when atoms combine, not through the will of gods. According to Epicurus, the **gods** do exist. But they live happily by themselves and **do not care about human beings**. That is why one need not fear them.

In the **“Letter to Menoeceus”** Epicurus explains his teaching briefly. A famous thought runs: **death is nothing to us.** As long as we live, death is not there. When death is there, we are no more. So one should not fear it. In this way Epicurus wants to take a great fear away from people.

The Christian writer **Lactantius** handed down an argument that people connect with Epicurus. It asks: if God wants to prevent evil and can, why does evil exist? This question later came to be called the **problem of theodicy**. Whether the argument really comes from Epicurus is uncertain. But it is still discussed in philosophy and theology today.

gewusst: The Roman poet Lucretius presented Epicurus’s teaching in the long poem “On the Nature of Things”.
Today the word “Epicurean” is often used for people who enjoy good living, although Epicurus himself lived very modestly.

teile.einleitung: A chapel is a small house of worship. In Switzerland many chapels stand along paths, on mountain pastures and in villages. They often tell of the worries and thanks of people in earlier times.
wichtigste: A chapel is a small church, often with only a few pews.
In the Swiss mountains many chapels stand along paths and on mountain pastures.
There mountain farmers asked for protection from avalanches, rockfall and thunderstorms.
Votive pictures are painted pictures of thanks for a rescue.
The small bell turret on the roof is called a roof ridge turret.
The Tell Chapel on Lake Uri recalls William Tell.

abschnitte.text: A **chapel** is a small house of worship. Often it has only a few pews and a simple altar. The word comes from the Latin “cappa”, the cloak of Saint **Martin**. This cloak was once kept in a small room that was called a “capella”. Chapels are found not only in the open air, but also in hospitals, castles or schools.

In the Swiss mountains, people built many chapels along paths and on **mountain pastures**. There were dangers there such as **avalanches**, rockfall and thunderstorms. In the chapel the mountain farmers asked for **protection**. A small mountain chapel does not normally have a priest of its own. A priest comes by only now and then for a Mass.

abschnitte.titel: Pictures of thanks and little bells
abschnitte.text: When someone had been rescued, they often hung a painted **votive picture** in a chapel. On it you see, for example, an accident and a saint who helps. On the roof of many chapels stands a small turret with a bell, the **roof ridge turret**. Even smaller is the **wayside shrine** by the path. This is a small pillar with a picture of Jesus, Mary or a saint.

One of the best-known chapels in Switzerland is the **Tell Chapel** on the shore of **Lake Uri**. It stands at the Tellsplatte. According to the legend, **William Tell** leapt from the boat there and so escaped the bailiff Gessler. Inside, large murals show scenes from the story of Tell. Many boats on Lake Lucerne stop nearby.

There are chapels in cities too. The famous **Chapel Bridge** in Lucerne takes its name from the chapel of St Peter, which stands nearby. Some chapels recall a special event or a saint. Others were built as thanks after an illness was survived. In this way almost every chapel has its own history.

gewusst: The word chapel goes back to the cloak of Saint Martin.
The Chapel Bridge in Lucerne is named after a chapel.

teile.einleitung: The Hebrew alphabet is the script in which the Torah, and today the language of Israel, is written. It has 22 letters and is read from right to left.
wichtigste: The Hebrew alphabet has 22 letters.
It is written from right to left.
The first letter is called alef, the second bet.
The last letter is called tav.
Usually only consonants are written, and the vowels are missing.
Letters can also be numbers; alef stands for 1.
In Israel Hebrew is the main language.

abschnitte.text: **Hebrew** is written **from right to left**. That is why a Hebrew book begins on the side that for us is the back. The alphabet has **22 letters**, fewer than the English one. Five letters have a special form when they stand at the end of a word. There are no capital and small letters.

The first letter is called **alef**. It is silent and has no sound of its own. After it comes **bet**. The word “alphabet” comes from the similar Greek letters alpha and beta. The last letter is called **tav** and is pronounced roughly like a T. The Greek and Hebrew scripts have a common ancestor: the script of the Phoenicians.

In Hebrew you usually write only the **consonants**, that is, letters such as B, M or S. The **vowels** such as A, E or O are missing. Anyone who knows the language still knows how a word sounds. In children’s books, prayer books and poems, the vowels are shown with small **dots and dashes** below or above the letters.

Hebrew letters can also be **numbers**. **Alef** stands for 1, bet for 2, and so on. This is how, for example, the years in the Jewish calendar are written. Because every word therefore also has a numerical value, scholars in the past searched for hidden meanings.

The **Torah** is written with these letters. For a long time Hebrew was above all a language for prayer and study. Today it is the main language of everyday life in **Israel**. There street signs, newspapers and mobile phones are also in Hebrew. Yiddish too is written with Hebrew letters.

gewusst: The usual Hebrew printed script is called square script, because many letters fit almost into a square.
In Hebrew the number 15 is not written in the usual way, because the sequence of letters would recall the name of God.

teile.einleitung: Isis was one of the most important goddesses in ancient Egypt. She was regarded as a loving mother, a protector and a great magician. Later she was even worshipped throughout the Roman Empire.
wichtigste: Isis was an important mother goddess of the ancient Egyptians.
Her husband was Osiris, the ruler of the realm of the dead.
Her son Horus is often shown with the head of a falcon.
On her head Isis often wears the sign for a throne.
She was famous for her magical power.
A great temple of Isis stands on the Nile island of Philae.

abschnitte.text: **Isis** was one of the most important goddesses of Egypt. In old pictures she often wears the sign for a **throne** on her head. Her name also means “throne” or “seat”. She was regarded as a loving mother and a protector. Many people prayed to her when they needed help.

Isis was married to the god **Osiris**. Their son is **Horus**, who is often shown with the head of a falcon. According to the myth, the wicked god **Seth** killed Osiris and scattered him. Isis gathered all the parts and brought Osiris back to life with her magical power. After that Osiris became the ruler of the realm of the dead.

Isis was especially famous for her **magical power**. People asked her for protection and healing, above all for children. On many figures you see Isis holding the little Horus on her lap. She was in this way an image of care and security.

On the Nile island of **Philae** in the south of Egypt stands a great temple of Isis. When a huge dam was built at Aswan, the island was threatened with sinking under the water. That is why the temple was moved stone by stone to a neighbouring island. Today visitors can marvel at it there.

The worship of Isis spread throughout the **Mediterranean region**. The Romans also built temples to her, for example in **Pompeii**. This temple survived under the ash of Vesuvius. In this way an Egyptian goddess also became known in Europe.

gewusst: The temple of Isis at Philae was moved stone by stone to another island.
Isis was worshipped not only in Egypt, but also by many Romans.

teile.einleitung: The Baha’i Gardens in Haifa are magnificent terraced gardens on Mount Carmel in Israel. In their middle stands the Shrine of the Bab with its golden dome. The gardens belong to the world centre of the Baha’is and to the UNESCO World Heritage.
wichtigste: The gardens lie in Haifa in the north of Israel.
They climb up Mount Carmel.
There are 19 terraces over a length of about one kilometre.
In the middle stands the tomb of the Bab with its golden dome.
The terraces were opened in May 2001.
Since 2008 the holy sites have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: **Haifa** is a port city in the north of **Israel**. Here is the world centre of the Baha’i religion. The gardens climb up **Mount Carmel**. From the top you can see across the city, the harbour and the **Mediterranean**. The carefully tended flower beds, paths and fountains are laid out in a very regular pattern.

The gardens consist of **19 terraces** and are about one kilometre long. The number 19 has a special meaning for the Baha’is. The Bab had 18 first followers, and with him that made 19. The Baha’i calendar also has 19 months. After about ten years of building, the terraces were opened in **May 2001**.

In the middle of the terraces stands the **Shrine of the Bab**. There lies the tomb of the **Bab**, the forerunner of the Baha’i religion. Its **golden dome** is one of the landmarks of Haifa. Many Baha’is visit the shrine as pilgrims. For the Baha’is it is the second holiest place after the tomb of Baha’u’llah.

Next to the gardens stands the seat of the **Universal House of Justice**. This is the highest elected body of the Baha’is, and its building on Carmel has been in use since 1983. In 2008, **UNESCO** added the holy sites of the Baha’is in Haifa and Western Galilee to the **World Heritage List**. Since the opening, very many people visit the gardens every year, whatever their religion.

gewusst: The Baha’i Gardens are among the most visited sights in Israel.
The 19 terraces recall the Bab and his 18 first followers.

teile.einleitung: The **Dragon Boat Festival** is one of the most important festivals in China. It takes place on the 5th day of the 5th month of the Chinese lunar calendar, usually in June. Famous are the races with long, colourful boats shaped like dragons.
wichtigste: The festival falls on the 5th day of the 5th lunar month.
It recalls the poet Qu Yuan.
People eat zongzi, parcels of sticky rice.
In the boats, a drum sets the beat.
The boats have a dragon’s head and a dragon’s tail.
Since 2009 the festival has been part of UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage.
