abschnitte.text: The festival recalls **Qu Yuan**, a poet and official from the ancient state of Chu. He lived over 2,000 years ago. He gave his king good advice, but was banished. Out of grief for his country, he threw himself into the **Miluo** river. The people went out in boats to search for him. They threw rice into the water so that the fish would spare his body.

The typical food is **zongzi**. These are parcels of **sticky rice** wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves and boiled. Depending on the region, they have a sweet or savoury filling, for example bean paste, dates or meat. They recall the rice that was once thrown into the river for Qu Yuan. Families often make them together.

The boats are long and narrow. At the front they have a **dragon’s head**, at the back a **dragon’s tail**. Many paddlers sit one behind the other. One person beats a **drum** and so sets the beat, so that everyone paddles at the same time. Today dragon boat racing is also a sport all over the world. Races take place on Swiss lakes too.

The festival falls in early summer, when it gets hot. In the past people believed that illness and misfortune threatened at this time. That is why many families hang **mugwort** and sweet flag on the door. Children often get small, fragrant pouches or coloured threads around the wrist. These customs are meant to keep misfortune away. In **2009**, **UNESCO** added the festival to the list of intangible cultural heritage.

gewusst: In Chinese the festival is called Duanwu.
A usual dragon boat in the sport has 20 paddlers, plus one person at the drum and one at the helm.

teile.einleitung: Israel is a state in the Middle East on the Mediterranean. It was founded in 1948 and sees itself as the homeland of the Jewish people. Its history is closely tied to Zionism and to many conflicts in the region.
wichtigste: The State of Israel was proclaimed in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948.
David Ben-Gurion read out the Declaration of Independence and became the first prime minister.
In 1949 Chaim Weizmann became the first president of the state.
In 1947 the UN decided on a partition plan for Palestine with Resolution 181.
The parliament is called the Knesset and has 120 seats.
The national anthem is called HaTikvah, “The Hope”.
Modern Hebrew is the official language of Israel.

abschnitte.text: The idea of a Jewish state is called **Zionism**. In 1897 the First Zionist Congress took place in **Basel**, led by Theodor Herzl. In 1917, Britain supported a “national home” for the Jewish people in Palestine in the **Balfour Declaration**. At the same time the rights of the non-Jewish population were to be preserved. Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour wrote a letter to Lord Rothschild about it.

In 1947 the UN General Assembly decided, with **Resolution 181**, on a plan to partition Palestine into a Jewish and an Arab state. Jerusalem was to receive an international status. The Jewish side agreed, the Arab side refused. On **14 May 1948**, **David Ben-Gurion** read out the Declaration of Independence in Tel Aviv. The next day neighbouring Arab states attacked, and war broke out.

Israel is a parliamentary democracy. The parliament is called the **Knesset** and has **120 seats**. The members are elected by pure proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency. The first head of government was Ben-Gurion, and in 1949 the chemist **Chaim Weizmann** became the first president of the state. The office of president is mainly ceremonial, and the government is led by the prime minister.

For a long time Hebrew was above all a language of prayer. **Eliezer Ben-Yehuda** consistently spoke Hebrew with his family and created a large dictionary with new words. He is regarded as the most important reviver of Hebrew as an everyday language. The national anthem is called **HaTikvah**, which means “The Hope”. It expresses the longing for a free people in its own land.

The **Law of Return** of 1950 gives Jews from all over the world the right to immigrate to Israel and become citizens. It also applies to children and grandchildren of Jews. Since the founding there have been conflicts with neighbouring Arab states and with the Palestinians. Borders, settlements and the status of Jerusalem are still disputed today. The positions of those involved are far apart.

gewusst: The First Zionist Congress took place in Basel in 1897.
The number of 120 seats in the Knesset goes back to the “Great Assembly” of antiquity.

teile.einleitung: Yiddish is the language that many Jews in Central and Eastern Europe spoke in everyday life for centuries. It is related to German and is written with Hebrew letters. Many Yiddish words are also known in German today.
wichtigste: Yiddish arose in the Middle Ages from German with many Hebrew words.
It is written with Hebrew letters from right to left.
Words such as Schlamassel, meschugge, Tacheles and Chuzpe come from Yiddish.
Before the Holocaust, over 10 million people spoke Yiddish.
Isaac Bashevis Singer received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1978.
In Aargau, Surbtal Yiddish was spoken until the 20th century.

abschnitte.titel: A language with its own script
abschnitte.text: **Yiddish** arose in the Middle Ages. It builds on German and contains many words from Hebrew and Aramaic, and later also from Slavic languages. It is written with the **Hebrew alphabet**, from right to left. Unlike in Hebrew, the vowels are usually written out. Speakers lovingly call their Yiddish **mame-loshn**, the “mother tongue”.

Many words came into German by way of Yiddish. **Schlamassel** means misfortune or a hopeless mess. **Meschugge** means crazy, and anyone who talks **Tacheles** says their opinion openly. **Chuzpe** refers to a mixture of cheekiness and nerve; in English it is known as chutzpah. The word goes back to Hebrew.

A rich literature arose in Yiddish. **Sholem Aleichem** wrote the stories of “Tevye the Dairyman”. The musical **“Fiddler on the Roof”**, which came out in 1964, is based on them. **Isaac Bashevis Singer** wrote his novels and stories in Yiddish. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in **1978**.

There was Yiddish in Switzerland too. In Aargau, Jewish families lived for a long time mainly in **Endingen and Lengnau** in the Surb valley. They spoke a form of Western Yiddish of their own, **Surbtal Yiddish**. When many families moved to the cities, this dialect died out in the 20th century.

Before the Second World War, Yiddish was the everyday language of about **11 to 13 million** people. In 1925 the **YIVO** was founded in Vilna, today Vilnius, a scholarly institute for Yiddish language and culture. Because of the war, it moved its seat to New York in 1940. The **Holocaust** destroyed the greater part of the language community. Today Yiddish is still spoken and cultivated in some Jewish communities.

gewusst: To this day Isaac Bashevis Singer is the only Nobel laureate who wrote in Yiddish.
The Hebrew of prayer is called loshn-koydesh in Yiddish, the “holy language”.

teile.einleitung: The **First Zionist Congress** took place in August 1897 in **Basel**. Jews from many countries met there to discuss a state of their own for the Jewish people. The congress is regarded as the beginning of the political Zionist movement.
wichtigste: Theodor Herzl convened and chaired the congress.
About 200 delegates took part.
At the congress the World Zionist Organization was founded.
Herzl’s pamphlet “The Jewish State” of 1896 prepared the congress.
Max Nordau gave the great speech on the situation of the Jews.
In 2022 a jubilee congress took place in Basel for the 125th anniversary.

abschnitte.text: **Theodor Herzl** was a journalist and writer from **Vienna**. He saw how Jews were attacked with hostility in many countries of Europe. In 1896 he published the pamphlet **“The Jewish State”**. In it he called for a state of their own for the Jews as an answer to **antisemitism**, that is, hostility towards Jews. To bring this idea about, he invited people to a congress.

The congress took place from 29 to 31 August 1897 in the **Stadtcasino Basel**. About **200 delegates** from many countries came, along with guests and journalists. Herzl was elected president. The doctor and writer **Max Nordau** gave an impressive speech on the plight of the Jews in East and West. He became one of Herzl’s most important allies.

The congress adopted the **Basel Programme**. It called for a **homeland in Palestine** for the Jewish people, secured by public law. To reach this goal, the **World Zionist Organization** was founded. It was to raise money, promote immigration and negotiate with governments. In 1948 the State of **Israel** was founded, more than 50 years after the congress.

Basel afterwards hosted Zionist congresses several more times. At the fifth congress in 1901, a famous photo was taken on the balcony of the **Drei Könige** hotel: Herzl looks out over the **Rhine**. It became a well-known image of the Zionist movement. In August **2022**, a jubilee congress in Basel recalled the **125th anniversary**. Because of the security situation, it took place under heavy police protection.

gewusst: The congress was actually meant to take place in Munich, but the Jewish community there was against it.
Herzl did not live to see the founding of Israel; he died as early as 1904.

t1gp69q1.t: Federal Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer

teile.einleitung: The **Federal Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer** is a special public holiday in Switzerland. In most cantons it takes place on the **third Sunday in September**. It is not meant for one religion only, but for all people in the country.
wichtigste: In most cantons the day falls on the third Sunday in September.
Its full name is Day of Thanksgiving, Repentance and Prayer.
People give thanks and pray, traditionally also for the whole country.
The day is meant for all faiths.
Many families eat a plum tart.
Geneva celebrates its own day of fasting on a Thursday.

abschnitte.titel: A day for the whole of Switzerland
abschnitte.text: The word **federal** means: for the whole of Switzerland. Even in earlier times, the places of the Confederation called for days of prayer in hard times. Since the 19th century the cantons have celebrated the day together on the same Sunday. The day was meant to unite people of different denominations and languages. That is why it is still a holiday fixed by the state and not by a single church.

The full name says what it is about. People **give thanks** for the good in their own lives and in the country. **Repenting** means thinking about one’s own mistakes and wanting to do better. And people **pray**, for example for peace and unity. In many churches there are services, and often different religions celebrate together. Some cantonal governments publish a **day-of-prayer proclamation** for the occasion, a message to the population.

In the past the day of prayer was a day of fasting on which people ate simply. That is how the **plum tart** came to the table. In September the plums are ripe, and the tart could be baked the day before. So nobody had to cook for long on the holiday. The custom lives on in many families today.

The canton of **Geneva** celebrates its own day, the **Jeûne genevois**. It falls on the Thursday after the first Sunday in September. In the canton of **Vaud**, the Monday after the day of prayer is a holiday. Around the time of the day of prayer, **autumn** also begins: around 22 or 23 September, day and night are almost equally long.

gewusst: The day of prayer is one of the few holidays in Switzerland meant for all religions at once.
In Geneva the Jeûne genevois is an official holiday on which many shops are closed.

teile.einleitung: An interreligious calendar shows the holidays of many religions at a glance. In this way you know when friends or classmates are celebrating something. Because religions use different calendars, some festivals move from year to year.
wichtigste: An interreligious calendar shows the holidays of many religions.
The Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar with about 354 days.
That is why Ramadan moves forward by about eleven days every year.
The Jewish calendar adds seven leap months in 19 years.
Many Orthodox churches celebrate Christmas on 7 January.
Easter is the first Sunday after the first full moon of spring.
The Baha’i calendar has 19 months of 19 days each.

abschnitte.text: The **Islamic calendar** is a pure **lunar calendar**. It has twelve months with about **354 days** altogether. That is about eleven days fewer than a solar year. Because it has no leap months, **Ramadan** moves forward by about eleven days every year. In this way the month of fasting travels through all the seasons over the years.

The **Jewish calendar** follows both the moon and the sun. Such a calendar is called a **lunisolar calendar**. So that the festivals stay in their season, **seven leap years** are inserted in **19 years**. They have an extra month of Adar. In this way Passover always stays in spring. Years are counted from the traditionally calculated creation of the world: with **Rosh Hashanah** in September 2025, the year **5786** began.

Many Orthodox churches celebrate **Christmas on 7 January**. They follow the **Julian calendar**, which at present lies 13 days behind our Gregorian calendar. So 25 December in the Julian calendar corresponds to 7 January. **Easter** has been celebrated since the Council of Nicaea on the first Sunday after the first full moon from the start of spring. That is why in the West Easter falls between 22 March and 25 April.

The calendar of the **Baha’is** is called the Badi calendar. It has **19 months of 19 days each**, that is, 361 days, plus four or five inserted days. The New Year, **Naw-Ruz**, falls on the start of spring. The Buddhist **Vesak festival** follows the **full moon** and usually falls in May. It recalls the birth, enlightenment and death of the Buddha.

In Switzerland people of many religions live together. An interreligious calendar helps schools, firms and societies to show consideration. For example, you do not plan an exam on a high holiday. Various organisations publish such calendars every year.

gewusst: A Muslim experiences Ramadan in all four seasons in the course of their life.
The Islamic count of years begins with Muhammad’s migration to Medina in the year 622.

teile.einleitung: The **druids** were the priests of the **Celts**. But they were responsible not only for the gods; they were also teachers, judges and scholars. Celts who knew druids also lived in the area of present-day Switzerland.
wichtigste: The druids were priests of the Celts.
The oak was especially sacred to them.
In disputes the druids gave judgement.
Julius Caesar wrote about the druids.
The Celtic Helvetii lived in the area of present-day Switzerland.
The site of La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel gave its name to a Celtic period.

abschnitte.text: The druids led the sacrificial ceremonies for the gods. They knew about the stars, the calendar and healing plants. In disputes among the Celts, they **gave judgement**. Young people learned from them. Especially sacred to them was the **oak**. The Roman Pliny relates that they cut **mistletoe** from oaks.

Several Celtic peoples lived in the area of present-day Switzerland. The best known are the **Helvetii**. From them comes the Latin name of Switzerland, **Helvetia**. The abbreviation CH on cars stands for Confoederatio Helvetica. On **Lake Neuchâtel** lies the site of **La Tène**. There, in the 19th century, many Celtic weapons and pieces of jewellery were found. The later Iron Age is named after the place, the **La Tène period**.

The druids did not write their knowledge down. That is why we know about them mainly from texts by Greeks and Romans. The most famous account comes from **Julius Caesar**, who had conquered Gaul. The Romans later pushed the druids back. Many present-day pictures of druids, for example in comics, are therefore more fantasy than history.

The Celts celebrated several great festivals in the year. One of them was **Samhain** at the beginning of November. It marked the start of the dark season. People believed that on this night the world of the living and that of the dead were especially close. Samhain is regarded as one origin of **Halloween**.

gewusst: The potion brewer Getafix from the Asterix comics is an invented druid.
The word druid is probably connected with a Celtic word for oak and for knowledge.

teile.einleitung: **Akhenaten** was a pharaoh in ancient Egypt who ruled around 1350 BC. He wanted people to worship above all a single god: the sun disc **Aten**. In doing so he turned the religion of his country upside down.
wichtigste: Akhenaten worshipped Aten as the only god.
Aten was shown as a sun disc with rays ending in hands.
At the start he ruled under the name Amenhotep IV.
His new capital lay near present-day Amarna.
His chief wife was Nefertiti.
Tutankhamun was probably his son.
Akhenaten belonged to the 18th Dynasty.

abschnitte.text: Akhenaten came to the throne as **Amenhotep IV**. He belonged to the **18th Dynasty**. Soon he placed the sun god **Aten** above all other gods. Aten was not shown as a human or an animal, but as a **sun disc**. Rays go out from it, ending in small **hands**. They hold the sign of life out to the king and his family. The king now called himself Akhenaten, which means roughly “he who is useful to Aten”.

Until then **Amun** in Thebes had been the most powerful god of Egypt. His priests had great wealth and much influence. Akhenaten had the **cult of Amun** attacked. His name was **chiselled out** at many temples. Other gods also lost importance. Because Akhenaten allowed almost only one god to count, some researchers speak of an early belief in one god.

In the middle of Egypt, Akhenaten built a new capital. It was called **Akhetaten**, “Horizon of Aten”. Today the place is called **Amarna**. There a new artistic style arose, **Amarna art**. In it the royal family is often shown in everyday life, for example playing with the children. In Amarna, clay tablets with letters to rulers of other countries were also found.

Akhenaten’s chief wife was **Nefertiti**. Her painted bust was found in Amarna in 1912 and today stands in **Berlin**. It is one of the most famous works of art in the world. After Akhenaten’s death, the young **Tutankhamun** soon came to the throne, probably a son of Akhenaten. Under him Egypt returned to Amun and the old gods. Amarna was abandoned, and later kings tried to wipe Akhenaten out of history.

From Akhenaten’s time comes the **Great Hymn to the Aten**. The song praises the sun as the creator of all life. It describes how people, animals and plants wake in the morning when Aten rises. The text was found in a tomb in Amarna. Researchers have often compared it with **Psalm 104** of the Bible, which uses similar images.

gewusst: Tutankhamun was first called Tutankhaten and changed his name when the cult of Amun returned.
In later lists of kings, Akhenaten was simply left out.

teile.einleitung: Freedom of belief and conscience is a fundamental right in Switzerland. It is set out in Article 15 of the Federal Constitution. Everyone may freely choose and practise their religion, or have no religion at all.
wichtigste: Freedom of belief and conscience is in Article 15 of the Federal Constitution.
Nobody may be forced to belong to a religion or to take part in religious instruction.
From the age of 16, a child decides for themselves on their religious affiliation.
The state may restrict the fundamental right only on a legal basis and proportionately.
In the past there were denominational exceptional articles, such as the ban on the Jesuits.
In 2009 and 2021 the people accepted provisions on building minarets and on face coverings.

abschnitte.text: **Article 15** of the Federal Constitution guarantees freedom of belief and conscience. Every person may freely choose their religion and practise it alone or with others. Paragraph 4 states that **nobody may be forced** to join a religious community, to perform a religious act or to follow religious instruction. This is called **negative freedom of religion**. Under **Article 36**, the state may restrict a fundamental right only if there is a **legal basis** and a public interest and the restriction is **proportionate**.

Under Article 303 of the **Civil Code**, a child decides on their religious affiliation from the age of **16**. This is called **religious majority**. In most cantons, parents can apply for time off for high religious **holidays**, and the child may then stay at home. In 2017 the **European Court of Human Rights** ruled in the case of Osmanoğlu and Kocabaş on parents from Basel. They wanted to have their daughters excused from mixed **swimming lessons**. The court saw no violation of freedom of religion in the requirement, because integration into school outweighed it.

The Federal Constitution of **1848** granted free settlement and freedom of worship only to Christians. **Jews** received free settlement only in **1866** through a popular vote, and full freedom of belief with the constitution of 1874. From the time of the Kulturkampf there were also **denominational exceptional articles**. The people struck out the **ban on the Jesuits** and the ban on new monasteries in **1973**. The last to fall, in **2001**, was the **diocese article**, which tied new dioceses to the approval of the Confederation.

On 29 November **2009**, about 57.5 per cent of voters accepted the **minaret initiative**. Since then Article 72 of the Federal Constitution has stated that building minarets is forbidden. On 7 March **2021**, about 51.2 per cent accepted the initiative for a **ban on face coverings** in public spaces. The debate centred strongly on the burqa and niqab. Supporters saw in it a protection of public order, while opponents criticised a restriction of freedom of religion.

gewusst: In Switzerland it is mainly the cantons that regulate the relationship between the state and religious communities.
Freedom of conscience also protects people who do not believe in God at all.

teile.einleitung: The Celts lived more than 2,000 years ago in large parts of Europe, including the area of present-day Switzerland. They worshipped many gods and goddesses of nature. Because they wrote little themselves, we know their beliefs mainly from finds and from reports by Greeks and Romans.
wichtigste: The Celts lived in many parts of Europe, and the Helvetii were Celts too.
Their priests were called druids.
Cernunnos is usually shown with antlers.
Epona was the goddess of horses and riders.
Taranis was the god of thunder and is often shown with a wheel.
The La Tène period is named after the site of La Tène on Lake Neuchâtel.

abschnitte.text: The priests of the Celts were called **druids**. They were judges and teachers as well. They passed on their knowledge **by word of mouth**, which is why there are hardly any Celtic writings about their beliefs. The Roman Pliny reported that druids cut **mistletoe** from sacred trees. What we know often comes from such reports by outsiders.

One well-known god is **Cernunnos**. He is usually shown with **antlers** and is regarded as lord of the animals and of nature. A famous picture of him appears on the **Gundestrup Cauldron**, a decorated silver cauldron from Denmark. The goddess **Epona** protected **horses** and riders. Later even Roman cavalry soldiers worshipped her.

**Taranis** was the god of **thunder**. He is often shown with a **wheel**, which probably stands for the sky or the sun. **Lugus** was an important god of many skills. The old name of the city of Lyon, **Lugdunum**, is often explained as “fortress of Lugus”. This explanation is not entirely certain, however.

A very important site lies in Switzerland: **La Tène** on Lake Neuchâtel. There many weapons, pieces of jewellery and tools were found. They were probably laid in the water as **offerings** to the gods. A whole period of Celtic culture, the later Iron Age, is named after this place: the **La Tène period**. The **Helvetii**, who lived on the Swiss Plateau, were Celts too.

gewusst: A whole period of European history is named after a place on Lake Neuchâtel.
The druid Getafix from the Asterix comics cuts his mistletoe with a golden sickle, as Pliny reported of the druids.

teile.einleitung: The Five Ks are five articles of faith of the Sikhs. Initiated Sikhs wear them every day as a visible sign of their faith. In Punjabi their names all begin with the sound K.
wichtigste: In Punjabi the Five Ks are called “Panj Kakar”.
Kesh means uncut hair.
The kangha is a small wooden comb.
The kara is a bangle of steel or iron.
The kirpan is a small sword.
Many Sikh men cover their long hair with a turban.

abschnitte.text: **Sikhism** arose about 500 years ago in the Punjab, a region in the north of India and in Pakistan. Anyone who is initiated into the community of the **Khalsa** commits to wearing the **Five Ks**. In Punjabi they are called **Panj Kakar**. The name comes from the fact that all five signs begin with the sound K. The rule goes back to the tenth guru, **Guru Gobind Singh**.

**Kesh** means uncut hair. Many Sikhs let their hair and beard grow, because they see the body as a gift from God. To keep the long hair tidy, they wear the **kangha**, a small wooden comb. It stands for **cleanliness** and order. Many Sikh men cover their hair with a **turban**, which in Punjabi is called a **dastar**.

The **kara** is a plain bangle of steel or iron. It is usually worn on the right wrist. Its round shape has no beginning and no end. That is why it recalls **God**, who is eternal. The kara is also meant to remind the wearer to do only good with their own hands.

The **kirpan** is a small sword or dagger. It recalls the duty to **protect the weak** and to stand up for justice. It is a religious sign and not a weapon for everyday use. The fifth K is the **kachera**, a short pair of cotton trousers worn under the clothing. It stands for decency and self-control.

gewusst: In some countries there are special rules on how Sikhs may carry the kirpan, for example on aeroplanes or in schools.
Many Sikh women also wear the Five Ks, and some of them wear a turban too.

teile.einleitung: The Ise Shrine in Japan is the most important sanctuary of Shinto. It is dedicated to the sun goddess Amaterasu. What is special is that its main buildings are completely rebuilt every 20 years.
wichtigste: The Ise Shrine lies in the city of Ise in Mie Prefecture in Japan.
In Japanese it is called Ise Jingu and is the most important sanctuary of Shinto.
The Inner Shrine is dedicated to the sun goddess Amaterasu.
The Outer Shrine honours Toyouke, the goddess of food.
The main buildings are rebuilt every 20 years, most recently in 2013.
They are built with the pale wood of the hinoki cypress.
The complex includes about 125 shrines in all.

abschnitte.text: The **Ise Shrine**, in Japanese Ise Jingu, lies in the city of Ise in Mie Prefecture. It is regarded as the most important sanctuary of **Shinto**, the ancient religion of Japan. In Shinto people worship divine beings called kami. Every year very many pilgrims come to Ise. The shrine lies in a large forest.

The complex has two main parts. The **Inner Shrine** (Naiku) is dedicated to the sun goddess **Amaterasu**. The **Outer Shrine** (Geku) honours Toyouke, the goddess of food. Besides these two, many smaller shrines belong to it. In all there are about **125 shrines** in the area around Ise.

In the Inner Shrine the sacred mirror **Yata no Kagami** is said to be kept. It is regarded as the seat of the sun goddess. Nobody may look at it. The mirror is one of the three imperial regalia of Japan, together with a sword and a jewel. Regalia are special signs of the emperor’s rule.

For over 1,300 years the main buildings have been rebuilt every **20 years**, on a site right next to the old one. This renewal is called **Shikinen Sengu**. The last one, the 62nd, took place in **2013**, and the next is planned for 2033. In this way knowledge of the old craftsmanship stays alive, because each generation learns the work itself.

The buildings are made of the pale wood of the Japanese cypress, the **hinoki**. They are built in a very old style and are not painted. The plain forms look calm and natural. It is precisely this simplicity that makes the shrine so beautiful for many people.

gewusst: Because it is rebuilt again and again, the buildings are at once ancient in style and almost new.
Nobody may look at the sacred mirror of Ise.

teile.einleitung: Angkor Wat is a huge temple complex in Cambodia. It was built almost 900 years ago by the Khmer people and is regarded as the largest religious building in the world.
wichtigste: Angkor Wat lies in north-western Cambodia, near the town of Siem Reap.
The Khmer built the temple in the first half of the 12th century.
The builder was King Suryavarman II.
A wide moat surrounds the whole complex.
The towers represent the sacred world mountain, Meru.
Almost 1,800 figures of heavenly dancers can be seen on the walls.
Angkor Wat is regarded as the largest religious building in the world.

abschnitte.text: Angkor was the capital of the **Khmer Empire**. From the 9th to the 15th century this empire ruled large parts of South-East Asia. In the area around Angkor there are many temples, and Angkor Wat is the best known. The name means roughly “City of the Temple”. It was built under King **Suryavarman II** in the first half of the 12th century.

Angkor Wat is built like a model of the universe. The five towers in the middle stand for the peaks of **Meru**. This is the mythical world mountain in Hinduism and Buddhism. The main tower in the centre is the tallest. The surrounding walls represent the mountain ranges at the edge of the world.

A **moat** about 190 metres wide surrounds the whole complex. It stands for the world ocean that encircles the world. A long stone causeway leads to the temple. With its moat, walls and courtyards, Angkor Wat covers a huge area. That is why the complex is regarded as the **largest sacred building** in the world, that is, the largest religious building.

The walls are richly decorated with pictures in stone. Almost 1,800 figures show **apsaras** and **devatas**. These are heavenly dancers and goddesses. Long reliefs tell stories from the Indian epics. They also show gods, kings and scenes from life at court.

abschnitte.titel: From Hindu temple to Buddhist site
abschnitte.text: Originally Angkor Wat was dedicated to the Hindu god **Vishnu**. Later the temple was used by Buddhists, and it still is today. Angkor Wat is a landmark of Cambodia and is even shown on the national flag. The temples of Angkor are a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and are visited by very many people.

gewusst: Angkor Wat is shown on the flag of Cambodia.
The moat around the temple is about 190 metres wide, almost twice as wide as a football pitch is long.

teile.einleitung: A bindi is a small dot on the forehead. It is especially common in India and is worn by many Hindu women and girls. Today the bindi is often simply a piece of jewellery.
wichtigste: The bindi is worn on the forehead, between the eyebrows.
The word bindi means dot or drop.
Traditionally the bindi is red.
In the past it was painted on with a red powder called kumkum.
For many women, a red bindi shows that they are married.
Today bindis come as sticky dots in many colours, often with glitter.

abschnitte.text: A **bindi** is a dot that is placed at the front of the **forehead**, usually between the eyebrows. The word comes from **Sanskrit**, an ancient language of India. It means **dot** or **drop**. You can see the bindi clearly when you look at someone from the front.

Traditionally the bindi is **red**. In the past it was painted on with **kumkum**. This is a red powder that is also used at religious ceremonies in the temple. In India, red is regarded as the colour of joy and good fortune.

For many Hindu women, a red bindi shows that they are **married**. A bride receives a red bindi at the wedding. After that, many married women go on wearing it. But mainly **women and girls** wear a bindi, including unmarried ones.

Today the bindi is often simply a pretty piece of **jewellery**. Instead of painting it on, you can buy little **sticky dots**. They come in many colours and shapes, often with glitter or tiny stones. Many women choose a colour that goes with their clothes. In Switzerland too, you can see bindis at festivals of the Indian and Tamil communities.

gewusst: Bindis are not only round: some have the shape of drops, stars or small patterns.
Indian actresses in films often wear striking bindis too, to match their dress.

teile.einleitung: Atman is an important concept from Hinduism. It refers to the innermost, unchanging self of a person. According to the Upanishads, the Atman is at its core one with Brahman, the divine ground of the world.
wichtigste: Atman is the innermost self of a person.
It lies behind body, thoughts and feelings.
Atman is often translated as “soul”.
“Aham brahmasmi” means “I am Brahman”.
Karma binds the Atman to the cycle of rebirths.
The goal is liberation, called moksha.

abschnitte.text: The word **Atman** comes from Sanskrit and originally means breath or self. It refers to the unchanging core of a person. It lies behind the body, the thoughts and the feelings. Atman is often translated as “soul”. More exactly, though, it means the pure **core of consciousness**, which does not change.

The **Katha Upanishad** explains the Atman with an image. The body is a chariot. The intellect, called **buddhi**, is the charioteer, the thinking mind (**manas**) is the reins, and the senses are the horses. The Atman rides along as the master in the chariot. Anyone who steers his chariot well reaches the goal.

The **Upanishads** are old philosophical texts of India. They teach that the Atman is, in its innermost being, one with **Brahman**, the divine ground of everything. The sentence **“Aham brahmasmi”** from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad means “I am Brahman”. It is one of the four **mahavakyas**, the great sayings. Another is “Tat tvam asi”, which means “That is you”.

According to Hindu teaching, actions leave effects, called **karma**. This karma determines a new birth. As long as karma and ignorance remain, the self stays in the cycle of rebirths, called **samsara**. Anyone who recognises who they really are can be freed from it. This liberation is called **moksha**. Buddhism, by contrast, teaches that there is no fixed self.

gewusst: The word Atman is related to the German word “atmen”, meaning “to breathe”.
In Buddhism there is the opposite teaching, “anatta”, which means “non-self”.

teile.einleitung: Candomblé is an Afro-Brazilian religion. It arose in the 19th century among enslaved Africans in Brazil and is especially widespread in the state of Bahia.
wichtigste: Candomblé is mainly found in Brazil, and its centre is Salvador da Bahia.
The deities are called orixás and come from the religion of the Yoruba.
The place of worship of a community is called a terreiro.
A leading priestess is called a mãe de santo or ialorixá.
On 2 February, thousands in Salvador honour the sea goddess Iemanjá.
The largest nation is Ketu, which is based on Yoruba traditions.

abschnitte.text: **Candomblé** arose in the **19th century** in **Brazil**. People who had been abducted from Africa and enslaved brought their faith with them. They preserved it despite bans. **Salvador da Bahia** is regarded as its centre. Today Candomblé has followers all over Brazil.

In Candomblé people worship **orixás**. These deities come from the religion of the **Yoruba** in West Africa. They embody forces of nature and areas of life. **Iemanjá** is regarded as the mother of the waters and queen of the sea. **Oxalá** is the orixá of creation. At festivals there is dancing, drumming and singing.

A community meets in a **terreiro**. This includes a house of worship, shrines and grounds for festivals and initiations. Several historic terreiros in Salvador are **protected as heritage sites**. A house is led by a **mãe de santo**, also called an **ialorixá**. Her male counterpart is called a **pai de santo**.

Because African religions were persecuted for a long time, believers linked the orixás with Catholic saints. In Salvador, **Oxalá** is identified with the **Senhor do Bonfim**, that is, Jesus. At the “**Lavagem do Bonfim**”, women in white robes wash the steps of the church. On **2 February**, thousands walk to the sea in the district of Rio Vermelho with flowers to honour **Iemanjá**.

Candomblé is divided into so-called **nations**. They go back to different African peoples. **Ketu** comes from the Yoruba and is the largest branch. **Jeje** goes back to the Fon, **Angola** to Bantu peoples. The nations differ in language, songs and rhythms.

gewusst: The offerings for Iemanjá are taken out to sea in boats and placed in the water there.
The drums in Candomblé are regarded as sacred and have names of their own.

teile.einleitung: Caodaism is a religion from Vietnam that was founded in 1926. It combines elements from Buddhism, Daoism, Confucianism and Christianity into a new teaching.
wichtigste: Caodaism was officially founded in southern Vietnam in 1926.
The most important symbol is the divine eye.
The full name means roughly “Great Way of the Third Universal Salvation”.
The Holy See with the great temple is in Tay Ninh.
Yellow stands for Buddhism, blue for Daoism, red for Confucianism.
The hierarchy is modelled on that of the Catholic Church.

abschnitte.text: **Caodaism** was officially founded in **southern Vietnam** in **1926**. At that time the area belonged to the French colony of **Cochinchina**. According to the founders, they received their messages in **spiritist sessions**, also called séances. Spirits and God himself are said to have spoken in them. Such sessions still play a role today.

The most important symbol is the **divine eye**. It reminds believers that God sees everything. It is often shown above a globe or in a triangle. The full name of the religion in Vietnamese is **Dai Dao Tam Ky Pho Do**. Roughly, this means “Great Way of the Third Universal Salvation”. According to the teaching, Caodaism is God’s third great revelation to humankind.

Caodaism wants to unite different religions. Three teachings are represented by colours: **yellow** stands for **Buddhism**, **blue** for **Daoism** and **red** for **Confucianism**. The robes of the dignitaries show these three branches. Jesus and other well-known figures are also revered.

The **Holy See** of Caodaism is in **Tay Ninh**, north-west of Ho Chi Minh City. The great temple is very colourful and a well-known destination for visitors. The **hierarchy** is modelled on that of the **Catholic Church**: there is a pope, cardinals, archbishops, bishops and priests. This shows the French Catholic influence of the colonial period.

gewusst: Among the saints revered in Caodaism is the French writer Victor Hugo.
In the temple at Tay Ninh, several times of prayer take place every day, which visitors can watch from a gallery.

teile.einleitung: Halal is an Arabic word and means “permitted”. In Islam it refers to everything that is permitted under the religious rules, especially in food. The opposite is called haram, that is, forbidden.
wichtigste: Halal means “permitted”.
Haram means “forbidden”.
For devout Muslims, pork and alcohol are haram.
Meat counts as halal only if the animal was slaughtered according to certain rules.
In Switzerland there are many shops and restaurants with halal products.

abschnitte.text: In Islam there are rules about what Muslims may eat and drink. What is permitted is called **halal**. What is forbidden is called **haram**. These rules come from the **Qur’an** and from the tradition about the Prophet Muhammad. Vegetables, fruit, grain, fish and many other foods are halal. **Pork** and **alcohol**, by contrast, are haram.

For meat to be halal, the animal must be slaughtered in a certain way. A prayer is often said as this is done. In Switzerland, slaughtering mammals without prior stunning has been forbidden since 1893. A lot of halal meat is therefore imported from other countries. Some Muslims also accept meat from stunned animals as halal, others do not.

Many products carry a **halal mark** on the packaging. In this way Muslims can quickly see what they may eat. Even gummy bears can be haram if they contain gelatine from pigs. In many Swiss towns there are butchers, shops and restaurants with halal offerings. Judaism also has similar food rules; there permitted food is called **kosher**.

gewusst: The ban on slaughter without stunning of 1893 was the very first popular initiative to be accepted in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Guru Nanak is the founder of Sikhism. He lived in the 15th and 16th centuries in the Punjab region. He taught that there is only one God and that all people are of equal worth.
wichtigste: Guru Nanak founded Sikhism.
He was born in 1469 in Talwandi, which is now called Nankana Sahib and lies in Pakistan.
He taught that there is only one God.
For him all people were of equal worth.
Nine more gurus followed him, ten in all.
The word “Sikh” means pupil.

abschnitte.text: **Guru Nanak** was born in 1469 in **Talwandi**. The place is now called **Nankana Sahib** and lies in **Pakistan**, in the Punjab region. He grew up in a Hindu family, but also got to know Islam. Even as a child he is said to have asked many questions about God and the world. He died in 1539 in Kartarpur.

Guru Nanak taught that there is only **one God**. This God is everywhere and has no form. This is an important foundation of **Sikhism**. He also taught that **all people are of equal worth**. Origin, caste and wealth should play no part. What matters are an honest life, hard work and sharing with others.

For many years Guru Nanak travelled on foot through India and other regions. On the way he spoke with people of different religions. He summed up his teaching in songs. Many of them are today in the holy book of the Sikhs, the **Guru Granth Sahib**.

Guru Nanak was followed by **nine more gurus**. So there were **ten human gurus** in all. The last, Guru Gobind Singh, declared the holy book the eternal guru. The followers are called **Sikhs**. The word comes from a word for “to learn” and means pupil or learner.

gewusst: Sikhs all over the world celebrate Guru Nanak’s birthday, usually in November.
Many pilgrims travel to Nankana Sahib, although most Sikhs today live in India.

teile.einleitung: The Haskalah was the Jewish Enlightenment of the 18th and 19th centuries. It wanted to familiarise Jews with secular education, science and the language of their country, without giving up Jewish tradition.
wichtigste: Haskalah means Enlightenment.
The word comes from “sechel”, reason.
The followers were called maskilim, the educated ones.
The movement began in the 18th century, above all in Berlin.
From 1783 the journal Ha-Meassef appeared in Königsberg.

abschnitte.text: In the 18th century the **Enlightenment** arose in Europe. People were to use their own reason. Among Jews too there was such a movement, the **Haskalah**. The word comes from the Hebrew “sechel”, reason. At that time many Jews lived apart and learned mainly religious texts. The Haskalah wanted to bring them subjects such as mathematics, natural science and the **language of the country** as well.

The followers of the Haskalah were called **maskilim**, which means roughly “the educated ones”. They founded modern schools and promoted science. At the same time they cultivated the **Hebrew language** and wrote poems and non-fiction in it. An important thinker was **Moses Mendelssohn** in Berlin. He translated the Torah into German, written in Hebrew letters.

From 1783 the Hebrew journal **Ha-Meassef** appeared in Königsberg. The name means “The Collector”. It published poems, scientific texts and Bible interpretations in Hebrew and became the mouthpiece of the Haskalah. Later the movement spread as far as Eastern Europe. It helped Jews in many countries gradually receive equal rights.

gewusst: The Haskalah helped to make Hebrew a modern language again for books and newspapers.
In Switzerland, Jews received the right to settle freely in 1866.

teile.einleitung: The **Edda** is the most important source for the gods and heroes of the Norse sagas. The name refers to two different works from **Iceland**: the **Poetic Edda** with old poems and the **Prose Edda** by Snorri Sturluson. Both come from the 13th century.
wichtigste: There are the Poetic Edda and the Prose Edda.
Most of the Poetic Edda is in the Codex Regius from the 13th century.
Around 1220, Snorri Sturluson wrote the Prose Edda as a textbook of poetry.
The first poem of the Poetic Edda is called Völuspá.
In 1971 Denmark returned the Codex Regius to Iceland.

abschnitte.text: The **Poetic Edda** is a collection of poems about gods such as **Odin**, **Thor** and **Loki** and about heroes such as Sigurd. The poems are older than the manuscript and were passed on orally for a long time. Most of it survives in the **Codex Regius**, a small manuscript from the 13th century. The first poem is the **Völuspá**, the “Prophecy of the Seeress”. In it a seeress tells of the creation of the world and of its end, **Ragnarök**.

The **Prose Edda** was written around 1220 by the Icelandic scholar and politician **Snorri Sturluson**. It is a **textbook for poets**. At that time poets used many images from the old tales of the gods, and Snorri wanted to explain them. That is why he retells the myths in prose, that is, in ordinary language instead of verse. Without his work we would know much less about the Norse gods.

In the 17th century an Icelandic bishop gave the Codex Regius to the king of **Denmark**, which then ruled over Iceland. That is why it lay in Copenhagen for a long time. After independence, Iceland wished to have its old manuscripts back. In **1971** Denmark brought the Codex Regius to Iceland. Many people celebrated its arrival in Reykjavik.

gewusst: The days of the week also recall Norse gods: Thursday is named after Thunor or Thor.
The world ash tree Yggdrasil, which connects all worlds, appears in the Völuspá.

teile.einleitung: Thailand is one of the countries with the highest share of Buddhists. There, Buddhism shapes everyday life, festivals and the look of the towns with their many monasteries and golden temples.
wichtigste: Over 90 per cent of people in Thailand are Buddhists, mostly of the Theravada school.
Fully ordained monks follow 227 rules, novices ten.
Early in the morning, monks go on an alms round and receive food.
Monks eat only between sunrise and noon.
A Buddhist monastery with a temple is called a wat.
In Wat Phra Kaeo in Bangkok, the Emerald Buddha is worshipped.

abschnitte.text: In Thailand, **Theravada** is the dominant school of Buddhism. Theravada means “teaching of the elders”. Over **90 per cent** of people describe themselves as Buddhists. The religion is closely linked with the royal family and with everyday life. Almost every village has a monastery of its own.

In Theravada, fully ordained monks follow **227 rules**, which are set out in the **Patimokkha**. Novices follow only ten rules. Early in the morning the monks go **barefoot** on their **alms round**. Believers put rice and other food into their bowls and so earn religious **merit**. Eating is only allowed between sunrise and **noon**; after that only drinks are permitted.

For many young men in Thailand it is usual to live for a time as a **monk**. This may be a few weeks or months. It is seen as an **honour** for the family. During the rainy season there is the retreat of **Vassa**: for about **three months** the monks stay in one place and devote themselves to study and meditation.

In Thailand a Buddhist monastery is called a **wat**. It includes temples, living quarters for monks and often a school. The most important sanctuary in the country is the **Emerald Buddha** in **Wat Phra Kaeo** in Bangkok. Despite its name, it is not made of emerald, but is a small green figure made of **jade**.

According to their rules, monks may **not touch a woman**. That is why women avoid touching a monk. They often hand over gifts by means of a cloth or simply put them down. Visitors take off their shoes in the temple and wear clothing that covers their shoulders and knees.

gewusst: The Emerald Buddha receives a new robe three times a year, to suit the season.
In Gretzenbach in the canton of Solothurn stands the Wat Srinagarindravararam, a large Thai monastery in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The **Enuma Elish** is the creation epic of the **Babylonians**. It tells how the gods arose from the primeval waters and how the god **Marduk** became king of the gods. The work survives in the Akkadian language on clay tablets in cuneiform.
wichtigste: The opening words “Enuma elish” mean “When above”.
The epic survives on seven clay tablets.
Tiamat embodies the salt sea water, Apsu the fresh water beneath the earth.
Marduk rises to become king of the gods.
From the body of Tiamat, Marduk forms heaven and earth.
Ea creates human beings from the blood of the god Kingu.
The epic was recited at the New Year festival Akitu in Babylon.

abschnitte.text: The epic begins with the words **“Enuma elish”**, which mean **“When above”**. At that time there was as yet no heaven and no earth. There were only two primeval waters: **Apsu**, the **fresh water** beneath the earth, and **Tiamat**, the **salt sea**. From their mingling the first gods arose. The young gods were noisy and disturbed Apsu.

The wise god **Ea** defeated Apsu. Tiamat then wanted revenge and created an army of monsters. At its head she placed the god **Kingu**. The other gods were afraid. Only **Marduk**, the son of Ea, was ready to fight. In return he demanded to become king of the gods. With winds and arrows he defeated Tiamat.

After his victory Marduk divided the body of Tiamat into two halves. From one he formed the **sky**, from the other the **earth**. He arranged the stars, the moon and the calendar. Then Kingu was punished. From his **blood** Ea created **human beings**. Their task was to serve the gods so that the gods could rest.

The Enuma Elish survives on **seven clay tablets**. It celebrates Marduk, the city god of **Babylon**, and with him the power of the city. It was recited in the temple at the great **New Year festival Akitu** in spring. Many tablets were found in the 19th century in the library of the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal in **Nineveh**. Since then researchers have often compared it with the creation story of the Bible.

gewusst: At the end of the epic, Marduk receives 50 honorary names.
Babylon lay in present-day Iraq, south of Baghdad.

teile.einleitung: infoSekta is a specialist agency in Zurich that provides information about sects and other group-like movements that take people over. It advises people who have questions or worries about such a group. In doing so it works independently of churches and religious communities.
wichtigste: infoSekta was founded in Zurich in 1990.
The founding took place under the leadership of the Social Department of the City of Zurich.
infoSekta is organised as an association.
The agency is independent of any denomination.
It advises those affected, relatives, people who have left, and professionals.
A group is judged above all by how it treats its members.

abschnitte.text: infoSekta was founded in **1990** under the leadership of the **Social Department of the City of Zurich**. Today the agency is organised as an **association** and has its seat in Zurich. It offers **information, advice, prevention** and **further training**. Prevention means: stopping problems before they arise.

The advice is aimed at people affected, but also especially at **relatives** and at **people who have left a group**. These are people who have left a group or want to leave one. **Professionals**, for example from schools, can also get in touch. The aim is to defuse conflicts around groups that take people over.

infoSekta describes itself as **independent of any denomination**. So it belongs to no church or religion. Agencies such as infoSekta judge a group above all by its **treatment of members**. Warning signs are, for example, strong **dependence**, **isolation** from the family or great **pressure on leaving**. An unusual belief alone does not make a group a problem.

There are further information agencies in Switzerland. The Protestant information agency **relinfo** in Rüti ZH works from an evangelical Reformed point of view. In French-speaking Switzerland, the **Centre intercantonal d’information sur les croyances (CIC)** in Geneva gives neutral information about faith communities. It is supported by several French-speaking cantons and Ticino. After the tragic events surrounding the Order of the Solar Temple, the **Control Committee of the National Council** published a report in 1999 on “sects or movements that take people over in Switzerland”.

gewusst: Instead of “sect”, experts often use the expression “movement that takes people over”, because it describes behaviour and not belief.
In Switzerland there are information agencies with a church background as well as independent ones.

teile.einleitung: The dharmachakra, the “wheel of the teaching”, is one of the most important symbols of Buddhism. It stands for the Buddha’s teaching, which spreads through the world like a wheel.
wichtigste: Dharmachakra means “wheel of the teaching”.
The Buddha’s first sermon is called “Setting the Wheel of the Dharma in Motion”.
On Tibetan monastery roofs, you often see the wheel with two gazelles.
In the 3rd century BC, Emperor Ashoka had pillars with a wheel put up.
A wheel with 24 spokes is shown on the Indian flag.
The eight spokes of the classic wheel stand for the Eightfold Path.

abschnitte.text: The word **dharmachakra** comes from Sanskrit. **Dharma** means teaching, **chakra** means wheel. The dharmachakra is one of the most important **symbols** of Buddhism. The round shape is seen as a sign of **perfection** and wholeness. The classic wheel has **eight spokes**. They stand for the **Eightfold Path**, the way the Buddha taught.

After his enlightenment, the Buddha gave his **first sermon** in a **deer park** near Sarnath. This sermon is called “**Setting the Wheel of the Dharma in Motion**”. According to tradition, with it the Buddha set the spread of his teaching in motion. That is why on **Tibetan monastery roofs** you often see a golden wheel with **two gazelles**, recalling this place.

In the **3rd century BC**, **Emperor Ashoka** of the Maurya dynasty ruled. After a bloody war he turned to **Buddhism**. Throughout the empire he had inscriptions and **pillars** with a wheel put up. A wheel of this kind with **24 spokes** stands today in the middle of the **flag of India**. It goes back to an old Buddhist pillar capital.

On many Buddha figures, the thumb and index finger of both hands form **circles** in front of the chest. This hand position is called the **dharmachakra mudra** and shows that the Buddha is **teaching**. In Tibetan Buddhism, believers turn **prayer wheels**. These are cylinders with **mantras** inside. One turn counts as much as saying the prayers they contain.

gewusst: The wheel on the Indian flag is blue and is called the “Ashoka Chakra” after the emperor.
There are giant prayer wheels so large that they can only be turned by many people together.

teile.einleitung: The Angelus bell is a ringing of bells that sounds three times a day in many Catholic places. It invites people to say a short prayer, the Angelus. Its name comes from the Latin word for angel.
wichtigste: The Angelus bell rings three times a day: in the morning, at midday and in the evening.
It invites people to say the Angelus prayer.
“Angelus” is Latin and means “angel”.
The prayer recalls the message of the angel Gabriel to Mary.
The Pope prays the Angelus with the faithful in Rome every Sunday at midday.

abschnitte.text: In many Catholic villages and towns, the **church bells** ring three times a day at fixed times: in the **morning**, at **midday** and in the **evening**. This ringing is called the **Angelus bell**. It reminds people to stop for a moment and pray. In the past, farmers in the fields also went by these bells to know what time it was.

The word **“Angelus”** is Latin and means “angel”. The prayer begins with the words “The angel of the Lord declared unto Mary”. It recalls the story in which the **angel Gabriel** announces to Mary that she is to become the mother of Jesus. Between short verses, the **Hail Mary** is prayed three times. In the Easter season, a different prayer to Mary, the Regina Caeli, is prayed instead of the Angelus.

The custom arose in the **Middle Ages**. First there was an evening bell, at which people prayed a Hail Mary. Later the morning and midday bells were added. The midday bell goes back to an appeal by Pope **Callixtus III** in 1456. In time, the ringing three times a day became usual in many Catholic countries.

Today not everyone prays when the Angelus bell rings, but the bells can still be heard in many places in Switzerland. They are part of the familiar sound of a village. The **Pope** prays the Angelus every Sunday at twelve o’clock from a window above St Peter’s Square in Rome. Thousands of people come, and many follow the prayer on television or online.

gewusst: The famous French painter Jean-François Millet painted a picture called “The Angelus”, showing two farm workers praying in a field.
In some regions the evening bell is also called the “Betzeitläuten”, the prayer-time bell.

teile.einleitung: Ashoka was an Indian emperor in the 3rd century BC. After a bloody war he turned away from violence and supported Buddhism. His inscriptions on rocks and pillars have survived to this day.
wichtigste: Ashoka belonged to the Maurya dynasty.
He was a grandson of the dynasty’s founder, Chandragupta Maurya.
After the war against Kalinga, he turned away from violence.
Most of his edicts are written in Brahmi script.
The Lion Capital of Sarnath is now the state emblem of India.
The Ashoka Chakra with 24 spokes is on the Indian flag.
James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837.

abschnitte.text: Ashoka belonged to the **Maurya** dynasty. He was a grandson of the founder, Chandragupta Maurya. The Maurya Empire covered large parts of the Indian subcontinent. Its capital was **Pataliputra**, today’s Patna. Ashoka ruled in the 3rd century BC and is regarded as one of the most important rulers of India.

Ashoka waged a bloody campaign against the land of **Kalinga**. In his 13th Rock Edict he regrets the many dead and the many people carried off. After that he wanted to rule only through **dharma**, that is, through right and just action. He supported Buddhism, demanded consideration for people and animals, and tolerance towards all religions. According to tradition, the **third Buddhist council** took place in Pataliputra under him.

Ashoka had his messages carved into rocks and pillars. These **edicts** are mostly written in **Brahmi**, the forerunner of many present-day South Asian scripts. In the north-west he also used Kharoshthi. Near **Kandahar** in Afghanistan, an inscription in Greek and Aramaic was even found in 1958. For a long time nobody could read the script, until **James Prinsep** deciphered it in 1837.

The **Lion Capital of Sarnath** shows four lions standing back to back. It once crowned a pillar at the place of the Buddha’s first sermon. Today it is the **state emblem of India**. The blue wheel in the middle of the Indian flag is called the **Ashoka Chakra** and has 24 spokes. According to tradition from Sri Lanka, Ashoka sent his son **Mahinda** to the island as a missionary.

gewusst: The wheel on the Indian flag comes from a work of art that is over 2,000 years old.
Ashoka was only rediscovered when his inscriptions could be read again in the 19th century.

teile.einleitung: St Peter’s Cathedral, in French Cathédrale Saint-Pierre, stands in the middle of the old town of Geneva. In the 16th century the reformer John Calvin preached here. This made the church a landmark of the Reformation.
wichtigste: Saint-Pierre Cathedral stands on the highest point of the old town of Geneva.
Building began in the 12th century.
John Calvin preached here in the 16th century.
Since the Reformation it has been a Reformed church.
From the towers there is a wide view over Geneva and the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Saint-Pierre Cathedral** stands on the hill of the **old town** of Geneva. Building began in the 12th century, first in the Romanesque and then in the Gothic style. In the 18th century it received a columned porch at the front, like an ancient temple. That is why it looks different from outside than from inside. Under the church, remains of much older buildings have been found, which can be visited today.

In the 16th century Geneva became Reformed. The reformer **John Calvin** lived in the city and preached in the cathedral. He made Geneva a centre of the **Reformation**, which drew people from many countries. In the church there is still a chair that is shown as **Calvin’s chair**. Inside, the church is plain, because the Reformed removed pictures and decoration.

Anyone who climbs the many steps in the **towers** has a wide view over Geneva, **Lake Geneva** and, on clear days, as far as the Alps. In the tower also hangs the great bell **“La Clémence”**. Not far from the cathedral, the large **Reformation Wall** in the Parc des Bastions recalls Calvin and other reformers.

gewusst: Under Saint-Pierre Cathedral lies a large archaeological excavation.
The front of the Gothic church looks like an ancient temple with columns.

teile.einleitung: The bat mitzvah is the celebration in Judaism at which a girl comes of age religiously. Under Jewish law this happens at the age of 12. From then on, the religious commandments apply to the girl as they do to adults.
wichtigste: “Bat mitzvah” means “daughter of the commandment”.
Girls become bat mitzvah at 12 years old, boys become bar mitzvah at 13.
Coming of age happens through age alone.
In liberal communities, girls read aloud from the Torah.
The haftarah from the Prophets is often recited as well.
Judith Kaplan celebrated the first public bat mitzvah in the USA in New York in 1922.

abschnitte.text: The word **bat** means “daughter” and **mitzvah** means “commandment”. Bat mitzvah therefore means **“daughter of the commandment”**. With this step, a girl comes of age religiously in Judaism. From then on she is herself responsible for keeping the commandments. For boys the corresponding celebration is called **bar mitzvah**; “bar” is the Aramaic word for “son”.

Under Jewish law, girls come of age religiously at **12 years old**, boys only at **13**. Coming of age happens **automatically** with age. Even without a celebration, a girl therefore becomes bat mitzvah. The celebration is a lovely custom, but not a requirement. Many families nevertheless prepare for it for a long time and celebrate with relatives and friends.

In **liberal communities**, girls at their bat mitzvah read aloud from the **Torah scroll** just like boys. They often also recite the **haftarah**. This is a passage from the books of the Prophets that follows the Torah reading on the Sabbath. In **Orthodox communities** the bat mitzvah is usually celebrated differently. There the girl gives, for example, a talk on a religious text.

The bar mitzvah for boys is an old custom, while the celebration for girls is much younger. In 1922 **Judith Kaplan** celebrated the first public bat mitzvah in the USA in **New York**. She was the daughter of Rabbi **Mordecai Kaplan**. Since then the custom has spread in many communities. Today the bat mitzvah is also celebrated in Jewish communities in Switzerland.

gewusst: The bat mitzvah has only been celebrated publicly for about 100 years.
In Judaism, girls come of age religiously a year earlier than boys.

teile.einleitung: Buddha statues are found in many countries of Asia and all over the world. They show Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, and have special features. Every posture and every hand position has a meaning.
wichtigste: Many statues show a raised bump on the head that looks like a topknot.
The long earlobes recall the heavy jewellery that Siddhartha wore as a prince.
Half-closed eyes show that the Buddha is looking calmly inwards.
The reclining Buddha shows him at the end of his life.
In Wat Pho in Bangkok lies a gilded Buddha about 46 metres long.
The Leshan Giant Buddha in China is about 71 metres high.

abschnitte.text: Buddha statues can be recognised by special signs. On the head you can see a **bump** that looks like a **topknot**. It is seen as a sign of his wisdom. The **earlobes** are long because Siddhartha wore heavy gold earrings as a prince. The **eyes** are often half closed. This shows that he is looking calmly inwards and meditating.

The posture of a statue tells something from the Buddha’s life. The **reclining Buddha** rests on his right side and shows him shortly before his death. When the Buddha touches the **earth** with one hand, he is calling on it as a **witness** to his enlightenment. This happened when the demon Mara disturbed him. Such hand gestures are called **mudras**.

In the temple of **Wat Pho** in **Bangkok** lies a gilded Buddha about **46 metres** long. In **Thailand** many statues are gilded or gold-coloured, because gold shows how precious the teaching is. In **China** stands the **Leshan Giant Buddha**. It is about **71 metres** high and was carved out of a cliff over 1,200 years ago.

You often also see a figure of a fat, **laughing** man. It shows **Budai**, a cheerful monk from China. He is not the Buddha Siddhartha. In China, Budai is regarded as a bringer of good luck. He can be recognised by his round belly and broad laugh.

For Buddhists, a Buddha statue is something **sacred**. You should not **climb** on a statue or sit on it. In temples you take off your shoes beforehand. In Switzerland too there are Buddhist monasteries and centres with Buddha statues, where these rules are observed.

gewusst: The soles of the feet of the reclining Buddha in Wat Pho are decorated with elaborate mother-of-pearl pictures.
The Leshan Giant Buddha is so big that many people can fit on one of his feet.

teile.einleitung: Brahman is a central concept of Indian philosophy. In the Upanishads, ancient holy texts of Hinduism, Brahman refers to the absolute reality that underlies everything.
wichtigste: In the Upanishads, Brahman is the impersonal ultimate ground of all things.
It must not be confused with the god Brahma or the caste of the Brahmins.
Brahman is often described as Sat-Chit-Ananda: being, consciousness, bliss.
Thought of without any qualities, it is called Nirguna Brahman.
With qualities, for example as a personal god, it is called Saguna Brahman.

abschnitte.text: The **Upanishads** are philosophical texts of Hinduism. They ask what lies behind all things. Their answer is **Brahman**: the absolute reality, the **ultimate ground** of everything. Brahman is not a person, but impersonal. Important: Brahman is not the same as the god **Brahma** or the caste of the **Brahmins**, even though the words sound similar.

Because the Absolute is hard to describe, a formula is used: **Sat-Chit-Ananda**. This means **being**, **consciousness** and **bliss**. These three words describe Brahman without limiting it. They are not an exact picture, but a pointer to how the Absolute can be experienced.

Indian thinkers distinguish two ways of seeing it. **Nirguna Brahman** means Brahman “without qualities”. Thought of in this way, it is beyond all words and forms. **Saguna Brahman** is the Absolute “with qualities”, for example as a personal god whom one can worship. Many believers pray in this way to a deity and see in it the one Brahman.

gewusst: A famous saying from the Upanishads is “Tat tvam asi”, which means “That is you”. It expresses that the innermost self of a person is connected with Brahman.
The innermost self of a person is called the Atman in the Upanishads.

teile.einleitung: Many Indigenous peoples of North America believe in a great, sacred power that created everything and is present in everything. It is often called the “Great Spirit”. Depending on the people, this power has a name of its own.
wichtigste: Many Indigenous peoples of North America believe in the Great Spirit.
Among the Lakota it is called Wakan Tanka, the great mystery.
Among Algonquian peoples it is called Manitou or Gitche Manitou.
The earth is respected as “Mother Earth”.
The eagle feather is regarded as sacred.
The dreamcatcher comes from the Ojibwe.

abschnitte.text: For many Indigenous peoples of North America there is one great sacred power. It created the world and lives in people, animals, plants, stones and in the wind. In English it is often called the **Great Spirit**. Among the **Lakota** this power is called **Wakan Tanka**, which means roughly “the great mystery”. Among Algonquian peoples in the north-east, people speak of **Manitou** or Gitche Manitou.

Many peoples call the earth **Mother Earth**. She gives food and life and is therefore respected. For the peoples of the prairie, the **bison** was especially important. It supplied meat, hides for clothes and tents, and bones for tools. That is why it was honoured and thanked. The **eagle** flies very high and is regarded as a messenger to the sky. Its feathers are therefore sacred and very valuable.

At important gatherings and ceremonies, among some peoples a **sacred pipe** was passed around the circle. The rising smoke was meant to carry the prayers to the Great Spirit. The circle is an important sign: it stands for the connection of all things. Ceremonies are often accompanied by drums, singing and dance.

The **dreamcatcher** comes from the **Ojibwe**. It consists of a ring with a net, often decorated with feathers. According to belief, bad dreams stay caught in the net. The good dreams slide through the hole in the middle to the sleeper. Today dreamcatchers hang all over the world, often as decoration.

gewusst: In North America there are hundreds of Indigenous peoples with languages and beliefs of their own.
The expression “Great Spirit” is a translation that sums up many different ideas in a simplified way.

teile.einleitung: John is one of the best-known first names in the world. It comes from Hebrew and has a beautiful meaning. In the Bible several important people bear this name.
wichtigste: The name John comes from Hebrew.
It means “God is gracious”.
Hans, Jan and Jean are forms of John.
In the Bible there are John the Baptist and the apostle John.
On 24 June people celebrate St John’s Day.

abschnitte.text: The name **John** goes back to the Hebrew name **Yochanan**. It means “**God is gracious**”. The name came to Europe by way of Greek and Latin. Through Christianity it became very popular in many countries.

In the Bible there are several important men with this name. **John the Baptist** baptised people in the Jordan and, according to the New Testament, Jesus too. The **apostle John** was one of the twelve disciples of Jesus. According to tradition, a Gospel is also ascribed to him. The feast day of John the Baptist is **24 June**, St John’s Day.

Hardly any name has so many forms. In German people also say **Hans** or Johann, in French **Jean**, in Italian Giovanni, in English John and in Spanish Juan. In Holland and Scandinavia it is **Jan**, in Russia Ivan. In Switzerland, Hans was for a long time one of the most common men’s names. Several popes also took the name John.

gewusst: Hans, Jean, John and Ivan are really all the same name.
The well-known inventor of printing with movable type was called Johannes Gutenberg.

teile.einleitung: Inti was the god of the sun for the Incas. He was among the most important deities of the Inca Empire in South America. Even today festivals, places and even flags recall him.
wichtigste: Inti was the sun god of the Incas.
The ruler, the Sapa Inca, was regarded as the son of the sun.
The great sun festival is called Inti Raymi and is celebrated on 24 June in Cusco.
The most important sun temple was the Coricancha in Cusco.
The moon goddess Mama Quilla was regarded as Inti’s consort.
The “Sun of May” on the flags of Argentina and Uruguay recalls Inti.

abschnitte.text: Among the **Incas**, **Inti** was the god of the **sun**. He brought light, warmth and good harvests. This was especially important in the high Andes. The ruler of the Incas, the **Sapa Inca**, was regarded as the **son of the sun**. This gave his rule a sacred meaning. The moon goddess **Mama Quilla** was regarded as Inti’s consort. The Incas arranged festivals and parts of their calendar by her.

The most important sun temple was the **Coricancha** in **Cusco**, the capital of the Inca Empire. Its walls were covered with **plates of gold**. When the Spanish came in the 16th century, they plundered the temple. On its walls they built a monastery. The finely worked stone walls of the Incas can still be seen there today.

The great sun festival is called **Inti Raymi**, which means “Festival of the Sun”. It takes place on **24 June**, near the winter solstice in the southern hemisphere. Then the sun stands at its lowest there. The Incas asked Inti to become stronger again. Today the festival is performed every year as a great spectacle in Cusco and attracts many visitors.

In **Machu Picchu** stands a carved stone called the **Intihuatana**. The name means “place where the sun is tied up”. It probably served for observing the sun. With it the Incas could determine important times of the year, for example for sowing and harvest.

On the flags of **Argentina** and **Uruguay** the **Sun of May**, the “Sol de Mayo”, can be seen. It shows a face with rays. It recalls the revolution of May 1810 and the sun god of the Incas. From 1985 to 1991 Peru even named its currency after him: the **inti**. Because of heavy inflation it was replaced by the nuevo sol.

gewusst: The present currency of Peru, the sol, also has the sun in its name.
The Incas spoke Quechua, which millions of people in the Andes still speak today.

teile.einleitung: Christopher is a saint of the Christian churches. According to the legend, he carried the infant Jesus across a river. That is why he is regarded as the protector of all travellers.
wichtigste: Christopher is regarded as the protector of travellers.
According to the legend, he carried the infant Jesus across a river.
His name means “Christ-bearer”.
He is usually shown as a giant with a child on his shoulder.
His feast day is 25 July.

abschnitte.text: The **legend** tells of a very big, strong man. He wanted to serve the most powerful lord in the world. A hermit advised him to carry people across a dangerous **river**. One night he carried a **child** across. The child grew heavier and heavier until he could hardly go on. On the other bank he learned that he had been carrying **Christ**.

The name **Christopher** comes from Greek and means “**Christ-bearer**”. Because he brought people safely across the river, he is regarded as the **protector of travellers**. Many people have a small **St Christopher medal** in their car. He is also one of the **Fourteen Holy Helpers**, a group of saints whom people ask for help in times of need.

Christopher is usually shown as a **giant** with a staff, carrying the infant Jesus on his shoulder. In many old churches, including in Switzerland, he is painted large on a wall. In the Middle Ages, many people believed that anyone who saw his picture in the morning was protected from sudden death that day. His **feast day** is **25 July**.

gewusst: Whether Christopher really lived is not certain; his story is handed down mainly as a legend.
Rescue helicopters in Austria bear the name “Christophorus”.

teile.einleitung: The **Eternal Light** is a lamp that burns day and night in Catholic churches. It is usually **red**. It shows that the consecrated bread is kept in the tabernacle.
wichtigste: The Eternal Light burns day and night.
In Catholic churches it is usually red.
It stands near the tabernacle.
It shows that the consecrated bread is kept there.
There is also an Eternal Light in synagogues.

abschnitte.text: In almost every Catholic church you see a small lamp, often in **red** glass. This is the **Eternal Light**. It stands near the **tabernacle**. This is a locked cupboard in which the **hosts** are kept. These are the breads that were consecrated at Mass. For Catholics, Christ is present in them. The light is meant to show: this is a particularly holy place.

In the past the Eternal Light usually burned **oil**, often olive oil. Today wax candles in a casing are often used. So that it never goes out, it is replaced regularly. If the tabernacle is empty, for example on Good Friday, the light is put out. In this way you notice that something has changed.

The idea is very old. The Bible describes that a lamp was to burn constantly in the sanctuary of the Israelites. That is why an Eternal Light also hangs in **synagogues**, in Hebrew **Ner Tamid**. There it burns in front of the cabinet with the Torah scrolls. In Orthodox churches too, oil lamps often glow in front of the icons.

gewusst: Anyone entering a Catholic church can tell from the red light where the tabernacle is.
Ner Tamid means roughly “constant light” in Hebrew.

teile.einleitung: At an interreligious celebration, people of different religions come together to pray, remember or celebrate together. Such celebrations are meant to strengthen respect and peace between the religions.
wichtigste: At interreligious celebrations, members of different religions come together.
In multireligious prayer, each religion prays in its own form, side by side.
In interreligious prayer, everyone says a text together.
In 1893 the first Parliament of the World’s Religions took place in Chicago.
The Federal Day of Prayer has been celebrated together since 1832.
In Switzerland there are often interreligious memorial services after accidents.

abschnitte.text: There are two ways of praying together. In **multireligious prayer**, each religion prays in turn in its own form. The others listen respectfully. In **interreligious prayer**, everyone says a text together. Many communities prefer the first form, because each keeps its own faith. At celebrations, Judaism, Christianity and Islam often refer to their common forefather Abraham. They are therefore called the **Abrahamic religions**.

In 1893 the first **Parliament of the World’s Religions** met in **Chicago** during the World’s Fair. Swami Vivekananda made Hinduism known in the West there. In 1965 the Second Vatican Council adopted the declaration **“Nostra aetate”**. In it the Catholic Church says that it rejects nothing that is true and holy in other religions. In 2019 Pope Francis and the Grand Imam of al-Azhar signed a document in **Abu Dhabi** on the brotherhood of all people.

In 2010 the UN, on a proposal from **Jordan**, proclaimed the **World Interfaith Harmony Week**. It takes place every year in the first week of February. Religious communities all over the world then arrange joint events. The UN also declared 4 February, the day of the Abu Dhabi Declaration, the International Day of Human Fraternity.
