His main work is called the Kitab-i-Aqdas.
From 1868 he lived in exile in Acre, where he died in 1892.
His successor was his son Abdu’l-Baha.

abschnitte.text: **Baha’u’llah** is an Arabic title of honour and means “Glory of God”. His birth name was **Mirza Husayn Ali Nuri**. He was born in 1817 in **Tehran** into a noble family. He joined the **Bab**, who announced the coming of a new messenger of God. The Bab was executed in Tabriz in 1850.

Because of his faith, Baha’u’llah was banished from Persia and lived in **Baghdad**. Before leaving there in 1863, he spent twelve days in the **Ridvan Garden**. There he declared that he was the messenger of God who had been announced. The twelve-day **Ridvan festival** of the Baha’is recalls this. For Baha’is, the Bab’s announcement was fulfilled in this way.

Baha’u’llah wrote many texts. His main work is the **Kitab-i-Aqdas**, the “Most Holy Book”. It was written around 1873 in Acre. It contains commandments on **prayer**, **fasting** and the organisation of the community. Baha’is read his writings as divine revelation.

From 1868 the Ottomans banished him to the fortress town of **Acre**. He died in 1892 in the nearby country house of **Bahji**. His tomb there is today the holiest place of the Baha’is. In his will he named his eldest son **Abdu’l-Baha** as his successor and interpreter of his writings. The highest body of the Baha’is, the **Universal House of Justice**, has its seat in Haifa.

gewusst: The tomb of Baha’u’llah near Acre is the point towards which Baha’is turn when they pray.
Baha’u’llah spent about 40 years of his life in captivity and exile.

teile.einleitung: The Kaaba is a cube-shaped building in Mecca in Saudi Arabia. It is the most important sanctuary in Islam. Muslims all over the world pray in its direction.
wichtigste: The Kaaba stands in Mecca in the middle of the Sacred Mosque.
It is the most important sanctuary of Islam.
It is covered with a black cloth, the kiswa.
In prayer, Muslims turn towards the Kaaba.
Pilgrims walk around the Kaaba seven times during the hajj.

abschnitte.text: The word **Kaaba** means “cube”. The building stands in **Mecca** in the courtyard of the great **Sacred Mosque**. It is built of stone and is roughly as tall as a house of four storeys. It is covered with a black cloth, the **kiswa**. The cloth is embroidered in gold with verses from the Qur’an and is renewed every year.

abschnitte.titel: Centre of the direction of prayer
abschnitte.text: The Kaaba is the most important sanctuary in **Islam**. Muslims all over the world pray five times a day in its direction. This direction of prayer is called the **qibla**. In every mosque a niche in the wall shows where the qibla lies. In Switzerland too, mosques are aligned in this way.

Every year very many people come to Mecca on pilgrimage, the **hajj**. Every Muslim should make it once in their life, if they are healthy and can afford it. The pilgrims walk **seven times** around the Kaaba. In one corner of the Kaaba the **Black Stone** is set into the wall, which many pilgrims want to touch. According to Islamic tradition, Abraham and his son Ishmael built the Kaaba.

gewusst: The black cloth of the Kaaba is replaced by a new one every year.
The pilgrims walk around the Kaaba anticlockwise.

teile.einleitung: The Baal Shem Tov was a Jewish teacher in Eastern Europe in the 18th century. He is regarded as the founder of Hasidism, a devout movement within Judaism. His real name was Israel ben Eliezer.
wichtigste: His real name was Israel ben Eliezer.
He lived from about 1700 to 1760.
“Baal Shem Tov” means “Master of the Good Name”.
He worked in Podolia, which is now part of Ukraine.
He is regarded as the founder of Hasidism.
Pupils such as Dov Ber of Mezritch passed on his teaching.

abschnitte.text: His real name was **Israel ben Eliezer**. He lived from about 1700 to 1760. His followers gave him the title of honour **Baal Shem Tov**, often shortened to “Besht”. A “Baal Shem” was a wonder-worker who healed with the name of God. The word “tov” means “good”, so the name means **“Master of the Good Name”**.

The Baal Shem Tov worked in **Podolia**, a region that is now part of Ukraine. In the end he lived in the little town of **Medzhybizh**. At that time many Jews lived there in simple circumstances. He travelled about, healed the sick and told stories. Soon pupils gathered around him.

The Baal Shem Tov is regarded as the founder of **Hasidism**. This movement stresses that one can meet God everywhere in everyday life. **Joy**, sincere prayer, singing and dancing are important. Not only learned men, but also ordinary people, were to be able to be close to God. In this way he appealed to many who did not feel at home in strict scholarship.

The Baal Shem Tov died in **1760**. He himself left hardly any writings. His teachings were passed on by pupils such as **Dov Ber of Mezritch**. In this way Hasidism spread quickly in Eastern Europe. Today there are Hasidic communities mainly in Israel and the USA, and his grave in Medzhybizh is a place for pilgrims.

gewusst: Many stories about the Baal Shem Tov were only collected and written down after his death.
His short name “Besht” is formed from the initial letters of Baal Shem Tov.

teile.einleitung: Deism is a religious and philosophical attitude from the time of the Enlightenment. Deists believe in a God who created the world but afterwards no longer intervenes in it.
wichtigste: Deists believe in a creator God who can be known through reason.
They reject revelation, miracles and God’s interventions in the world.
God is often compared to a watchmaker.
With “De veritate” (1624), Edward Herbert of Cherbury is regarded as the father of English deism.
Matthew Tindal’s work of 1730 was called the “Bible of Deism”.
From 1774, Lessing published the writings of Hermann Samuel Reimarus.

abschnitte.text: **Deism** says: God created the world but no longer intervenes. Deists often compare God to a **watchmaker**. He built the world like a **clockwork** and wound it up. After that it runs by itself according to fixed **laws of nature**. This image suited the thinking of the **Enlightenment**, when scientists were exploring the laws of nature.

Deists think that God can be known through **reason**. That is why they see no need for **revelation**, that is, for a message from God through prophets or holy books. They also reject **miracles**. What matters to them is a creator God and a virtuous life. This attitude is also called **natural religion**.

**Edward Herbert of Cherbury** is regarded as the father of English deism. In his work “De veritate” of **1624**, he named five principles of a natural religion, such as that God exists and that one should live virtuously. **Matthew Tindal** wrote “Christianity as Old as the Creation” in 1730. In it he says that true religion is as old as creation. The book was called the “**Bible of Deism**”.

There were well-known deists in America too. From 1794, **Thomas Paine** wrote “**The Age of Reason**”. He believed in God, but sharply criticised churches and revealed religion. **Thomas Jefferson** cut the **accounts of miracles** out of the Gospels. In this so-called **Jefferson Bible**, Jesus remained as a teacher of morality.

The Hamburg scholar **Hermann Samuel Reimarus** secretly wrote a sharp criticism of the Bible. After his death, **Gotthold Ephraim Lessing** published parts of it from **1774** as the “**Fragments of an Anonymous Author**”. This set off the **Fragments Controversy** with the chief pastor **Goeze**. The Genevan **Jean-Jacques Rousseau** also held ideas of a natural religion.

gewusst: The word deism comes from the Latin “deus”, which means God.
Lessing’s famous play “Nathan the Wise” arose in connection with the Fragments Controversy.

teile.einleitung: The Ganges is one of the largest rivers in Asia. It flows mainly through India and is holy to Hindus. They worship it as the goddess Ganga.
wichtigste: The Ganges flows mainly through India and finally through Bangladesh.
It rises from a glacier in the Himalayas.
It flows into the Bay of Bengal, part of the Indian Ocean.
For Hindus the Ganges is holy; they worship it as the goddess Ganga.
Many Hindus bathe in the Ganges to cleanse their souls.
The holy city of Varanasi lies on the Ganges.

abschnitte.titel: From the mountains to the sea
abschnitte.text: The Ganges rises high in the **Himalayas** from a **glacier**. The source stream is called the **Bhagirathi**. Later it joins another mountain river and is then called the Ganges. It flows through the great plain in the north of India. Finally it reaches **Bangladesh** and flows into the **Bay of Bengal**. The river is about 2,600 kilometres long.

For Hindus the Ganges is a **holy river**. They worship it as the goddess **Ganga**. A bath in the Ganges is said to **cleanse the soul**. Many people take water from the river home with them. In the evening they set small **lights** and flowers on the water, which drift away on the river. This ceremony with lights is called **aarti**.

**Varanasi** is one of the holiest cities of the Hindus. There many broad flights of steps lead down to the river. They are called **ghats**. In the morning many people come to pray and bathe. Haridwar and Prayagraj on the Ganges are also important places of pilgrimage. In Prayagraj the **Kumbh Mela** takes place regularly, one of the largest pilgrim festivals in the world.

Very many people live on the Ganges. The river brings water for fields, villages and towns. In the estuary it forms, together with the river **Brahmaputra**, a huge **delta**. There grow great mangrove forests, the **Sundarbans**, where the Bengal tiger lives. Today the river is badly **polluted** in many places. India is trying to make the water cleaner with large programmes.

gewusst: The Ganges river dolphin lives in the Ganges; it is almost blind and finds its way with clicking sounds.
The delta of the Ganges and Brahmaputra is one of the largest river deltas in the world.

teile.einleitung: Animism is the belief that nature has a soul. According to this idea, animals, plants, mountains, rivers or stones have a soul or a spirit. This view is found in many nature religions all over the world.
wichtigste: Animism means that animals, plants and things also have a soul.
The word comes from the Latin “anima”, which means soul or breath.
The British scholar Edward Burnett Tylor made the term known in 1871.
In many animist religions, the spirits of the ancestors are revered.
A totem is a protective symbol of a family or clan.
In Polynesia, a mysterious power is called mana.
For the Aboriginal people of Australia, Uluru is a sacred place.

abschnitte.text: In **animism**, the world is full of life and spirits. A tree, a river or a mountain can have a soul of its own. That is why people treat nature with respect. For example, they ask for permission before they fell a tree or hunt an animal. The word comes from the Latin **anima**, which means soul or breath.

The British anthropologist **Edward Burnett Tylor** made the term known. In 1871 he described animism in his book “Primitive Culture”. Tylor regarded it as a very early form of religion. He is regarded as one of the founders of **ethnology**, the study of peoples and cultures, in Britain. Today researchers no longer see such forms of belief as “primitive”, but as worldviews in their own right, and rich ones.

In many nature religions, the dead forebears remain part of the family. People honour the **spirits of the ancestors** and ask them for protection. Some groups have a **totem**. This is usually an animal or plant with which a family or clan feels closely connected. The totem is often seen as an ancestor or protector of the group.

In Polynesia and Melanesia, people know of **mana**. This is a supernatural power that can work in people and things. Anyone with a lot of mana is regarded as powerful and respected. The Aboriginal people of Australia tell of the **Dreaming**. At that time ancestral beings shaped landscapes, animals and rules, and this time is seen as still active today.

For the Anangu, an Aboriginal people, the great red rock **Uluru** is sacred. That is why climbing it has been banned since 2019. In Japanese **Shinto** too, spirits, the kami, live in nature. A **torii**, a gate made of two posts and two crossbeams, marks the entrance to a shrine. It separates the everyday world from the sacred area.

gewusst: Climbing Uluru has been banned since 2019, out of respect for the Anangu.
A torii is often painted bright red and sometimes even stands in the water.

teile.einleitung: Chinese folk religion is the belief of many people in China and Taiwan that is not tied to any single church. It reveres many gods, spirits and above all one’s own ancestors.
wichtigste: At the head of the world of the gods stands the Jade Emperor.
Before New Year, the Kitchen God reports to the Jade Emperor about the family.
Mazu is revered especially by sailors in Fujian and Taiwan.
The general Guan Yu was deified as the god of loyalty.
At the Qingming Festival, families tend the graves of their ancestors in spring.
In the seventh lunar month, hungry ghosts are provided for at the Ghost Festival.

abschnitte.titel: A world of gods like an imperial court
abschnitte.text: At the head of the heavenly order stands the **Jade Emperor**. He rules heaven like an emperor with his **officials**. The world of the gods thus mirrors the administration of ancient China. At the bottom are local gods such as **Tudigong**, the earth god of a village or a piece of land. He often has a small shrine by the wayside.

In many homes there is a place for the **Kitchen God Zao Jun**. He watches over the family all year round. Before the New Year festival he travels to heaven and makes his **report to the Jade Emperor**. So that he will say only good things, he is given **sweets** beforehand. In this way his words are meant to be sweet.

**Mazu** is the goddess of sailors. She is said to have lived in the 10th century as a girl named Lin Moniang and to have saved sailors. In **Fujian** and **Taiwan** she is one of the most popular deities. **Guan Yu** was a general from the time of the **Three Kingdoms**. After his death he was deified as **Guandi**. He is regarded as the god of **loyalty** and as the patron of merchants and police officers.

The **ancestors** are very important. At the **Qingming Festival**, around the beginning of April, families clean the graves and make offerings. It is therefore also called the Tomb-Sweeping Festival. Believers burn **paper money for the afterlife**, also called ghost money, and today even paper models of houses or cars. In the **seventh lunar month**, the gates of the underworld are said to open. On the 15th day, wandering ghosts receive food and offerings at the **Ghost Festival**.

gewusst: There are Mazu temples in many port cities of Asia where Chinese sailors and merchants lived.
Many Chinese restaurants and shops have a small altar to Guandi, the god of loyalty.

teile.einleitung: Antisemitism means hostility and hatred towards Jewish people. It has a long history that reaches back to the Middle Ages and even further. It existed in Switzerland too, and today the law punishes incitement against groups.
wichtigste: The term “antisemitism” became known from 1879 through Wilhelm Marr.
The religiously based hostility to Jews in the Middle Ages is called anti-Judaism.
During the plague of 1348/49, Jews were falsely accused of poisoning wells.
From 1894 the Dreyfus Affair divided France.
In 1935 a Bernese court ruled that the “Protocols of the Elders of Zion” are a forgery.
In the November pogrom of 9 to 10 November 1938, synagogues burned.
Article 261bis of the Criminal Code has punished racial discrimination since 1995.

abschnitte.titel: Hostility to Jews in the Middle Ages
abschnitte.text: In the Christian Middle Ages there was a hostility to Jews that was mainly religious in origin, called **anti-Judaism**. For example, Jews were reproached for not recognising Jesus as the Messiah. The **Fourth Lateran Council** of 1215 laid down that Jews had to be distinguishable from Christians by their clothing. After that, in many places they wore badges or a pointed Jewish hat.

When the great **plague** raged in Europe in 1348/49, many people looked for someone to blame. It was falsely claimed that Jews had poisoned the wells. This accusation of **well poisoning** led to persecutions all over Europe. Thousands were murdered or driven out. In **Basel** too, many Jews were killed on an island in the Rhine in January 1349, and the survivors had to leave the city.

abschnitte.titel: A new word and an affair
abschnitte.text: From 1879 the journalist **Wilhelm Marr** made the word “antisemitism” known. It was meant to present hatred of Jews as a seemingly scientific, racist attitude. In France, from 1894, the Jewish captain **Alfred Dreyfus** was wrongly accused of treason. The writer Émile Zola defended him in 1898 with the letter “J’accuse”. In 1906 Dreyfus was cleared of the charges.

In the **Bern trial** of 1935, Jewish communities took legal action against Frontists who were spreading a hate pamphlet. The court ruled that the “Protocols of the Elders of Zion” are a **forgery**. At Switzerland’s urging, Germany marked the passports of German Jews with a **“J”** in 1938. That allowed Swiss authorities to recognise Jewish refugees at the border and turn them away. The Federal Council officially apologised for this in 1995.

On the night of 9 to 10 November 1938, the SA and SS destroyed synagogues, shops and homes in Germany and Austria. This **November pogrom** marks the move to open persecution, which ended in the Holocaust. In Switzerland, the **anti-racism law** was accepted in a national vote in 1994. Article 261bis of the Criminal Code has applied since 1995 and also punishes denial of the Holocaust.

gewusst: The Bern trial of 1935 was one of the first in which a court declared the “Protocols of the Elders of Zion” a forgery.
Switzerland’s anti-racism law was accepted by the people in a vote.

teile.einleitung: A house of worship is a building where people come together to pray and celebrate. Every religion has its own houses of worship: churches, mosques, synagogues, temples and many more. In Switzerland too there are many different ones.
wichtigste: In houses of worship people pray and celebrate together.
Christians usually go to church on Sunday, while Muslims meet for prayer at the mosque on Friday.
The prayer niche in a mosque points towards Mecca.
The house of worship of the Sikhs is called a gurdwara.
The Bern Minster has the tallest church tower in Switzerland.
In Bern there has been the House of Religions since 2014.

abschnitte.text: Christians gather in **churches**, usually on **Sunday**. A particularly large church is called a minster or a cathedral. The **Bern Minster** is the great main church in the old town of Bern. It is a **Reformed** church. With about 100 metres, its tower is the **tallest church tower in Switzerland**. The house of worship of the Jews, the **synagogue**, is also an important place for prayer and study.

Muslims pray in the **mosque**. On **Friday** they meet for the most important shared prayer of the week, the Friday prayer at midday. Before entering you take off your **shoes**, because you pray on carpets on the floor. In the wall there is a **prayer niche**, which shows the direction of **Mecca** in Saudi Arabia. Everyone prays in this direction.

A **pagoda** is a Buddhist tower with several storeys and curved roofs one above the other. You see them in China, Japan and other countries of Asia. Often valuable objects of Buddhism are kept in them. The house of worship of the Sikhs is called a **gurdwara**, which means “door to the Guru”. There, after the prayer, all guests get a meal free of charge.

In **Bern** there has been the **House of Religions** since **2014**. There different religions have their rooms under one roof, for example a Hindu temple, a mosque and a church. Church, mosque and synagogue have something in common: people come together there to **pray** and celebrate. Anyone who visits a house of worship behaves quietly and respectfully. Before photographing people at prayer, you first ask for **permission**.

gewusst: You can often recognise a house of worship from the outside, for example by a church tower, a minaret or a dome.
Many houses of worship can also be visited as a guest without a faith of your own, if you observe the rules.

teile.einleitung: Many religions have a holy scripture. In it are stories, commandments and prayers that are especially important to believers. Well-known examples are the Bible, the Torah, the Qur’an and the Vedas.
wichtigste: The holy book of the Christians is the Bible.
The Bible consists of the Old and New Testaments.
The Torah comprises the five books of Moses and is written in Hebrew.
The Qur’an is the holy book of the Muslims and is written in Arabic.
The Vedas are the oldest holy scriptures of the Hindus.
In Zurich, at the time of the Reformation, the Zurich Bible came into being.

abschnitte.text: For Jews, the **five books of Moses** are especially holy. They are called the **Torah**. It tells of the creation of the world up to the death of Moses and contains many commandments. The Torah is written in **Hebrew**, which is read from right to left. In the synagogue it is read aloud from a handwritten scroll. The Torah also stands at the beginning of the Christian Bible.

The holy book of the Christians is the **Bible**. The word comes from the Greek word for “books”, because the Bible consists of many individual books. It has two great parts. The **Old Testament** tells the story before Jesus. The **New Testament** tells of the life of Jesus and the first Christians. In it are the four **Gospels** according to Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

For Muslims the **Qur’an** contains the words of God to the Prophet **Muhammad**. It is divided into **114 chapters**, which are called **surahs**. The Qur’an was written down in **Arabic**. That is why many Muslims all over the world learn to read Arabic, even if they speak a different language in everyday life. Some even learn the whole Qur’an by heart.

The oldest holy scriptures of the Hindus are the **Vedas**. They are over 3,000 years old and were composed in Sanskrit. For a long time they were passed on only orally, from teacher to pupil. Other religions also have holy texts: the Sikhs have the Guru Granth Sahib, the Buddhists, for example, the discourses of the Buddha.

At the time of the **Reformation**, scholars in Zurich under **Huldrych Zwingli** translated the Bible into German. In 1531 it was printed complete in Zurich. This **Zurich Bible** has been revised again and again since then. The Reformed Church in Switzerland uses it to this day.

gewusst: The Bible has been translated completely into over 700 languages.
The Zurich Bible of 1531 appeared a few years before the complete Luther Bible of 1534.

teile.einleitung: **Endingen** and **Lengnau** are two neighbouring villages in the **Surbtal** in the canton of **Aargau**. For a long time they were the only places in Switzerland where Jews were allowed to live. That is why they are among the most important places in Jewish history in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Endingen and Lengnau lie in the Surbtal in the canton of Aargau.
From 1776, Jews in Switzerland were allowed to live only in these two villages.
In the 18th century the villages belonged to the County of Baden, a common bailiwick.
The Jewish cemetery between the villages is the oldest surviving one in Switzerland.
The synagogue of Endingen has a clock on its gable.
Ferdinand Stadler built the synagogue of Lengnau, consecrated in 1847.
From 1866, Jews were allowed to settle freely all over Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: In the 18th century Endingen and Lengnau belonged to the **County of Baden**. This was a **common bailiwick**, which several Confederate places administered together. Jews there had to buy expensive **letters of protection** in order to be allowed to stay. From **1776**, they were permitted to live in Switzerland only in these two villages. They were not allowed to practise many trades and could not own land. Many earned their living as traders, for example in cattle or cloth.

In Endingen and Lengnau you can see old **double-door houses**. They have two entrance doors side by side. Jews and Christians were not allowed to use a shared entrance. With two doors they could still live in the same house. Today these houses recall the rules that separated Jews and Christians.

Both villages have a **synagogue**. The synagogue of Lengnau was built by the Zurich architect **Ferdinand Stadler** and was consecrated in 1847. The synagogue of Endingen dates from 1852. Because Endingen had no church with a tower, it carries the **village clock on its gable**. For a synagogue this is very unusual. Before 1750, the Jews had to bury their dead on a small **island in the Rhine** near Koblenz. After that the cemetery between the villages came into being, today the **oldest surviving Jewish cemetery in Switzerland**.

Only in the 19th century did the situation change. After a **popular vote**, Jews were allowed to settle freely all over Switzerland from **1866**. With the Federal Constitution of 1874 they also received full freedom of belief. After that many families moved to towns such as Baden and Zurich. Today a **Jewish cultural trail** leads through the two villages and explains their history.

gewusst: The Jews from these villages were often called “Surbtal Jews”.
The Surb, after which the valley is named, is a tributary of the Aare.

teile.einleitung: A hongbao is a red envelope with money in it. It is given in China and other countries above all at Chinese New Year. It is meant to bring good fortune for the new year.
wichtigste: Hongbao means “red packet”.
In the red envelope there is money.
Usually older relatives give children a hongbao.
It is given and received politely with both hands.
Eight is regarded as a lucky number, four is avoided.
Today many people send digital hongbao with their phones.

abschnitte.text: **Hongbao** means **“red packet”** in Chinese. In some regions, for example in Hong Kong, it is also called **lai see**. In the red envelope there is **money**. Red is regarded in China as the colour of good fortune and is meant to keep misfortune away. The envelopes are often decorated with golden characters or pictures, for example with the animal of the new year.

Most hongbao are given at **Chinese New Year**, the Spring Festival. Older relatives give them to the **children**. In return the children wish them a good new year. Red envelopes are also given at weddings or birthdays. You give and receive the envelope with **both hands**. This shows respect. Often you do not open it right away in front of the giver.

With the amount, people pay attention to numbers. The **eight** sounds similar in Chinese to “getting rich”. That is why it counts as a **lucky number**. The **four**, by contrast, sounds similar to the word for “death”. That is why you do not give amounts with a four. Many people get new, clean banknotes at the bank before the festival.

Today many people in China send **digital red envelopes**. This works with apps on the **phone**. In this way you can send a hongbao to relatives and friends far away too. In group chats it is popular to distribute an amount that everyone can quickly grab. In Switzerland too, Chinese families celebrate the New Year festival with red envelopes.

gewusst: Every year, billions of digital hongbao are sent around Chinese New Year.
Chinese New Year falls on a different date every year between late January and mid February.

teile.einleitung: We know about the **druids** of Gaul mainly from the work **“De bello Gallico”** by Gaius Julius Caesar. In it he describes in detail their position, their training and their teaching. Caesar was, however, a conqueror who wrote for a Roman audience.
wichtigste: Caesar describes the druids in “De bello Gallico”.
For some pupils the training lasted up to 20 years.
The druids did not write their teaching down.
They taught that after death the soul passes into another person.
Every year they assembled in the territory of the Carnutes.
The severest punishment was exclusion from the sacrifices.
According to Caesar, the teaching came from Britain.

abschnitte.text: From 58 to 50 BC, Gaius Julius Caesar conquered **Gaul**, present-day France and its surroundings. He wrote his work **“De bello Gallico”**, “On the Gallic War”, about this. In the sixth book he describes the society of the Gauls. He names two respected groups: the **druids** and the knights. Because Caesar was a party to the conflict, historians check his statements closely.

Many young men went to the druids as apprentices. According to Caesar, they learned many verses by heart, some for up to **20 years**. The druids **did not write down** their teaching, although they knew Greek letters for other purposes. Caesar gives two reasons: the knowledge should not become public, and the pupils should train their **memory**. Druids did not have to do military service or pay taxes.

As the most important teaching, Caesar names that the **soul does not die**. After death it passes into another person. This, he says, made the Gauls brave, because they feared death less. Besides this, the druids taught about the stars, the size of the world, nature and the power of the gods. According to Caesar, their teaching came from **Britain**. Anyone who wanted to learn it thoroughly travelled there.

The druids decided almost all disputes, over inheritances, boundaries and crimes. Every year they assembled at a sacred place in the territory of the **Carnutes**, roughly in the middle of Gaul. Everyone who had a dispute came there. At the head stood a chief druid. Whoever did not accept a judgement was **excluded from the sacrifices**. This was the severest punishment: nobody wanted to have anything to do with him any more.

gewusst: The territory of the Carnutes lay around the present-day French towns of Chartres and Orléans.
Under Roman rule the druids lost their power in the 1st century AD.

teile.einleitung: Prayer flags are colourful cloth flags with prayers and good wishes printed on them. They come from Tibet and often flutter high in the mountains of the Himalayas. According to belief, the wind carries the good wishes out into the world.
wichtigste: Prayer flags come from Tibetan Buddhism.
They are seen especially often in the Himalayas, on passes, bridges and mountains.
Tibetan prayer flags have five colours: blue, white, red, green and yellow.
Each colour stands for something from nature.
On many flags a wind horse is printed.
The wind is meant to carry the good wishes onwards.

abschnitte.text: **Prayer flags** come from **Tibet** and belong to Tibetan Buddhism. They often hang on long strings between trees, houses or rocks. In the **Himalayas** you see them especially on **passes**, **bridges** and mountain summits. On the flags are prayers, good wishes and holy signs. According to belief, the **wind** carries these good wishes to all beings in the whole world.

Tibetan prayer flags have **five colours**. They always hang in the same order: **blue, white, red, green and yellow**. Each colour stands for something from nature. Blue stands for the **sky**, white for the **air** and the wind, red for **fire**, green for **water** and yellow for the **earth**. Together they are meant to bring balance and harmony.

In the middle of many flags a **horse** is printed, the **wind horse**. In Tibetan it is called **lungta**. On its back the horse carries a jewel, which means good fortune. It is meant to spread the good wishes as fast as the wind. That is why the flags are sometimes simply called wind-horse flags.

Prayer flags are not taken down when they get old. They are left hanging until **wind and weather** bleach and tear them. This is regarded as a good sign, because the prayers have then gone out into the world. Then new flags are hung beside them. Many mountaineers bring prayer flags back from the Himalayas. That is why they sometimes flutter at **mountain huts** in the Swiss Alps too.

gewusst: Besides the horizontal strings of flags, there are also tall vertical prayer flags on a pole.
According to custom, prayer flags should never be laid on the ground.

teile.einleitung: Yom Kippur is the highest holiday in Judaism. In English it is called the Day of Atonement. People fast, pray and think about their own mistakes.
wichtigste: Yom Kippur means Day of Atonement.
Adults fast for about 25 hours.
Small children and the sick do not have to fast.
Many people wear white clothing on this day.
At the end the shofar, a ram’s horn, is blown.
Yom Kippur is ten days after the Jewish New Year.

abschnitte.text: **Yom Kippur** is the most important holiday in Judaism. In English it is called the **Day of Atonement**. On this day people think about the mistakes of the past year. They ask God for forgiveness and make peace with other people. Anyone who has wronged someone should first ask them for forgiveness.

Yom Kippur has a fixed place in the Jewish calendar. Ten days earlier, the Jewish New Year **Rosh Hashanah** is celebrated on the first day of the month of Tishrei. Yom Kippur follows on the **tenth day**. The time in between is often called the Ten Days of Awe. They serve for reflection and turning back.

Most adults **fast** on Yom Kippur. They eat and drink nothing all day. The fast begins the evening before at sunset and ends the next evening. So it lasts about **25 hours**. **Small children and the sick** do not have to fast, because health is more important. Many spend the day praying in the **synagogue**.

Many people wear **white clothing** on Yom Kippur. White stands for purity and a new beginning. At the end of the day the **shofar** sounds in the synagogue. It is usually a hollowed-out **ram’s horn** and one of the oldest musical instruments. With its sound the Day of Atonement ends, and people eat together.

gewusst: In Israel almost no cars drive on Yom Kippur; the streets are completely quiet.
The shofar is one of the oldest musical instruments still played today.

teile.einleitung: Cargo cults are religious movements that arose mainly in Melanesia in the South Pacific. Their followers hoped that valuable goods, the “cargo”, would come to them from the ancestors or from supernatural powers.
wichtigste: Most cargo cults arose in Melanesia, for example in New Guinea, Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands.
They were reactions to the encounter with the goods and power of the colonial rulers.
The Vailala Madness of 1919 in Papua New Guinea is regarded as one of the first cargo cults.
The John Frum movement arose on the island of Tanna in Vanuatu and celebrates on 15 February.
Some followers built imitation airstrips and radio towers.
In 1974 Richard Feynman coined the term “cargo cult science”.

abschnitte.text: The English word **cargo** means freight. When Europeans and Americans came to the South Pacific, they brought many unfamiliar goods with them. The people of **Melanesia** saw that ships and aeroplanes brought these goods, without the foreigners making them themselves. From this arose movements that hoped the goods would also reach them, often as a gift from the **ancestors**. Experts see in them reactions to the **colonial** encounter with foreign power.

One of the first cargo cults was the **Vailala Madness** of **1919** in Papua New Guinea. Many people fell into a **trembling trance** and expected a ship of the ancestors carrying goods. The Australian colonial administration suppressed the movement. Later, similar movements arose on many islands.

In the **Second World War**, American troops came to the islands with very many goods. Afterwards, some followers of cargo cults imitated what they had seen. They built **airstrips**, **radio towers** and radio sets out of wood and carried out drill exercises. They hoped that in this way aeroplanes carrying cargo would land again.

On the island of **Tanna** in **Vanuatu**, the **John Frum movement** arose in the late 1930s. It still exists today. On **15 February**, men march with bamboo rifles and the letters “USA” painted on their chests. In some villages on Tanna, **Prince Philip**, the Duke of Edinburgh, was also revered as a divine being. After his death in 2021, the inhabitants held mourning ceremonies.

In **1974**, in a speech at Caltech, the physicist **Richard Feynman** coined the term “**cargo cult science**”. By this he meant research that looks scientific on the outside but does not test honestly. As with the imitation airstrips, only the outward forms are copied, and the hoped-for result does not appear. The term is still used today.

gewusst: The villagers on Tanna believed that Prince Philip was the son of a mountain spirit who had gone across the sea.
The name “John Frum” is only known from the movement itself; whether a real person of that name ever existed is unclear.

teile.einleitung: In Hinduism, Brahma is the god of creation. Together with Vishnu and Shiva he forms the Trimurti, the triad of gods. Despite his important role, he is rarely worshipped today.
wichtigste: In the Trimurti, Brahma creates the world, Vishnu preserves it and Shiva destroys it.
Brahma is usually shown with four heads.
His mount is the hamsa, a swan or a goose.
His consort is Saraswati, the goddess of wisdom and the arts.
According to one legend, he appears in a lotus flower growing from Vishnu’s navel.
The most famous Brahma temple stands in Pushkar in Rajasthan.

abschnitte.text: In Hinduism there is the **Trimurti**, the triad of three great gods. **Brahma** is the **creator**, who creates the world. **Vishnu** preserves it, and **Shiva** destroys it so that something new can arise. In this way an eternal cycle of coming into being and passing away arises.

In most pictures Brahma has **four heads**. They look in all four directions. He also often has four arms and a beard. His mount is the **hamsa**, a **swan** or a goose. The hamsa is seen as a sign of purity and wisdom. His consort is **Saraswati**, the goddess of wisdom, music and the arts.

A well-known legend tells of how Brahma came into being. Vishnu rests on the primeval ocean. From his **navel** grows a **lotus flower**. In this flower Brahma appears and begins to create the world. In Hinduism the lotus is an important symbol of purity and new beginnings.

Although Brahma is important as the creator, he is **hardly worshipped** in everyday life. Vishnu and Shiva have many more followers and many more temples. That is why there are only very few temples to Brahma in India. The most famous stands in **Pushkar** in the state of **Rajasthan**, beside a sacred lake. Many pilgrims visit it.

gewusst: Brahma must not be confused with “Brahman”: in philosophy, Brahman is the impersonal reality that underlies everything.
At the lake in Pushkar there are many steps on which pilgrims go down into the water.

teile.einleitung: The Golden Rule is a simple rule for living together: treat others as you want to be treated yourself. It is found in many different religions and also outside religions. That is why it connects many people all over the world.
wichtigste: The Golden Rule says: treat others as you want to be treated.
A well-known German proverb runs: “Do not do to others what you would not want done to you.”
Forms of the Golden Rule exist in many religions.
Jesus says it in the Sermon on the Mount.
Confucius and Rabbi Hillel also taught something similar.
It is called “golden” because it is regarded as especially valuable.

abschnitte.text: The **Golden Rule** calls on us to **put ourselves in the place** of others. What I wish for myself, I should give to others too. What I would not want to experience myself, I should not do to others either. In German it is known as a proverb: **“Do not do to others what you would not want done to you.”** It is called “golden” because it is as **valuable** as gold.

Similar sentences exist in **Judaism**, **Christianity**, **Islam**, **Hinduism** and **Buddhism**. People without a religion also consider the rule important. In the Bible, **Jesus** says in the **Sermon on the Mount** in the Gospel of Matthew: “Do to others what you would have them do to you.” The Jewish teacher **Rabbi Hillel** lived about 2,000 years ago in Jerusalem. He said: what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbour. That is the whole Torah, and the rest is explanation.

Already about **2,500 years ago**, the Chinese teacher **Confucius** taught something similar. He said: what you do not wish for yourself, do not do to others. Confucius lived in China and thought a great deal about how people can live well together. His teachings shape China and other countries in Asia to this day.

The Golden Rule helps at school and at home too. Anyone who does not want to be **laughed at** does not laugh at others. When a child is **new in the class**, you can greet them in a friendly way, just as you would like to be greeted yourself. Anyone who wants to be listened to also listens to others. In this way living together becomes more pleasant for everyone.

gewusst: The name “Golden Rule” is only a few hundred years old; the idea itself is much older.
The Golden Rule exists in two forms: as a call to do good, and as a call to refrain from doing bad.

teile.einleitung: Bern Minster is the largest late Gothic church in Switzerland. Its tower is the tallest church tower in the country. The largest bell in Switzerland also hangs in the minster.
wichtigste: Building of Bern Minster began in 1421.
The tower was only finished in 1893.
At about 100 metres it is the tallest church tower in Switzerland.
The Great Bell was cast in 1611 and weighs almost 10 tonnes.
It is the largest bell in Switzerland.
Above the main doorway the Last Judgement is shown.
The minster is part of Bern’s old town, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: Building of **Bern Minster** began in **1421**. The church was built in the **late Gothic** style. Many generations worked on it. The tower was only completed in **1893**, over 470 years after building began. The minster is regarded as the largest late Gothic church in Switzerland.

The tower of Bern Minster is about **100 metres** high. That makes it the **tallest church tower in Switzerland**. You can climb up it by more than 300 steps. At the top there is a wide view over the old town, the Aare and, in good weather, as far as the Bernese Alps. Bern’s old town is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

In the tower hangs the **Great Bell**. It was cast in **1611** and weighs almost **10 tonnes**. That makes it the **largest bell in Switzerland**. It rings only on special occasions, for example on major holy days. Its deep sound can be heard far across the city.

Above the main doorway, the **Last Judgement** is shown in many stone figures. According to Christian belief, Christ judges all people at the end of time. The figures show the good on one side and the wicked on the other. Since the **Reformation** of 1528 the minster has been a **Protestant** church. Next to the minster lies the **Münsterplattform**, a popular park high above the Aare.

gewusst: The tower of Bern Minster was only finished more than 470 years after building began.
The Great Bell weighs almost as much as two elephants.

teile.einleitung: Hanami is a Japanese custom: in spring people look at the blossoming cherry trees and celebrate beneath them. All over Japan, people look forward to it every year.
wichtigste: Hanami means “looking at blossoms”.
People admire above all the cherry blossom.
Cherry blossoms are called sakura in Japanese.
Many families have a picnic under the trees.
The blossoms are mostly pink or white.
The blossom lasts only about one to two weeks.
In the south the trees blossom first, in the north on Hokkaido not until May.

abschnitte.text: The word **hanami** consists of “hana”, flower, and “mi”, to look. So hanami means **looking at blossoms**. What is meant above all is the cherry blossom, in Japanese **sakura**. The cherry blossom is one of the most popular flowers in Japan. It is delicate pink or white, and whole parks then glow brightly.

At hanami, families, friends and colleagues sit on blankets under the blossoming trees. They eat, drink and celebrate together. In popular parks, some people secure a good spot as early as the morning. Many also visit the trees in the evening, when they are lit by lanterns. This is called **yozakura**, cherry blossoms at night.

The cherry trees blossom in **spring**. In the warm south of Japan they begin first. In Tokyo it is usually the end of March or the beginning of April. In the cold north, on **Hokkaido**, they do not blossom until May. On television and on the internet, people follow every year how the blossom moves from south to north.

The cherry blossom lasts only briefly, about **one to two weeks**. Then the petals fall to the ground like snow. For many people in Japan this is a sign that beautiful things do not last for ever. That is why people enjoy the blossom all the more consciously. The custom is over a thousand years old and was once cultivated at the imperial court.

gewusst: Before the cherry became popular, people in Japan admired above all the blossoms of the plum.
In 1912 Japan gave the city of Washington about 3,000 cherry trees; there is now a cherry blossom festival of its own there.

teile.einleitung: **Dionysus** was the god of wine, intoxication and growing nature in ancient Greece. The worship of him is called the **cult of Dionysus**. From his festivals in Athens came the theatre as we still know it today.
wichtigste: Dionysus is the son of Zeus and Semele.
His ecstatic female followers were called maenads.
His staff with a pine cone and ivy is called a thyrsus.
His retinue includes the satyrs, hybrid creatures with horses’ tails.
From the festivals for Dionysus in Athens came tragedy.
The Romans called him Bacchus. In 186 BC the Senate sharply restricted the Bacchanalia.

abschnitte.text: According to the myth, Dionysus is the son of the father of the gods, **Zeus**, and the king’s daughter **Semele**. Semele was a mortal. That is why Dionysus was seen as a god who stands between gods and humans. He brought people **wine**. But he also stood for joy, dance, transformation and the power of nature, which grows anew every year.

Dionysus travelled about with a wild retinue. It included the **maenads**, ecstatic women who danced and sang. They are also called **bacchae**. Then came the **satyrs**, hybrid creatures with horses’ tails and pointed ears. Typical is the **thyrsus**, a staff with ivy and a pine cone at the top. Ivy and vine leaves were his plants.

In **Athens**, great festivals for Dionysus, the **Dionysia**, were celebrated every year. Choruses appeared and sang for the god. From this developed **tragedy** and later comedy too. Poets such as Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides wrote plays for these festivals. The great theatre at the foot of the Acropolis was called the **Theatre of Dionysus**.

The poet **Euripides** wrote the tragedy **“The Bacchae”**. In it, King **Pentheus** of Thebes refuses to recognise Dionysus as a god. He wants to ban the cult. The play ends very badly for Pentheus. It shows that, according to Greek belief, one does not reject a god without being punished.

The Romans called the god **Bacchus**. His nocturnal celebrations were called the **Bacchanalia**. In 186 BC the Roman **Senate** regarded these celebrations as dangerous to the state. It issued a decree that sharply restricted the Bacchanalia. Small celebrations were only permitted with authorisation. The historian **Livy** reports on this.

gewusst: The word “tragedy” probably literally means “goat song”.
An inscription with the Senate’s decree of 186 BC has survived to this day and is kept in Vienna.

teile.einleitung: Athena was one of the most important goddesses of the ancient Greeks. She was the goddess of wisdom and the protector of the city of Athens. Her symbol is the owl, which still stands for cleverness today.
wichtigste: Athena was the goddess of wisdom and clever plans.
Her sacred animal was the owl.
The city of Athens is named after her.
According to legend, she sprang from the head of her father Zeus.
She gave the Athenians an olive tree.
Her most famous temple is the Parthenon on the Acropolis.
The Greek 1 euro coin shows an owl.

abschnitte.text: **Athena** was the goddess of wisdom and clever plans. She also helped craftspeople, for example with weaving and pottery. Her sacred animal was the **owl**, which was seen as a sign of cleverness. She is often shown with **helmet, shield and spear**. She protected the city in war, but stood for thoughtful action and not for wild violence.

The legend tells an unusual story about Athena’s birth. She sprang from the **head of her father Zeus**, the chief god. She was already wearing armour. Athena was Zeus’s favourite daughter. The Romans had a similar goddess called **Minerva**.

According to the legend, Athena and the sea god **Poseidon** quarrelled over who should protect the city. Each was to give the people a gift. Poseidon made a spring of salt water gush forth. Athena gave an **olive tree**, and the people chose her. That is why the city of **Athens** bears her name, and it is now the capital of Greece.

On the **Acropolis**, a hill in Athens, stands the **Parthenon**. This temple was built for Athena in the 5th century BC. In it once stood a large statue of the goddess made of gold and ivory. Even today Athena can be seen in Greece: the Greek **1 euro coin** shows an owl. The picture comes from an old coin of Athens.

gewusst: The owl on the Greek 1 euro coin is copied from a coin that is over 2,400 years old.
Athena was often also called “Pallas Athena”.

teile.einleitung: Bhakti is a Sanskrit word that means loving devotion to God. In Hinduism, bhakti is a way of coming close to God not mainly through knowledge or rituals, but through love, prayer and song.
wichtigste: Bhakti means loving devotion to a deity such as Krishna, Rama or Shiva.
The bhakti movement began between the 6th and 9th centuries in the Tamil south of India.
The Tamil poets were called Alvars (Vishnu) and Nayanars (Shiva).
Well-known bhakti poets are Kabir, Mirabai and Tulsidas.
In the 16th century, Chaitanya made the communal singing of Krishna’s name popular in Bengal.
Bhakti was open to all, including women and people of low castes.

abschnitte.text: **Bhakti** means loving devotion. It refers to a personal, heartfelt relationship with a deity. Many believers revere **Krishna**, **Rama** or **Shiva**. They pray, sing songs and think of God again and again. What matters is not how learned someone is, but how sincere their love is.

The bhakti movement began in the **Tamil south** of India. Between the 6th and 9th centuries, poets travelled from temple to temple and sang songs in their own language. The **Alvars** revered Vishnu, and the **Nayanars** revered Shiva. Their songs are still sung in temples today. From there bhakti gradually spread to the north.

In northern India, many bhakti poets became famous. **Kabir** lived in the 15th century and criticised empty outward show in Hinduism and Islam. He is revered by Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs, and some of his verses are in the holy book of the Sikhs. The Rajput princess **Mirabai** sang songs to Krishna in the 16th century. **Tulsidas** wrote the **Ramcharitmanas**, the story of Rama in the everyday language Awadhi instead of Sanskrit.

In the 16th century, the Bengali saint **Chaitanya** spread the communal singing of Krishna’s name. This singing is called **kirtan**. Chaitanya is regarded as the founder of Gaudiya Vaishnavism. The **Hare Krishna movement** (ISKCON), founded in New York in 1966, also draws on this tradition. Its followers also sing in the streets of Swiss cities.

The bhakti movement was also important socially. Many of its saints came from low **castes** or were women. They taught that true devotion matters more than birth, education or expensive rituals. Because the songs were sung in everyday languages, everyone could understand them. In this way bhakti became one of the most important currents in Hinduism.

gewusst: Kabir’s verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib, the holy book of the Sikhs, although Kabir was not a Sikh.
Mirabai’s songs have been sung in northern India for about 500 years.
The Hare Krishna movement, which became known worldwide, has its roots in the bhakti tradition of Bengal.

teile.einleitung: A fire temple is the house of worship of the Zoroastrians. Inside it burns a sacred fire that is never supposed to go out. Zoroastrianism is a very old religion from the area of present-day Iran.
wichtigste: Zoroastrianism goes back to the prophet Zarathustra.
In the fire temple a sacred fire burns without interruption.
The fire is a sign of purity and of the light of God; it is not itself worshipped as God.
The highest grade of a sacred fire is called Atash Behram.
Priests wear a mouth cloth called a padan in front of the fire.
Famous fire temples stand in Yazd in Iran and in Udvada in India.

abschnitte.text: The Zoroastrians worship one God, whom they call **Ahura Mazda**. For them fire is a sign of **purity** and of the light of God. When they pray, they turn towards the fire or another source of light. But they do not worship the fire as God. The fire reminds them of goodness, of truth and of light.

At the heart of every fire temple is a room with a large vessel in which the **sacred fire** burns. Priests keep it burning day and night. They often add **sandalwood**, which smells pleasant. Visitors too bring sandalwood as an offering. In front of the fire, the priests wear a cloth over the mouth, the **padan**. In this way their breath is not to make the pure fire unclean.

Not every sacred fire is equally important. The highest grade is called **Atash Behram**, which means “victorious fire”. For its consecration, fires from many different sources are collected and purified in long ceremonies. Below it there are simpler grades of fire for smaller temples. An Atash Behram exists in only a few places in the world.

The city of **Yazd** in Iran is a centre of the Zoroastrians. In the fire temple there, a fire burns that, according to tradition, has not gone out for about 1,500 years. Long ago many Zoroastrians moved to India, where they are called **Parsis**. Their most important fire, the **Iranshah fire**, was consecrated in Sanjan in the 8th century. Since 1742 it has burned in the town of **Udvada** in the state of Gujarat.

gewusst: The Iranshah fire is regarded as the oldest continuously burning sacred fire of the Parsis.
In many Parsi fire temples in India, only Zoroastrians may enter the inner part.

teile.einleitung: The hamsa is a protective hand with five fingers. It is known in Judaism, in Islam and in many countries around the Mediterranean. It is meant to keep misfortune and the evil eye away.
wichtigste: The hamsa is a hand with five fingers.
It is regarded as a protective sign against misfortune.
In the middle an eye is often shown.
The eye is meant to ward off the evil eye.
The hamsa often hangs on walls, doors or on chains.

abschnitte.text: The **hamsa** looks like an open hand with five fingers. Often the thumb and little finger are shaped the same, so that the hand looks almost like its own mirror image. The name comes from the Arabic word for **five**. Many people believe that the hand **keeps misfortune away**. It is hung on walls, above doors, in the car, or worn as a pendant on a chain.

In the middle of the hand an **eye** is often painted. It is meant to ward off the **evil eye**. This refers to the old belief that envious looks could harm others. The hamsa is often decorated in blue, because blue is regarded as a protective colour in many countries.

The hamsa is a very old sign and is used in both religions. In Islam it is sometimes called the **Hand of Fatima**, after the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad. In Judaism people also speak of the **Hand of Miriam**, after the sister of Moses. Many scholars see it more as a folk custom than as a religious requirement. Today it is also simply a popular piece of jewellery.

gewusst: In Israel, Morocco and Tunisia, the hamsa is seen very often in markets, on houses and as jewellery.

teile.einleitung: Kabbalah is a mystical teaching in Judaism. It asks about the hidden side of God and about how God works in the world. Its most important writings arose in the Middle Ages.
wichtigste: Kabbalah literally means “tradition”.
It calls the infinite, unknowable God Ein Sof.
According to the Kabbalah, God works through ten emanations, the sefirot.
An important book is the Zohar from the 13th century.
Isaac Luria taught in Safed in the 16th century.
Tzimtzum is, for Luria, God’s withdrawal to make room for creation.

abschnitte.text: The Hebrew word **Kabbalah** means “**tradition**”. It comes from the verb “kibbel”, which means to receive. What is meant is a received teaching about the hidden side of God. The Kabbalah is a form of **mysticism**. Mysticism is the attempt to experience God in a wholly inward and direct way.

God in his hidden nature is called **Ein Sof** in the Kabbalah, which means “without end”. For human beings he is unknowable. But he reveals himself through ten emanations, the **sefirot**. They are often shown as a **tree of life**. They include, for example, Keter (crown), Chochma (wisdom) and Malchut (kingship).

A particularly important work of the Kabbalah is the **Zohar**, the “Book of Splendour”. It arose in the 13th century in **Spain**. The Zohar interprets the Torah in a mysterious way. Every word is said to have a deeper, hidden meaning. The book became very influential for many centuries.

After the expulsion of the Jews from Spain in 1492, **Safed** in Galilee became a centre of the Kabbalah. There in the 16th century **Isaac Luria**, called the Ari, taught. According to his teaching, God first withdrew into himself, so that anything else could come into being at all. He calls this withdrawal **tzimtzum**. **Tikkun**, by contrast, refers to the repair of the world, in which human beings are also meant to take part.

gewusst: The name “Ari” for Isaac Luria means “lion” in Hebrew.
The ten sefirot are often drawn as a tree with branches.

teile.einleitung: Saint Barbara of Nicomedia is a Christian saint from the time of the early persecutions of Christians. Her life is known mainly from legends. She is regarded as the protector of miners and tunnel builders and is very well known in Switzerland too.
wichtigste: Barbara is said to have lived in the 3rd century.
Her life is handed down mainly through legends.
She is regarded as the patron saint of miners and tunnel builders.
Her feast day is 4 December.
On St Barbara’s Day, people cut branches that are meant to bloom by Christmas.
During the building of the Gotthard Base Tunnel, a figure of Barbara stood at the entrance.

abschnitte.text: According to the legend, **Barbara** lived in the 3rd century in Nicomedia, in the area of present-day Turkey. Her father is said to have shut her in a **tower**. There Barbara became a Christian. She had a third window built into the tower, as a sign of the **Trinity** of God. Because she stayed true to her faith, she was killed and has been regarded as a **martyr** ever since.

Saint Barbara is regarded as the protector of **miners** and **tunnel builders**. These people work underground and are often in danger. They ask Barbara for protection from accidents. During the building of the **Gotthard Base Tunnel** too, a figure of Saint Barbara stood at the entrance. She is still revered in many tunnel construction projects in Switzerland.

The feast day of Saint Barbara is **4 December**. On this day, many people cut branches, for example from a cherry tree, and put them in a vase of water. The **Barbara branches** are supposed to bloom by **Christmas**. Blossoming branches are seen as a good sign. In this way they bring a piece of spring into the house in the middle of winter.

Barbara is one of the **Fourteen Holy Helpers**, a group of saints who are called upon in times of need. In pictures she often carries a **tower**, a chalice or a crown. Besides the miners, artillerymen and other dangerous occupations are also among those she protects. Because little is known for certain about her real life, her feast day was removed from the general Roman calendar in 1969. She is still revered, however.

gewusst: The name Barbara originally means “the foreign woman”.
Saint Barbara belongs to the group of the Fourteen Holy Helpers.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Freethinkers Association is a society for people who live without religion. It campaigns for a clear separation of state and church. Its roots go back more than a hundred years.
wichtigste: A forerunner was founded in Zurich on 12 April 1908.
The association campaigns for the separation of state and church.
It helps people with sample letters when they leave a church.
Since 2010 it has published the magazine “frei denken”.
Since 2011 it has held the Denkfest about every three years.
It is a member of Humanists International.

abschnitte.text: **Freethinkers** are people who do not base their lives on a religion. On questions about the world they want to rely on **reason** and **science**. Many of them also call themselves **humanists** or secular. “Secular” means worldly, that is, not religious. Freethinkers believe that everyone should be free to decide what they believe.

On **12 April 1908** the German-Swiss Freethinkers’ League was founded in **Zurich**. This date counts as the official founding date of today’s association. For a long time its magazine was called “Der Schweizer Freidenker”. Since **2010** the quarterly **“frei denken”** has appeared in three national languages. A quarterly appears four times a year.

The freethinkers campaign for the **separation of state and church**. In many Swiss cantons, certain churches are recognised as **established churches** and receive money from the state. The freethinkers criticise this. They support people who want to leave a church with explanations and **sample letters**. In Lucerne and in Valais they opposed public money for the new barracks of the **Swiss Guard** in the Vatican. The churches and other groups often see such questions differently.

Since **2011** the association has held the **Denkfest** about every three years. Scientists and people from the arts appear there. It is the association’s biggest event. The freethinkers are a member of **Humanists International**, the world federation of humanist organisations. Since 23 June 2024, Sonja Stocker and Valentin Abgottspon have led the association as co-presidents (as of 2024). Their predecessor Andreas Kyriacou was president from 2013 to 2024.

gewusst: The magazine “frei denken” appears in German, French and Italian.
The Freethinkers Association is also the sponsoring association of the Humanist Press Service.

teile.einleitung: A grave light is a candle that burns on a grave. With the light, people show that they are thinking of someone who has died. The custom is widespread above all in Christianity, but other religions also have memorial candles.
wichtigste: A grave light is a candle on a grave.
It shows that you are thinking of the person who has died.
The light is regarded as a sign of hope.
Grave lights usually stand in a glass or cup with a lid.
Especially many grave lights burn around All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day.

abschnitte.text: Many people place a **candle** on the grave of a loved one. The burning flame shows: we are thinking of you. For Christians the light is also a sign of **hope** for a life after death. Grave lights usually stand in a red or clear cup with a lid. In this way the flame is protected from wind and rain, and the candle can burn for a long time.

abschnitte.titel: All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day
abschnitte.text: On 1 November it is **All Saints’ Day**, on 2 November **All Souls’ Day**. On these days many Catholic families visit the graves of their relatives. They decorate them and light candles. In Catholic regions of Switzerland, the cemeteries then often glow in a warm light in the evening.

In Judaism too there are memorial candles. On the anniversary of a death, the **yahrzeit**, a candle is lit at home that burns for about a whole day. In many cultures of the world, light and fire are signs of remembrance. Today there are also electric grave lights that glow with a battery.

gewusst: In Poland the custom is especially strong: on All Saints’ Day countless lights burn in the cemeteries there.

teile.einleitung: Kashrut is the name for the Jewish dietary laws. They lay down which foods are permitted and how they are prepared. Permitted foods are called kosher.
wichtigste: Kosher originally means “fit” or “suitable”.
Permitted land animals have split hooves and chew the cud.
Permitted water creatures have fins and scales.
Meat and milk are strictly kept separate.
Neutral foods such as eggs, fruit and vegetables are called pareve.
A seal of approval on the packaging is called a hechsher.

abschnitte.text: The Jewish dietary laws are called **kashrut**. They go back to rules in the **Torah**, the most important part of the Hebrew Bible. The word **kosher** comes from the Hebrew “kasher” and means “fit” or “suitable”. What is meant is food that is permitted according to the rules. How strictly someone follows the rules differs from family to family.

Among land animals, only mammals that have **split hooves** and **chew the cud** are permitted. Cattle, sheep and goats meet both conditions, pigs do not. For water creatures, **fins and scales** are needed. That is why salmon and trout are kosher, but prawns and mussels are not. Eating **blood** is forbidden in the Torah.

The Torah forbids boiling a kid in its mother’s milk. From this arose the rule to keep **meat and dairy products** strictly apart. Many families even have separate crockery for this. Neutral foods such as eggs, fruit or vegetables are called **pareve**. They may be eaten with both kinds of meal.

Wine and grape juice count as kosher only if they were made under **Jewish supervision**. One reason is that wine was once used in sacrifices to other gods. On many packages there is a sign, the **hechsher**. It confirms that a rabbi’s supervision has checked the ingredients and the production.

Ritual slaughter is called **shechita**. In it the animal is killed with a very sharp knife so that the blood drains out. In Switzerland, slaughter without prior stunning has been forbidden since **1893**. This rule got into the constitution through the first **popular initiative** of the Confederation to be accepted. Kosher meat is therefore imported from abroad.

gewusst: The very first popular initiative accepted in Switzerland, in 1893, concerned ritual slaughter.
Salmon is kosher, prawns are not, because they lack fins and scales.

teile.einleitung: The caste system is an ancient social order in India. It divides people into groups by their birth. Today the Indian constitution forbids discrimination because of caste, but in everyday life it still plays a part.
wichtigste: The classical order has four main classes, the varnas.
Varna literally means “colour”.
At the top stood the Brahmins, priests and scholars.
Kshatriyas were warriors and rulers, Vaishyas traders and farmers.
In everyday life, the caste system consists of thousands of jatis.
Those once excluded as “untouchables” today call themselves Dalits.
Since 1950 the Indian constitution has forbidden untouchability.

abschnitte.text: The classical Indian social order has **four varnas**, that is, main classes. The Sanskrit word **varna** literally means “colour”. The division is already mentioned in very old texts such as the **Rigveda**. Later the caste system arose from it. You were born into your class and could hardly change it.

At the top stood the **Brahmins**, the priests and scholars. Next came the **Kshatriyas**, the princes and warriors, who were to protect and govern the land. The hero Rama from the epic Ramayana was also a Kshatriya. The **Vaishyas** were responsible for trade, farming and cattle breeding. The fourth class, the **Shudras**, was to serve the others.

In everyday life the caste system does not consist of only four classes. There are many thousands of groups called **jatis**. Often they are connected with a particular trade. You are born into a jati. In the past it determined whom you could marry and with whom you could eat.

Some people stood entirely outside the four varnas. They were formerly called “**untouchables**” and were strongly excluded. Today they call themselves **Dalits**, which means roughly “oppressed”. A well-known fighter for their rights was **Bhimrao Ambedkar**, himself a Dalit. He played a decisive part in the Indian constitution.

The constitution of the Republic of India came into force in **1950**. It forbids **untouchability** and discrimination because of caste. For disadvantaged groups there are reserved places at universities and in offices. Even so, caste still plays a part, especially in the countryside. The best ways to greater equality are still debated in India today.

gewusst: The word “caste” does not come from India, but from Portuguese.
Bhimrao Ambedkar, a Dalit, is regarded as one of the fathers of the Indian constitution.

teile.einleitung: Chinese New Year is the most important festival in China. There it is also called the Spring Festival. Because the Chinese calendar follows the moon, it falls on a different day every year.
wichtigste: Chinese New Year is also called the Spring Festival in China.
It always falls between 21 January and 20 February.
The date depends on the moon.
Red is the colour of good fortune and is seen everywhere.
Many families eat dumplings called jiaozi.
The celebrations end after 15 days with the Lantern Festival.

abschnitte.text: **Chinese New Year** is also called the **Spring Festival** in China. It is the most important festival of the year. The Chinese calendar follows the **moon**. That is why New Year is on a different day every year. But it always falls between **21 January** and **20 February**. On **17 February 2026**, the **Year of the Horse** began.

Before the festival, many families **clean** the house thoroughly. In this way they sweep the bad luck of the old year out. Then the house is decorated, above all in **red**. In China red is regarded as the colour of **good fortune**. People hang red paper strips with good wishes on the doors. Many people travel home to their families, which is why trains and buses are very full.

On the evening before New Year, the family gathers for a big meal. In northern China, **jiaozi** are part of it, filled dumplings. Their shape recalls old Chinese **coins** and is meant to bring prosperity. Children often get **red envelopes** with money. At midnight there are **fireworks** in many places.

The New Year celebrations last **15 days**. On the 15th day of the new year, people celebrate the **Lantern Festival**. Then glowing **lanterns** hang everywhere. There are parades with lion and dragon dances. In Swiss cities such as Zurich too, Chinese communities celebrate New Year with festivals.

gewusst: Around Chinese New Year, hundreds of millions of people in China travel home every year; it is regarded as the largest regular wave of travel in the world.
Not only in China, but also in Vietnam, Korea and Singapore, the New Year is celebrated according to the lunar calendar.

teile.einleitung: In Shinto, the ancient religion of Japan, kami are divine beings and forces. They can dwell in nature, but are also worshipped in ancestors or important people. For the kami there are countless shrines all over Japan.
wichtigste: In Shinto, kami are divine beings and forces.
According to belief they dwell in mountains, trees, rocks or waterfalls.
People speak of eight million kami, which means: countless.
Sacred places are marked with a straw rope, the shimenawa.
Inari is the kami of rice and prosperity; his messengers are foxes.
The priests at a shrine are called kannushi.
Many people in Japan follow Shinto and Buddhism at the same time.

abschnitte.text: In **Shinto**, **kami** are divine beings and forces. They can dwell in natural phenomena, for example in **mountains**, waterfalls, old **trees** or **rocks**. The sun goddess Amaterasu is also a kami. A Japanese saying speaks of “yaoyorozu no kami”, the **eight million kami**. The number simply means “countless”.

Trees or rocks in which a kami dwells are marked with a braided rope of rice straw. This rope is called a **shimenawa**. From it often hang white strips of paper in zigzag shapes. The entrance to a shrine is shown by a gate, the **torii**. Whoever walks through it enters a sacred area.

One of the most popular kami is **Inari**. He is responsible for **rice**, the fertility of the fields and **prosperity**. Thousands of shrines in Japan are dedicated to Inari. In front of them there are often stone figures of **foxes**. The foxes are regarded as messengers of the kami.

At a Shinto shrine, priests look after the kami. They are called **kannushi** and carry out ceremonies. Often they are helped by young women in white and red, the **miko**. Visitors write their wishes on small wooden tablets, the **ema**. They are hung up in the shrine, so that the kami can read the wishes.

In Japan it is usual to keep up the festivals of Shinto and the rituals of **Buddhism** side by side. Many people often follow both at once. People sometimes say: birth in Shinto, funeral in Buddhism. At New Year very many families visit a Shinto shrine. So for many the kami belong to quite ordinary everyday life.

gewusst: “Eight million kami” is not an exact number, but means “countless”.
On many ema wooden tablets the animal of the new year is painted.

teile.einleitung: The Khalsa is the community of initiated Sikhs. It was founded in 1699 by Guru Gobind Singh. Whoever belongs to the Khalsa promises to live by fixed rules and wears special signs.
wichtigste: Khalsa means “pure”.
The Khalsa was founded in 1699 in Anandpur Sahib in the Punjab.
The first five initiated are called the Panj Pyare, “the five beloved”.
Men bear the name Singh, “lion”, and women the name Kaur.
The initiation ceremony is called Amrit Sanchar.
The sweetened water is stirred with a double-edged sword, the Khanda.

abschnitte.text: The word **Khalsa** means “pure”. It is the name of the community of initiated **Sikhs**. It was founded in **1699** by the tenth guru, **Guru Gobind Singh**. The founding took place in **Anandpur Sahib** in the Punjab, a region in the north of India. Today a large gurdwara, a Sikh house of worship, stands there.

At the founding the guru asked who was ready to give his life for the faith. Five men stepped forward one after another. They were the first to be initiated and are called the **Panj Pyare**, “the five beloved”. They came from different castes. In this way the Khalsa showed that before God all are equal.

Male Sikhs bear the name **Singh**, which means “**lion**”. It is meant to show courage and to remove the differences of caste. Women bear the name **Kaur**, which is often translated as “princess”. It stresses their dignity and equality. Because many people bear the same name, it no longer reveals anything about a family’s origin.

The initiation ceremony is called **Amrit Sanchar**. In it sweetened water, the **Amrit**, is stirred with a double-edged sword. This sword is called the **Khanda** and is also part of the Sikh symbol. The initiated drink the Amrit and promise to live by the rules of the Khalsa. These include five signs, such as uncut hair, a comb and a steel bangle.

gewusst: Because Singh means “lion”, very many Sikh men have the same family name.
The first five initiated came from different castes.

teile.einleitung: Corpus Christi is a festival of the Catholic Church. It is always celebrated on a Thursday, 60 days after Easter. Typical are solemn parades through villages and towns, which are called processions.
wichtigste: Corpus Christi is a Catholic festival and always falls on a Thursday.
The festival is 60 days after Easter.
At its centre is a procession, that is, a solemn parade.
The priest carries the monstrance with the host under a canopy.
On the way people stop at decorated altars to pray.
In Catholic cantons of Switzerland, Corpus Christi is a public holiday.

abschnitte.text: In German the name comes from Middle High German: “vrône lîcham” means **“body of the Lord”**. Catholics believe that Jesus is present in the consecrated **host**. On Corpus Christi they celebrate this publicly. The festival was introduced in the 13th century. It always falls on a **Thursday**, 60 days after Easter, and recalls the Last Supper on Maundy Thursday.

A **procession** is a solemn parade. Many people walk through the streets praying and singing. The priest carries the **monstrance**, a golden vessel that shows the host in the middle. Four men carry a **canopy** over him, a cloth roof on poles. Often children, brass bands and societies with banners walk along.

On the way there are **decorated altars** in the open air. The procession stops there. People pray, read from the Bible, and the priest gives the **blessing**. In some places people lay colourful **carpets of flowers** made of blossoms on the street. The procession then passes over these pictures made of flowers. Often many people work on a flower carpet early in the morning.

In many **Catholic cantons** Corpus Christi is a public holiday, for example in Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Zug, Fribourg or Valais. In the Valais **Lötschental**, the **Herrgottsgrenadiere** (“Grenadiers of the Lord”) accompany the procession. They wear old uniforms and tall caps and recall men from the valley who once served in foreign armies. In Reformed cantons Corpus Christi is usually an ordinary working day.

gewusst: Corpus Christi falls on a different date each year, at the earliest in May and at the latest in June.
It is celebrated on a Thursday because, according to the Bible, Jesus held the Last Supper on a Thursday, Maundy Thursday.

teile.einleitung: The Holocaust is the mass murder of about six million Jews in Europe by National Socialist Germany and its helpers. It took place during the Second World War. In Hebrew it is called the Shoah.
wichtigste: In the Holocaust about six million Jews were murdered.
In Hebrew it is called the Shoah, which means catastrophe.
The National Socialists concealed the plan with the word “Final Solution”.
On 27 January 1945 the camp at Auschwitz was liberated.
27 January is today International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
During the war Switzerland turned back many Jewish refugees at the border.
In 1942 Gertrud Kurz spoke up for them as the “mother of refugees”.

abschnitte.text: The Hebrew word **Shoah** means catastrophe or great disaster. Many Jews prefer it to the Greek word **Holocaust**, which means burnt offering. The National Socialists under Adolf Hitler persecuted Jews because they had declared them enemies. During the Second World War they murdered about **six million** Jews. For the plan they used the cover term **“Final Solution of the Jewish Question”**. Other groups were also persecuted, such as Roma and Sinti and sick and disabled people.
