The lawyer **Raphael Lemkin** coined the word **genocide** in 1944. He campaigned for the UN Genocide Convention of 1948. The organiser of the deportations, **Adolf Eichmann**, was captured in Argentina in 1960 and put on trial in Jerusalem in 1961. The philosopher **Hannah Arendt** reported on it. She coined the phrase **“the banality of evil”**: Eichmann struck her as a thoughtless official.

During the war Switzerland took in refugees, but also turned many Jewish refugees back at the border. In August 1942 it largely closed the border to them. Federal Councillor **Eduard von Steiger** compared Switzerland to a full lifeboat. From this came the slogan **“The boat is full”**. The Bernese woman **Gertrud Kurz** pleaded with him for the refugees and became known as the **“mother of refugees”**. A Swiss delegate of the ICRC visited the ghetto of **Theresienstadt** in 1944, which the SS had dressed up as a model camp, and afterwards wrote a glossed-over report.

On **27 January 1945** the Red Army liberated the camp at **Auschwitz-Birkenau**. The UN declared this day **International Holocaust Remembrance Day** in 2005. In Israel there is in addition the day of remembrance **Yom HaShoah** in spring. Then sirens sound across the country, and traffic stops for two minutes. Remembering is meant to help ensure that such a thing never happens again.

gewusst: In 1938 the St Gallen police commander Paul Grüninger let Jewish refugees enter against the rules, and was rehabilitated only long after his death.
The Swiss diplomat Carl Lutz saved tens of thousands of Jews in Budapest with letters of protection.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland tens of thousands of people of Hindu faith live. Most come from Sri Lanka and speak Tamil. They have built temples of their own in several cantons.
wichtigste: Most Hindus in Switzerland come from Sri Lanka.
According to the 2000 census, about 81 per cent of them were Tamils.
Many fled from the 1980s onwards from the civil war in Sri Lanka.
Their mother tongue is usually Tamil.
In the House of Religions in Bern there has been a Hindu temple since 2014.
This temple is dedicated mainly to Shiva and trained women as priestesses.
In Dürnten in the canton of Zurich stands the Sri Vishnu Thurkkai Amman Temple.

abschnitte.text: The largest part of the Hindus in Switzerland come from **Sri Lanka**. According to the 2000 census, about **81 per cent** of them were **Tamils**. In Sri Lanka there was a **civil war** from 1983 to 2009. Many Tamils therefore fled from the 1980s onwards and found refuge in Switzerland. Further Hindus came from India and other countries.

Most Hindus from Sri Lanka speak **Tamil** as their mother tongue. It is a very old language with its own script. It is spoken in southern India and in the north of Sri Lanka. In Switzerland there are Tamil schools where children learn the language, dance and music of their families. Many young Tamils were born in Switzerland and also speak Swiss German dialect.

In the **House of Religions** on Europaplatz in Bern, several religious communities have their rooms. Since 2014 a **Hindu temple** has been part of it. It is run by the association Saivanerikoodam and is dedicated mainly to the god **Shiva**, as is usual among many Tamil Hindus. What was new for Switzerland: here **women were trained as priestesses**.

In Switzerland there are several Hindu temples, often in converted buildings in industrial areas. In **Dürnten** in the canton of Zurich stands the **Sri Vishnu Thurkkai Amman Temple**. It was opened in 2010 in a converted warehouse, because the community had too little space before that in Adliswil. At great temple festivals, the faithful move through the streets with decorated chariots of the gods.

gewusst: At great temple festivals in Switzerland, thousands of people often come together, some from abroad.
A Hindu priestess in the temple was a novelty for the whole of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: A prayer wheel is a cylinder that can be turned. Inside it is paper with prayers. Prayer wheels are especially important in Tibetan Buddhism.
wichtigste: A prayer wheel is turned while you think of good wishes.
It is turned clockwise.
Inside is a roll of paper on which a prayer is written many times.
The best-known prayer on it is “Om mani padme hum”.
Prayer wheels come mainly from Tibet and are also widespread in Nepal and Bhutan.
Some large prayer wheels are driven by a stream.

abschnitte.text: A **prayer wheel** is a cylinder of metal or wood that turns on an axis. Inside it is a tightly wound roll of **paper**. On it a prayer is written very many times. According to belief, each turn counts like a **spoken prayer**. The wheel is always turned **clockwise**, so that the prayer is read in the right order.

On many prayer wheels is the prayer **“Om mani padme hum”**. It is a **mantra**, that is, a short holy formula that is repeated again and again. It wishes **compassion** for all beings. The syllables are often written on the outside of the wheel in beautiful Tibetan letters. Many Buddhists say the mantra quietly while they turn the wheel.

There are small prayer wheels with a **handle**. You hold them in one hand and make them circle, helped by a small weight on a chain. At many **temples** there are long rows of prayer wheels along the wall. People walk along them and turn each one. Some prayer wheels are as big as a room and are turned by several people.

In the mountains some prayer wheels stand over a **stream**. The flowing **water** turns them without a break. There are also prayer wheels that are moved by the **wind** or by the warm air above a candle. In this way, according to belief, they pray day and night. Prayer wheels are seen above all in **Tibet**, **Nepal** and **Bhutan**.

gewusst: Some prayer wheels contain the mantra many thousands of times on tiny, closely written paper.
Even today there are prayer wheels driven by a small electric motor.

teile.einleitung: “Grüss Gott” is a greeting that you hear above all in Austria and southern Germany. It contains an old wish for a blessing. In Switzerland people usually say “Grüezi” instead.
wichtigste: “Grüss Gott” is a word of greeting.
You hear it especially in Austria, Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg.
Originally it means roughly “God greet you” or “God bless you”.
So the greeting is a small wish for a blessing.
The Swiss “Grüezi” has a similar origin.

abschnitte.titel: Where does the greeting come from?
abschnitte.text: “Grüss Gott” is a short form. In earlier times people said something like “Grüss dich Gott”, which means roughly “May God greet you” or “God bless you”. So the greeting is a small **wish for a blessing**. It comes from a time when almost all people in Central Europe were Christian. Today many people use it simply as a friendly hello, without thinking of religion.

You hear the greeting above all in **Austria**, in **Bavaria** and in Baden-Württemberg, and also in South Tyrol. People say it on entering a shop, in the street or when walking in the hills. In northern Germany people are more likely to say “Guten Tag” (“good day”) or “Moin”. Among friends in Austria and Bavaria, “Servus” is also popular.

In German-speaking Switzerland, people usually greet strangers with **“Grüezi”**, and several people with “Grüessech” or “Grüezi mitenand” (“hello, everyone”). “Grüezi” too goes back to an old greeting with God, roughly “Gott grüez i”, that is, “God greet you”. But today you no longer hear God’s name in it. Among friends people say “Hoi” or “Sali”.

gewusst: Anyone who says “Grüss Gott” in Vienna often gets “Grüss Gott” back, regardless of whether someone is religious.

teile.einleitung: **Esotericism** is a collective term for teachings and practices that promise hidden or inner knowledge about human beings and the world. These include, for example, astrology, theosophy or certain healing methods. Scholars study esotericism as a cultural and religious phenomenon.
wichtigste: The Greek word it comes from means “directed inwards”.
In 1875 Helena Blavatsky and Henry Steel Olcott founded the Theosophical Society in New York.
The Goetheanum, the centre of anthroposophy, stands in Dornach.
Monte Verità near Ascona was around 1900 a centre of life reform and alternative spirituality.
The New Age movement refers to the Age of Aquarius.
The healing method Reiki comes from Japan.

abschnitte.text: The word comes from the Greek “esoterikos”, **directed inwards**. It meant knowledge for an inner circle of initiates. The opposite is called “exoteric”, meaning intended for everyone. The scholar of religion **Antoine Faivre** described Western esotericism as a particular **form of thought**. One feature is the idea of **correspondences**: everything in the universe is supposed to be connected with everything else, for example the stars with human beings.

The **Theosophical Society** was founded in New York in 1875 by **Helena Blavatsky** and **Henry Steel Olcott**. It combined Western ideas with teachings from Hinduism and Buddhism. From it came the **anthroposophy** of Rudolf Steiner. Its centre is the **Goetheanum** in **Dornach** in the canton of Solothurn. Around 1900, a settlement for life reform, vegetarian diet and alternative spirituality arose on **Monte Verità** near Ascona.

The **New Age movement** became well known above all in the 1970s and 1980s. It expected a new age of consciousness. It linked this with the astrological transition into the **Age of Aquarius**. Typical is the search for personal spirituality outside the big churches. The researchers **Paul Heelas** and **Linda Woodhead** described this change in 2005 in their study **“The Spiritual Revolution”**.

Many esoteric offerings concern health. One example is **Reiki**, which comes from **Japan**. In it the hands are supposed to transfer energy. A medical effect beyond the placebo effect has not been scientifically proved. Esoteric ideas are also widespread among people with no religious affiliation. According to a survey by the Federal Statistical Office, in 2014 **around 30 per cent** of people in Switzerland with no denomination believed in a higher power.

gewusst: The first Goetheanum was made of wood and burned down on New Year’s Eve 1922; the present building is made of concrete.
Around 1900, artists, dancers and thinkers from all over Europe visited Monte Verità.

teile.einleitung: Challah is a fine, braided bread that belongs to the Sabbath and holidays in Judaism. It looks very similar to the Swiss Sunday plait.
wichtigste: Challah is a braided bread for the Sabbath.
It looks very similar to the Swiss plait.
On the Sabbath, two challot lie on the table.
The two loaves recall the manna in the desert.
Before the blessing, the loaves are covered with a cloth.
At the New Year festival Rosh Hashanah, the challah is often round and is dipped in honey.

abschnitte.text: **Challah** is a soft, light bread made of strands of dough that are **braided** into a plait. It belongs at every **Sabbath meal** on Friday evening. The plural of challah is **challot**. In Switzerland, challah immediately recalls the **Sunday plait**, because the two breads look very alike.

For the Sabbath, **two challot** are put on the table. They recall the **manna**: according to the Bible, God gave the people of Israel manna as food in the desert, and before the Sabbath there was a double amount. The loaves are covered with a beautiful, often embroidered **cloth**. Only at the **blessing** over the bread is the cloth taken away.

abschnitte.titel: Round and sweet for the New Year
abschnitte.text: For the Jewish New Year festival, **Rosh Hashanah**, the challah is often baked **round**. The round shape stands for the year that turns in a circle. Bread and apples are dipped in **honey**. This is a wish for a sweet new year. Sometimes raisins are also added to the dough.

Jewish communities live in Switzerland too, for example in Zurich, Basel and Geneva. In Jewish bakeries you can buy fresh challot before the Sabbath. Many families also bake them themselves. The braiding works in a very similar way to the plait, often with three, four or six strands.

gewusst: Challah is often baked without milk and butter, so that under Jewish dietary rules it may also be eaten with a meal containing meat.
Before baking, challah is often sprinkled with poppy seeds or sesame.

teile.einleitung: The Chinese zodiac assigns one of twelve animals to each year. After twelve years the cycle begins again from the start. There is a well-known legend about a great race that explains the animals.
wichtigste: The Chinese zodiac has twelve animals.
The order begins with the rat, ox, tiger and rabbit.
Then follow the dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog and pig.
The rat is the first animal and the pig is the last.
The dragon is the only mythical creature in the zodiac.
The cat is missing from the zodiac.

abschnitte.text: In the **Chinese zodiac** there are **twelve animals**. Each year belongs to one of these animals. The order is: **rat**, **ox**, **tiger**, **rabbit**, **dragon**, **snake**, **horse**, **goat**, **monkey**, **rooster**, **dog** and **pig**. After the pig the cycle begins again with the rat. Someone born in a year of the horse, for example, has the horse as their animal sign.

A well-known **legend** tells how the order came about. The animals held a race across a river. The clever **rat** sat on the back of the **ox**. Just before the finish line, it jumped off and arrived first. In this way the rat became the first animal and the ox the second.

The **cat** is not in the zodiac. According to one legend, the rat had promised to wake her before the race. But the rat did not wake her, and the cat missed the race. That is why, so the story goes, cats still chase rats and mice today.

Almost all the animals in the zodiac really exist. Only the **dragon** is a **mythical creature**. In China it is seen as a sign of strength and good fortune, unlike in many European fairy tales. The dragon is followed by the **snake**, then the **horse**. The last animal is the **pig**, preceded by the **rooster** and the **dog**.

gewusst: In Vietnam, the cat takes the place of the rabbit in the zodiac.
The year 2026 is a year of the horse.

teile.einleitung: The Golden Temple is the most important sanctuary of the Sikhs. It stands in the city of Amritsar in the north of India. Its proper name is Harmandir Sahib.
wichtigste: The Golden Temple stands in Amritsar in the Indian state of Punjab.
It is the most important sanctuary of the Sikhs.
In Punjabi it is called Harmandir Sahib.
It stands in the middle of a large pool of water.
The upper parts are covered with gold leaf.
The temple has four entrances, as a sign that everyone is welcome.

abschnitte.text: The **Golden Temple** stands in **Amritsar** in the state of **Punjab** in the north of India. For the religion of **Sikhism**, it is the most important sanctuary. Many Sikhs would like to visit it once in their lives. Its proper name is **Harmandir Sahib**, which means roughly “House of God”. Every day very many visitors come, not only Sikhs.

The temple stands in the middle of a large **pool of water**. A narrow **causeway** leads across the water to the temple. The upper parts are covered with **gold leaf**. That is why it gleams in the sun and is reflected in the water. The gilding was added in the 19th century by the ruler **Ranjit Singh**. The temple itself was built around 1600 under **Guru Arjan**.

The temple has **four entrances**, facing all four points of the compass. This shows: **everyone** is welcome, no matter where they come from and what they believe. Inside lies the holy book of the Sikhs, the **Guru Granth Sahib**. It is sung and read from all day long. The music can be heard all around the pool.

In the Golden Temple, all visitors cover their **heads**, for example with a cloth. **Shoes** are taken off beforehand, and you wash your feet. The temple includes a huge communal kitchen, the **langar**. There every guest gets a simple meal free of charge. Many volunteers help with the cooking and washing up, and every day tens of thousands of people are fed.

gewusst: In the langar all guests sit together on the floor, whether rich or poor.
The name of the city of Amritsar goes back to the holy pool and means roughly “pool of nectar”.
